title: 嘉靖二十八年山西鄉試錄
text:
山西鄉試錄序
嘉靖二十有八年天下復當
鄉試之期巡按監察御史黃
〔洪〕〔毗〕飭憲炳文範身而明約
束罔弗祇慎寔維監臨〔廷〕〔俊〕
及教諭朱〔安〕〔道〕謬膺考試官
教授蔡〔節〕〔淵〕錢教諭姜〔周〕〔明〕
===
〔善〕〔嶠〕黃李〔文〕〔蔚〕膺同考試官
試事既成亦既錄矣於戲爾
二三子今日斯其學之成乎
夫士須學也記曰興於詩立
於禮成於樂成斯士也是故
歌鹿鳴而賓興之所以昭其
成而要之始進者也匪直擊
punctuated:
山西鄉試錄序

嘉靖二十有八年，天下復當鄉試之期。巡按監察御史黃〔洪〕〔毗〕，飭憲炳文，範身而明約束，罔弗祇慎，寔維監臨。〔廷〕〔俊〕及教諭朱〔安〕〔道〕，謬膺考試官；教授蔡〔節〕〔淵〕、錢、教諭姜〔周〕〔明〕〔善〕〔嶠〕、黃、李〔文〕〔蔚〕，膺同考試官。

試事既成，亦既錄矣。於戲！爾二三子，今日斯其學之成乎？夫士須學也。記曰：「興於詩，立於禮，成於樂。」成斯士也。是故歌鹿鳴而賓興之，所以昭其成而要之始進者也。匪直擊
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Shanxi Provincial Examination

In the twenty-eighth year of Jiajing [1549], the time for the Provincial Examination had again arrived throughout the realm. The Regional Inspecting Censor, Huang Hongpi [?], upheld the regulations and brought literary culture to prominence. He made his own conduct exemplary and clarified the rules, attending to everything with reverent care; he served as Supervising Official. Tingjun [?] and Instructor Zhu Andao were undeservedly entrusted with the duties of Examiners. Professor Cai Jieyuan [?], Qian [?], Instructor Jiang Zhouming [?], Shanqiao [?], Huang [?], and Li Wenwei [?] were appointed Associate Examiners. [The transcription appears disordered here; the attachment of several names and titles is uncertain.]

The examination has now been completed, and its record compiled. Ah, you gentlemen! Does this day mark the completion of your learning? A scholar must indeed learn. The Record says: “Be stirred by the Odes, established through ritual, and perfected through music.” Thus is the scholar brought to completion. Accordingly, they sing “The Deer Call” and honor the worthy as guests when advancing them: this makes manifest their attainment and places expectations upon them as they first enter public life. It is not merely a matter of striking …

title: 嘉靖二十八年山西鄉試錄
text:
鐘考鼓律倡而呂和為觀聽
之美已也於戲爾二三子其
慎斯往哉夫樂之義大矣志
學相成道器一貫故達其本
者可以觀氣可以審象可以
洞聲可以諳音可以考成是
故吹律聽鐘周武知捷乎牧
野精矣假之物也聽角審音
師曠決競於楚風精矣待諳
===
外也夫人物之靈士人之秀
也樂和之興文樂之章也二
三子言以成文而文不足以
觀志是物之槬焉已耳寙焉
已耳奚其成凡音之起由人
punctuated: 鐘考鼓，律倡而呂和，為觀聽之美已也。於戲！爾二三子，其慎斯往哉！夫樂之義大矣，志學相成，道器一貫。故達其本者，可以觀氣，可以審象，可以洞聲，可以諳音，可以考成。是故吹律聽鐘，周武知捷乎牧野，精矣，假之物也；聽角審音，師曠決競於楚風，精矣，待諳外也。夫人，物之靈；士，人之秀也。樂，和之興；文，樂之章也。二三子言以成文，而文不足以觀志，是物之槬焉已耳，寙焉已耳，奚其成？凡音之起，由人
translation_en: …bells and beating drums, with the yang pitch-pipes leading and the yin pitch-pipes responding, merely to delight the eyes and ears. Ah, you gentlemen, proceed hence with care! The significance of music is great indeed. Aspiration and learning bring each other to fulfillment; the Way and its concrete manifestations form a single continuum. Thus, those who comprehend its foundation can observe vital energies, scrutinize manifestations, penetrate sounds, understand tones, and assess accomplishment. Hence, by blowing pitch-pipes and listening to bells, King Wu of Zhou knew that he would triumph at Muye. This was subtle discernment indeed, yet it drew upon material things. By listening to the jue tone and examining the notes, Shi Kuang determined the outcome of the contest from the airs of Chu. This was subtle discernment indeed, yet it depended upon understanding what lay outside himself [?]. Human beings are the most spiritually perceptive of creatures; scholars are the finest among human beings. Music is the arising of harmony; writing is the outward expression of music. You gentlemen fashion words into writing, but if that writing does not suffice to reveal your aspirations, it is merely something unwieldy and inert [?]. What accomplishment is there in that? Whenever musical tones arise, they originate in human…

title: 嘉靖二十八年山西鄉試錄
text:
心生也舜命夔典樂曰詩言
志歌永言聲依永律和聲八
音克諧無相奪倫神人以和
言非強世也諸士產唐虞之
故墟服禮樂之遺化肆惟我
朝
二祖
===
列聖以至
今上道化浹洽金聲玉振以丕闡
文教又益深且遠涵育釁序
條貫攸明宜其戍文之音惻
隱而慈溫良而寬大善養好
施清越以長方廉而好義也
執此以往將和其心與聲以
punctuated: 心生也。舜命夔典樂，曰：「詩言志，歌永言，聲依永，律和聲。八音克諧，無相奪倫，神人以和。」言非強世也。諸士產唐虞之故墟，服禮樂之遺化。肆惟我朝二祖列聖，以至今上，道化浹洽，金聲玉振，以丕闡文教，又益深且遠。涵育釁序，條貫攸明，宜其戍文之音，惻隱而慈，溫良而寬，大善養好施，清越以長，方廉而好義也。執此以往，將和其心與聲以
translation_en:
…arises from the human heart. When Shun charged Kui with overseeing music, he said: “Poetry expresses intent; song prolongs the words; musical notes follow that prolongation; the pitch standards harmonize the notes. When the eight classes of instruments are brought into harmony, none disrupting the proper order of another, spirits and human beings are thereby brought into concord.” These words do not impose upon the world [?]. You scholars were born in the ancient lands of Tang and Yu, and have received the enduring civilizing influence of their rites and music.
Now, under the Two Founding Ancestors of our dynasty and the succession of sage sovereigns down to His present Majesty, the transforming influence of the Way has spread everywhere. Like the sounding of bronze bells and the concluding resonance of jade chimes, they have magnificently promoted literary culture, making its influence ever deeper and more far-reaching. Through nurture and ordered development [?], its principles and organization have become clear. Thus the tones of your literary compositions [?] should be compassionate and kind, gentle and generous, ample, nourishing, and disposed to giving; clear, resonant, and sustained; upright, incorruptible, and devoted to righteousness. Carrying this forward, you will harmonize your hearts and voices in order to…

title: 嘉靖二十八年山西鄉試錄
text:
宣鴻龐之化而鳴其〔盛〕君臣
民事與物五者各得其音而
無相陵慢焉則足以禔身而
光科目乃或琴瑟乖調塤篪
靡合甚至投竽而舍我所好
膠柱而不知變奏雅以飾曲
之終工弗若矣奚其士嗟夫
===
𧮭聾以知音以知樂知政〔注〕
〔俊〕等固有慚於精妙神解者
矣爾諸士自許謂何以和平
進以涊濦終匪非士殆非夫
矣於戲二三子其慎所以感
之者哉是役也布政司左布
政使韓〔威〕右布政使盧〔紳〕提
punctuated:
宣鴻龐之化而鳴其〔盛〕，君臣民事與物五者各得其音，而無相陵慢焉，則足以禔身而光科目。乃或琴瑟乖調，塤篪靡合，甚至投竽而舍我所好，膠柱而不知變，奏雅以飾曲之終，工弗若矣，奚其士？嗟夫！𧮭聾以知音，以知樂知政，〔注〕〔俊〕等固有慚於精妙神解者矣。爾諸士自許謂何？以和平進，以涊濦終，匪非士，殆非夫矣。於戲！二三子其慎所以感之者哉！
是役也，布政司左布政使韓〔威〕、右布政使盧〔紳〕提
translation_en:
…to proclaim the vast transforming influence and give voice to its flourishing, so that ruler, ministers, people, affairs, and things each attain their proper tone, without encroaching upon or slighting one another. This would suffice to secure your persons and bring distinction to the examination. Yet some may let their zithers fall out of tune and their ocarinas and flutes fail to harmonize. They may even cast aside their reed pipes and abandon what they cherished, or glue their tuning bridges in place and know nothing of adaptation. Though they play elegant music to embellish the conclusion of the piece, they fall short even of musicians—how could they count as scholars? Alas! [The phrase 𧮭聾 is unclear.] In understanding tones, and through them understanding music and government, we, Jun and the others [the annotations 〔注〕〔俊〕 appear doubtful], surely feel ashamed before those whose understanding is subtle and inspired. What do you scholars claim for yourselves? To advance in harmony and peace but end in turmoil [?] is not merely to fail as a scholar; it is almost to fail as a man. Ah! You gentlemen must be cautious about what moves you!
For this examination, Han Wei, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner, and Lu Shen, Right Provincial Administration Commissioner, of the Provincial Administration Commission, undertook the proctoring…

title: 嘉靖二十八年山西鄉試錄
text:
調乎爾按察司按察使陶〔諧〕
副使何〔城〕監試乎爾提學僉
事鄭〔光溥〕前分巡冀北僉事
尹〔綸〕遴選乎爾總督軍務前
兵部尚書翁〔萬達〕今侍郎郭
〔宗皐〕巡撫都御史今陞刑部
右侍郎蘇〔祐〕巡撫大同前都
===
御史今侍郎詹〔榮〕都御史李
〔仁〕巡按直隷監察御史王〔楠〕
巡鹽御史劉〔應熊〕皆風示丕
振乎爾參政潘〔九齡〕劉〔璽〕參
議張〔舜臣〕謝〔淮〕副使楊〔守約〕
魏〔尚綸〕王〔朝賢〕吳〔嶽〕僉事朱
〔徵〕喬〔佑〕戴〔楩〕侯〔鉞〕行太僕寺
punctuated: 調乎爾；按察司按察使陶〔諧〕、副使何〔城〕監試乎爾；提學僉事鄭〔光溥〕、前分巡冀北僉事尹〔綸〕遴選乎爾；總督軍務前兵部尚書翁〔萬達〕、今侍郎郭〔宗皐〕，巡撫都御史今陞刑部右侍郎蘇〔祐〕，巡撫大同前都御史今侍郎詹〔榮〕、都御史李〔仁〕，巡按直隷監察御史王〔楠〕、巡鹽御史劉〔應熊〕，皆風示丕振乎爾；參政潘〔九齡〕、劉〔璽〕，參議張〔舜臣〕、謝〔淮〕，副使楊〔守約〕、魏〔尚綸〕、王〔朝賢〕、吳〔嶽〕，僉事朱〔徵〕、喬〔佑〕、戴〔楩〕、侯〔鉞〕，行太僕寺
translation_en:
…served as Proctors for you. Tao Xie, Surveillance Commissioner of the Provincial Surveillance Commission, and He Cheng, Surveillance Vice Commissioner, supervised your examination. Zheng Guangpu, Education Intendant with the rank of Surveillance Assistant Commissioner, and Yin Lun, formerly Surveillance Assistant Commissioner assigned to the Jibei circuit, selected you.

Those who provided exemplary guidance and greatly inspired you were Weng Wanda, formerly Minister of War, and Guo Zonggao, currently Vice Minister, as Supreme Commanders of Military Affairs; Su You, Grand Coordinator and Censor-in-chief, now promoted to Right Vice Minister of Justice; Zhan Rong, formerly Censor-in-chief and now Vice Minister, and Li Ren, Censor-in-chief, as Grand Coordinators of Datong; Wang Nan, Investigating Censor serving as Regional Inspector of Zhili; and Liu Yingxiong, Salt-inspecting Censor.

Administration Vice Commissioners Pan Jiuling and Liu Xi; Administration Assistant Commissioners Zhang Shunchen and Xie Huai; Surveillance Vice Commissioners Yang Shouyue, Wei Shanglun, Wang Chaoxian, and Wu Yue; Surveillance Assistant Commissioners Zhu Zheng, Qiao You, Dai Pian, and Hou Yue; the Regional Court of the Imperial Stud…

title: 嘉靖二十八年山西鄉試錄
text:
卿楊〔時泰〕又皆贊成乎爾總
理糧儲戶部署郎中李〔材〕主
事崔〔栻〕總兵官沈〔俊〕署都指
揮僉事周〔寳〕吳〔熹〕朱〔玉〕又皆
贍望乎爾於時巡撫都御史
石〔遷高〕巡按御史陳〔九德〕奉
命將代蒇舉成乎爾為
===
朝廷得人慶焉夫省方以觀樂
御史志也亦責也尤所欲告
爾二三子者也爰推著之首
簡以廣笙歌之意尚懋戒之
哉
江西瑞州府上高縣儒學教
諭鄭〔廷俊〕謹序
punctuated:
卿楊〔時泰〕又皆贊成乎爾。總理糧儲戶部署郎中李〔材〕、主事崔〔栻〕、總兵官沈〔俊〕、署都指揮僉事周〔寳〕、吳〔熹〕、朱〔玉〕，又皆贍望乎爾。於時，巡撫都御史石〔遷高〕、巡按御史陳〔九德〕奉命將代，蒇舉成乎爾，為朝廷得人慶焉。夫省方以觀樂，御史志也，亦責也，尤所欲告爾二三子者也。爰推著之首簡，以廣笙歌之意，尚懋戒之哉！
江西瑞州府上高縣儒學教諭鄭〔廷俊〕謹序。
translation_en:
…Yang Shitai, Chief Minister of the Regional Court of the Imperial Stud, likewise joins them in supporting you. Li Cai, Acting Director in the Ministry of Revenue with overall responsibility for grain provisions; Cui Shi, a Principal Secretary; Shen Jun, Regional Commander; and Zhou Bao, Wu Xi, and Zhu Yu, Acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioners, all likewise look to you with expectation [?]. At this time, Shi Qiangao, Grand Coordinator and Censor-in-chief, and Chen Jiude, Regional Inspector, had received orders to take over their posts and bring this undertaking to completion for you. They rejoice that the court has obtained worthy men.
To tour the region and observe its music is the censor’s aspiration and also his responsibility; it is especially what I wish to convey to you gentlemen. I have therefore elaborated on this and set it down at the beginning of this record, to extend the meaning of the mouth-organ music and singing. May you strive diligently and remain vigilant!
Preface respectfully written by Zheng Tingjun, Instructor of the Confucian School of Shanggao County, Ruizhou Prefecture, Jiangxi.

title: 嘉靖二十八年山西鄉試錄
text:
嘉靖二十八年山西鄉試
監臨官
巡按山西監察御史黄洪毗〔恊恭福建莆田縣人　戊戌進士〕

山西等處承宣布政使司左布政使韓威〔德陽直隷河間衛人　壬辰進士〕

===

直隷順德府儒學教授蔡節〔介夫廣東順德縣人　壬午貢士〕

punctuated:
嘉靖二十八年山西鄉試。

監臨官：
巡按山西監察御史黄洪毗〔恊恭，福建莆田縣人，戊戌進士〕。

提調官：
山西等處承宣布政使司左布政使韓威〔德陽，直隷河間衛人，壬辰進士〕。
山西等處承宣布政使司右布政使盧紳〔汝佩，陜西咸寧縣人，癸未進士〕。

監試官：
山西等處提刑按察司按察使陶珪〔廷獻，湖廣黄岡縣人，丙戌進士〕。
山西等處提刑按察司副使何城〔叔防，陜西綏德衛人，壬辰進士〕。

江西瑞州府上高縣儒學教諭鄭廷俊〔章卿，福建莆田縣人，癸卯貢士〕。

同考試官：
直隷順德府儒學教授蔡節〔介夫，廣東順德縣人，壬午貢士〕。
福建建寧府儒學教授錢淵〔子深，直隷建平縣人，辛卯貢士〕。
浙江處州府麗水縣儒學教諭姜周〔廷佐，直隷太倉州人，丁酉貢士〕。
河南開封府鈞州新鄭縣儒學教諭明善〔思誠，湖廣麻城縣人，丙午貢士〕。
直隷鳳陽府壽州蒙城縣儒學教諭黄璠〔子瑒，福建南平縣人，甲午貢士〕。
translation_en:
Shanxi Provincial Examination, the twenty-eighth year of Jiajing (1549).

Supervising Official:
Huang Hongpi, Investigating Censor touring Shanxi. His courtesy name was Xiegong; he was from Putian County, Fujian, and was a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the wuxu year.

Proctors:
Han Wei, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner of Shanxi. His courtesy name was Deyang; he was from Hejian Guard, Zhili, and was a metropolitan graduate of the renchen year.
Lu Shen, Right Provincial Administration Commissioner of Shanxi. His courtesy name was Rupei; he was from Xianning County, Shaanxi, and was a metropolitan graduate of the guiwei year.

Examination Monitoring Officials:
Tao Gui, Provincial Surveillance Commissioner of Shanxi. His courtesy name was Tingxian; he was from Huanggang County, Huguang, and was a metropolitan graduate of the bingxu year.
He Cheng, Vice Commissioner of the Shanxi Provincial Surveillance Commission. His courtesy name was Shufang; he was from Suide Guard, Shaanxi, and was a metropolitan graduate of the renchen year.

Examiners:
Zheng Tingjun, Instructor at the Confucian School of Shanggao County, Ruizhou Prefecture, Jiangxi. His courtesy name was Zhangqing; he was from Putian County, Fujian, and was a tribute scholar (gongshi) of the guimao year.
Zhu Andao, Instructor at the Confucian School of Dongxiang County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi. His courtesy name was Renfu; he was from Shanyin County, Zhejiang, and was a tribute scholar of the guimao year.

Associate Examiners:
Cai Jie, Professor at the Confucian School of Shunde Prefecture, Zhili. His courtesy name was Jiefu; he was from Shunde County, Guangdong, and was a tribute scholar of the renwu year.
Qian Yuan, Professor at the Confucian School of Jianning Prefecture, Fujian. His courtesy name was Zishen; he was from Jianping County, Zhili, and was a tribute scholar of the xinmao year.
Jiang Zhou, Instructor at the Confucian School of Lishui County, Chuzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang. His courtesy name was Tingzuo; he was from Taicang Subprefecture, Zhili, and was a tribute scholar of the dingyou year.
Ming Shan, Instructor at the Confucian School of Xinzheng County, Junzhou Subprefecture, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan. His courtesy name was Sicheng; he was from Macheng County, Huguang, and was a tribute scholar of the bingwu year.
Huang Fan, Instructor at the Confucian School of Mengcheng County, Shouzhou Subprefecture, Fengyang Prefecture, Zhili. His courtesy name was Ziyang; he was from Nanping County, Fujian, and was a tribute scholar of the jiawu year.

title: 嘉靖二十八年山西鄉試錄
text:
直隸揚州府高郵州寶應縣儒學教諭李　蔚〔道州雲南石屏州人　丙午貢士〕
印卷官
山西等處承宣布政使司經歷司經歷吳　棋〔辰州湖廣武昌護衛籍　丙子貢士〕
山西等處提刑按察司經歷司經歷黃　甲〔上卿山東沂水縣人　監生〕
收掌試卷官
太原府知府張　祉〔子受河南固始縣人　戊戌進士〕
平陽府知府張　松〔汝喬河南洛陽縣人　戊戌進士〕
潞安府知府孫　國〔道甫直隸開州人乙未　進士〕
受卷官
===
太原府推官鄭　眞〔惟誠山東青州府寧海衛籍丁　未進士〕
平陽府推官黃希周〔宗魯山東滕縣人甲辰　進士〕
汾州知州李　當〔任父河南嵩縣人戊　子貢士〕
太原府岢嵐州知州李　慧〔汝哲山東平度州人　監生〕
汾州平遙縣知縣馬　快〔汝孈直隸廣平縣人　甲辰進士〕
潞安府潞城縣知縣王惟善〔東甫河南新蔡縣人　丁未進士〕
彌封官
潞安府襄垣縣知縣王尚禮〔叔夫陝西渭南縣人　丁未進士〕
太原府榆次縣知縣朱熙載〔懋勳山東平山衛籍甲　辰進士〕
punctuated:
直隸揚州府高郵州寶應縣儒學教諭李　蔚〔道州，雲南石屏州人，丙午貢士〕。

印卷官：
山西等處承宣布政使司經歷司經歷吳　棋〔辰州，湖廣武昌護衛籍，丙子貢士〕。
山西等處提刑按察司經歷司經歷黃　甲〔上卿，山東沂水縣人，監生〕。

收掌試卷官：
太原府知府張　祉〔子受，河南固始縣人，戊戌進士〕。
平陽府知府張　松〔汝喬，河南洛陽縣人，戊戌進士〕。
潞安府知府孫　國〔道甫，直隸開州人，乙未　進士〕。

受卷官：
太原府推官鄭　眞〔惟誠，山東青州府寧海衛籍，丁　未進士〕。
平陽府推官黃希周〔宗魯，山東滕縣人，甲辰　進士〕。
汾州知州李　當〔任父，河南嵩縣人，戊　子貢士〕。
太原府岢嵐州知州李　慧〔汝哲，山東平度州人，監生〕。
汾州平遙縣知縣馬　快〔汝孈，直隸廣平縣人，甲辰進士〕。
潞安府潞城縣知縣王惟善〔東甫，河南新蔡縣人，丁未進士〕。

彌封官：
潞安府襄垣縣知縣王尚禮〔叔夫，陝西渭南縣人，丁未進士〕。
太原府榆次縣知縣朱熙載〔懋勳，山東平山衛籍，甲　辰進士〕。
translation_en:
Li Wei, Instructor of the Confucian School of Baoying County, Gaoyou Subprefecture, Yangzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. His courtesy name was Daozhou; he was from Shiping Subprefecture, Yunnan, and was a tribute scholar (gongshi) of the bingwu year.

Officials for Printing Examination Papers

Wu Qi, Registrar in the Registry of the Shanxi Provincial Administration Commission. His courtesy name was Chenzhou; he was registered with the Wuchang Princely Escort Guard in Huguang and was a tribute scholar (gongshi) of the bingzi year.

Huang Jia, Registrar in the Registry of the Shanxi Provincial Surveillance Commission. His courtesy name was Shangqing; he was from Yishui County, Shandong, and was a National University student.

Officials for Custody of Examination Scripts

Zhang Zhi, Prefect of Taiyuan. His courtesy name was Zishou; he was from Gushi County, Henan, and was a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the wuxu year.

Zhang Song, Prefect of Pingyang. His courtesy name was Ruqiao; he was from Luoyang County, Henan, and was a metropolitan graduate of the wuxu year.

Sun Guo, Prefect of Lu’an. His courtesy name was Daofu; he was from Kai Subprefecture in the directly administered metropolitan region and was a metropolitan graduate of the yiwei year.

Officials for Receiving Examination Scripts

Zheng Zhen, Prefectural Judge of Taiyuan. His courtesy name was Weicheng; he was registered with the Ninghai Guard in Qingzhou Prefecture, Shandong, and was a metropolitan graduate of the dingwei year.

Huang Xizhou, Prefectural Judge of Pingyang. His courtesy name was Zonglu; he was from Teng County, Shandong, and was a metropolitan graduate of the jiachen year.

Li Dang, Subprefect of Fen Subprefecture. His courtesy name was Renfu; he was from Song County, Henan, and was a tribute scholar (gongshi) of the wuzi year.

Li Hui, Subprefect of Kelan Subprefecture, Taiyuan Prefecture. His courtesy name was Ruzhe; he was from Pingdu Subprefecture, Shandong, and was a National University student.

Ma Kuai, Magistrate of Pingyao County, Fen Subprefecture. His courtesy name was Ruhui; he was from Guangping County in the directly administered metropolitan region and was a metropolitan graduate of the jiachen year.

Wang Weishan, Magistrate of Lucheng County, Lu’an Prefecture. His courtesy name was Dongfu; he was from Xincai County, Henan, and was a metropolitan graduate of the dingwei year.

Officials for Sealing Candidates’ Names

Wang Shangli, Magistrate of Xiangyuan County, Lu’an Prefecture. His courtesy name was Shufu; he was from Weinan County, Shaanxi, and was a metropolitan graduate of the dingwei year.

Zhu Xizai, Magistrate of Yuci County, Taiyuan Prefecture. His courtesy name was Maoxun; he was registered with the Pingshan Guard in Shandong and was a metropolitan graduate of the jiachen year.

title: 嘉靖二十八年山西鄉試錄

沁州知州劉孝學〔典于山東壽光縣人　辛卯貢士〕

平陽府解州夏縣知縣岳粹〔純甫，山東冠縣人，丁未進士〕。潞安府壺關縣知縣殷錦〔美中，山東恩縣人，丁未進士〕。潞安府長治縣知縣張𡕒〔以貞，陝西安定縣人，丁未進士〕。平陽府解州聞喜縣知縣鄭東藩〔鎮夫，山東金鄉縣人，丁未進士〕。

謄錄官
太原府陽曲縣知縣陳瓚〔敬夫，直隷獻縣人，丁未進士〕。平陽府曲沃縣知縣劉曾〔希孔，山東恩縣人，丁未進士〕。平陽府趙城縣知縣宋時〔宗易，河南鈞州人，甲午貢士〕。太原府太谷縣知縣白世璧〔德如，陝西秦州衛人，甲午貢士〕。平陽府解州安邑縣知縣吳大道〔行父，直隷任丘縣人，丁酉貢士〕。平陽府絳州稷山縣知縣楊文卿〔子質，直隷蠡山縣人，辛卯貢士〕。

對讀官
太原府代州知州李良能〔子純，河南郟縣人，甲午貢士〕。沁州知州劉孝學〔典于，山東壽光縣人，辛卯貢士〕。平陽府蒲州臨晉縣知縣李爻〔子仁，濟陽衛籍，丁未進士〕。平陽府蒲州滎河縣知縣楊灝〔紹源，河南汝陽縣人，丁酉貢士〕。太原府代州崞縣知縣吳府〔季脩，山東青州衛人，丁酉貢士〕。潞安府襄垣縣縣丞李郁〔文甫，四川安居縣人，丁未進士〕。
translation_en:
Yue Cui, Magistrate of Xia County in Jie Subprefecture, Pingyang Prefecture, had the courtesy name Chunfu and was from Guan County, Shandong. He was a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the dingwei year.

Yin Jin, Magistrate of Huguan County, Lu’an Prefecture, had the courtesy name Meizhong and was from En County, Shandong. He was a metropolitan graduate of the dingwei year.

Zhang 𡕒 [given name reading uncertain: ?], Magistrate of Changzhi County, Lu’an Prefecture, had the courtesy name Yizhen and was from Anding County, Shaanxi. He was a metropolitan graduate of the dingwei year.

Zheng Dongfan, Magistrate of Wenxi County in Jie Subprefecture, Pingyang Prefecture, had the courtesy name Zhenfu and was from Jinxiang County, Shandong. He was a metropolitan graduate of the dingwei year.

Chen Zan, Magistrate of Yangqu County, Taiyuan Prefecture, had the courtesy name Jingfu and was from Xian County, Zhili. He was a metropolitan graduate of the dingwei year.

Liu Zeng, Magistrate of Quwo County, Pingyang Prefecture, had the courtesy name Xikong and was from En County, Shandong. He was a metropolitan graduate of the dingwei year.

Song Shi, Magistrate of Zhaocheng County, Pingyang Prefecture, had the courtesy name Zongyi and was from Jun Subprefecture, Henan. He was a tribute scholar (gongshi) of the jiawu year.

Bai Shibi, Magistrate of Taigu County, Taiyuan Prefecture, had the courtesy name Deru and was from Qinzhou Guard, Shaanxi. He was a tribute scholar of the jiawu year.

Wu Dadao, Magistrate of Anyi County in Jie Subprefecture, Pingyang Prefecture, had the courtesy name Xingfu and was from Renqiu County, Zhili. He was a tribute scholar of the dingyou year.

Yang Wenqing, Magistrate of Jishan County in Jiang Subprefecture, Pingyang Prefecture, had the courtesy name Zizhi and was from Lishan County [?], Zhili. He was a tribute scholar of the xinmao year.

Liu Xiaoxue, Subprefect of Qin Subprefecture, had the courtesy name Dianyu and was from Shouguang County, Shandong. He was a tribute scholar of the xinmao year.

Li Yao, Magistrate of Linjin County in Pu Subprefecture, Pingyang Prefecture, had the courtesy name Ziren and was registered with Jiyang Guard. He was a metropolitan graduate of the dingwei year.

Yang Hao, Magistrate of Ronghe County in Pu Subprefecture, Pingyang Prefecture, had the courtesy name Shaoyuan and was from Ruyang County, Henan. He was a tribute scholar of the dingyou year.

Li Yu, Vice Magistrate of Xiangyuan County, Lu’an Prefecture, had the courtesy name Wenfu and was from Anju County, Sichuan. He was a metropolitan graduate of the dingwei year.

title: 嘉靖二十八年山西鄉試錄
text:

太原右衛指揮僉事林爵〔守忠福建□□□縣人〕

===

punctuated:
巡綽官
太原右衛指揮僉事曰清〔□夫，□南□□縣人〕。太原右衛指揮僉事林爵〔守忠，福建□□□縣人〕。平陽衛指揮同知謝恩〔君賜，四川建昌府人〕。太原左衛中右所正千戶郝銘〔新之，直隸鳳陽府人〕。太原前衛左所正千戶楊鈺〔朝重，湖廣澧州人〕。

搜檢官
太原右衛指揮使鄭憲〔子榮，儀州人〕。太原右衛指揮僉事王璋〔君重，直隸臨淮縣人〕。振武衛指揮僉事許韶〔孝□，湖廣□陽州人〕。潞州衛指揮僉事盧蕙恭〔克讓，直隸臨淮縣人〕。太原左衛後所武舉署正千戶譚纓〔世簪，江西都昌縣人〕。

供給官
山西等處承宣布政使司照磨所檢校崔伸〔引之，山東汶上縣人，監生〕。太原府同知張文行〔宗敎，直隸□陽縣人，乙酉貢士〕。太原府通判劉東藩〔道輔，直隸景州人，甲午貢士〕。太原府徐溝縣知縣邵鶴〔九皐，直隸盧龍縣人，戊子貢士〕。平陽府臨汾縣知縣邢玳〔朝重，陝西狄道縣人，丁酉貢士〕。

punctuated: 潞安府屯留縣知縣陳松〔伯喬，直隸定州衛官籍，戊子貢士〕。太原府照磨王卓〔立夫，陝西鎮番衛官籍，監生〕。平陽府絳州同知方升〔文中，四川遂寧縣人，吏員〕。汾州判官高寧〔希顏，順天府寶坻縣人，監生〕。太原府嵢嵐州判官彭橋〔利夫，陝西寶雞縣人，監生〕。太原前衛經歷李茂〔文獻，山東長山縣人，吏員〕。振武衛經歷楊遵〔惟善，河南光州人，吏員〕。平陽府霍州吏目張鑑〔克明，山東陽穀縣人，吏員〕。太原府文水縣縣丞張雲從〔子龍，陝西秦州人，監生〕。太原府壽陽縣主簿田仁〔元善，順天府密雲縣人，監生〕。平陽府霍州靈石縣主簿王應招〔際明，直隸灤州人，監生〕。太原府陽曲縣典史南紀〔大綱，陝西寧州人，吏員〕。太原府徐溝縣典史張輝〔晦之，山東平原縣人，吏員〕。太原府清源縣典史谷寬〔德洪，直隸隆慶州人，吏員〕。太原府忻州定襄縣典史韓銳〔退夫，山東壽光縣人，吏員〕。太原府陽曲縣臨汾驛驛丞賀文卿〔朝縉，湖廣澧州人，承差〕。平陽府聞喜縣涑川驛驛丞吳克裕〔汝仁，陝西華陰縣人，承差〕。平陽府曲沃縣侯馬驛驛丞盛華〔子實，廣西臨桂縣人，承差〕。

title: 嘉靖二十八年山西鄉試錄
text:
第壹塲
四書
能行五者於天下爲仁矣請問之曰恭寛
信敏惠
自誠明謂之性自明誠謂之敎誠則明矣
明則誠矣
江漢以濯之秋陽以暴之皜皜乎不可尚
已
易
===
介于石不終日貞吉
恒亨无咎利貞利有攸往
生生之謂易
是故變化云爲吉事有祥象事知器占事
知來
書
予欲觀古人之象日月星辰山龍華蟲作
會宗彝藻火粉米黼黻絺繡以五采彰
施于五色作服汝明
punctuated:
第壹塲

四書

「能行五者於天下，爲仁矣。」「請問之。」曰：「恭、寛、信、敏、惠。」

自誠明，謂之性；自明誠，謂之敎。誠則明矣，明則誠矣。

江漢以濯之，秋陽以暴之，皜皜乎不可尚已。

易

介于石，不終日，貞吉。

恒，亨，无咎，利貞，利有攸往。

生生之謂易。

是故變化云爲，吉事有祥。象事知器，占事知來。

書

予欲觀古人之象：日、月、星辰、山、龍、華蟲，作會；宗彝、藻、火、粉米、黼、黻，絺繡。以五采彰施于五色，作服，汝明。
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

“To be able to practice five things throughout the world constitutes humaneness.” “May I ask what they are?” The Master said: “Respectfulness, generosity, trustworthiness, diligence, and kindness.”

To attain understanding through sincerity is called nature; to attain sincerity through understanding is called instruction. With sincerity comes understanding; with understanding comes sincerity.

Washed in the Jiang and Han rivers and dried in the autumn sun, his purity shines so brilliantly that none can surpass it.

Book of Changes (Yijing)

Firm as a rock, not waiting until the day is over. Perseverance brings good fortune.

Constancy: success, without blame. It is beneficial to persevere; it is beneficial to have somewhere to go.

Life continually generating life is what is meant by change.

Thus, amid transformations and changes, speech and action, auspicious affairs have favorable portents. By forming images of affairs, one understands the implements suited to them; by divining about affairs, one knows what is to come.

Book of Documents (Shujing)

I wish to see the emblematic designs of the ancients: the sun, moon, stars, mountains, dragons, and pheasants rendered in painting; ancestral sacrificial vessels, water plants, fire, grains of rice, axe patterns, and paired bow-shaped patterns rendered in fine embroidery. Use the five colors to display these designs distinctly upon the fabrics of five colors, making ceremonial robes. You are to make these distinctions clear.

title: 嘉靖二十八年山西鄉試錄
text:
惟皇上帝降衷于下民若有恒性克綏厥
猷惟后
五者來備各以其敘庶草蕃廡
惟德惟義時乃大訓
詩
知子之來之雜佩以贈之知子之順之雜
佩以問之知子之好之雜佩以報之
大田多稼既種既戒既備乃事以我覃耜
俶載南畝播厥百穀既庭且碩曾孫是
===
若
天子是若明命使賦
載見辟王曰求厥章龍旂陽陽和鈴央央
鞗革有鶬休有烈光
春秋
秋七月庚午宋公齊侯衛侯盟于瓦屋〔隱〕
〔公八年〕
會宋公陳侯蔡人衛人伐鄭〔隱公四年〕郲
人鄭人伐宋〔隱公五年〕夏公會齊侯宋
punctuated:
惟皇上帝，降衷于下民，若有恒性，克綏厥猷，惟后。
五者來備，各以其敘，庶草蕃廡。
惟德惟義，時乃大訓。

詩
知子之來之，雜佩以贈之；知子之順之，雜佩以問之；知子之好之，雜佩以報之。
大田多稼，既種既戒，既備乃事。以我覃耜，俶載南畝，播厥百穀，既庭且碩，曾孫是若。
天子是若，明命使賦。
載見辟王，曰求厥章。龍旂陽陽，和鈴央央，鞗革有鶬，休有烈光。

春秋
秋七月庚午，宋公、齊侯、衛侯盟于瓦屋。〔隱〕〔公八年〕
會宋公、陳侯、蔡人、衛人伐鄭。〔隱公四年〕郲人、鄭人伐宋。〔隱公五年〕夏，公會齊侯、宋
translation_en:
August Heaven, the Supreme Lord, bestowed an inner moral mean upon the people below. To guide them in accordance with their constant nature and bring peace to their ways is the ruler’s task.
When all five come in full measure, each in its proper sequence, the various plants flourish abundantly.
Virtue and righteousness: these are the great instructions.

The Book of Odes
Knowing that you have come, I give you assorted girdle pendants; knowing your kindness, I offer assorted girdle pendants in greeting; knowing your affection, I repay it with assorted girdle pendants.
The great fields bear abundant crops. Having prepared the seed and put the implements in order, and having made everything ready for the work, we take our sharp plowshares and begin work on the south-facing fields. We sow the hundred grains; they grow upright and large. The royal descendant approves of them.
The Son of Heaven approves of him and expressly commands him to promulgate his orders.
They come to appear before their sovereign king, seeking his rules and ordinances. Dragon banners flutter brightly; chariot bells ring harmoniously. Bridle straps have gleaming metal ornaments, splendid with brilliant radiance.

The Spring and Autumn Annals
In autumn, in the seventh month, on the gengwu day, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Qi, and the Marquis of Wei made a covenant at Wawu. 〔Duke Yin,〕〔eighth year〕
[The Duke] joined the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, and men of Cai and Wei in attacking Zheng. 〔Duke Yin, fourth year〕 Men of Lai [?] and Zheng attacked Song. 〔Duke Yin, fifth year〕 In summer, the Duke met with the Marquis of Qi and the Duke of Song …

title: 嘉靖二十八年山西鄉試錄
text:
公陳侯衛侯曹伯伐鄭圍新城〔僖公六〕
〔年〕春齊侯伐宋圍緡〔僖公二十三年〕
甲午晦晉侯及楚子鄭伯戰于鄢陵楚子
鄭師敗績〔成公十有六年〕夏楚子鄭伯
伐宋宋魚石復入于彭城〔成公十有八〕
〔年〕仲孫蔑會晉欒黶宋華元衛甯殖曹
人莒人邾人滕人薛人圍宋彭城　夏
晉韓厥帥師伐鄭仲孫蔑會齊崔杼曹
人邾人杞人次于鄫　秋楚公子壬夫
帥師侵宋〔俱襄公元年〕
叔孫州仇帥師墮郈　季孫斯仲孫何忌
帥師墮費　十有二月公圍成公至自
圍成〔俱定公十有二年〕
===
禮記
天子賜諸侯樂則以柷將之賜伯子男樂
則以鼗將之
五行之動迭相竭也五行四時十二月還
相爲本也五聲六律十二管還相爲宮
punctuated:
公、陳侯、衛侯、曹伯伐鄭，圍新城。〔僖公六〕〔年〕春，齊侯伐宋，圍緡。〔僖公二十三年〕甲午，晦，晉侯及楚子、鄭伯戰于鄢陵，楚子、鄭師敗績。〔成公十有六年〕夏，楚子、鄭伯伐宋，宋魚石復入于彭城。〔成公十有八〕〔年〕仲孫蔑會晉欒黶、宋華元、衛甯殖、曹人、莒人、邾人、滕人、薛人圍宋彭城。夏，晉韓厥帥師伐鄭，仲孫蔑會齊崔杼、曹人、邾人、杞人次于鄫。秋，楚公子壬夫帥師侵宋。〔俱襄公元年〕
叔孫州仇帥師墮郈。季孫斯、仲孫何忌帥師墮費。十有二月，公圍成。公至自圍成。〔俱定公十有二年〕
禮記
天子賜諸侯樂，則以柷將之；賜伯子男樂，則以鼗將之。
五行之動，迭相竭也。五行、四時、十二月，還相爲本也。五聲、六律、十二管，還相爲宮
translation_en:
…the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, and the Earl of Cao attacked Zheng and besieged Xincheng. 〔Sixth year of Duke Xi〕 In spring, the Marquis of Qi attacked Song and besieged Min. 〔Twenty-third year of Duke Xi〕 On the jiawu day, the last day of the month, the Marquis of Jin fought against the Viscount of Chu and the Earl of Zheng at Yanling. The Viscount of Chu and the army of Zheng suffered a crushing defeat. 〔Sixteenth year of Duke Cheng〕 In summer, the Viscount of Chu and the Earl of Zheng attacked Song. Yu Shi of Song reentered Pengcheng. 〔Eighteenth year of Duke Cheng〕 Zhongsun Mie joined Luan Yan of Jin, Hua Yuan of Song, Ning Zhi of Wei, and men of Cao, Ju, Zhu, Teng, and Xue in besieging Pengcheng in Song. In summer, Han Jue of Jin led an army to attack Zheng. Zhongsun Mie joined Cui Zhu of Qi and men of Cao, Zhu, and Qi (杞) in encamping at Zeng. In autumn, Prince Renfu of Chu led an army to invade Song. 〔All in the first year of Duke Xiang〕
Shusun Zhouchou led an army to demolish the fortifications of Hou. Jisun Si and Zhongsun Heji led an army to demolish the fortifications of Fei. In the twelfth month, the duke besieged Cheng. The duke returned from besieging Cheng. 〔All in the twelfth year of Duke Ding〕
Book of Rites (Liji)
When the Son of Heaven grants musical instruments to the feudal lords, a zhu, a wooden percussion instrument, leads the presentation; when he grants musical instruments to earls, viscounts, and barons, a tao, a pellet drum, leads the presentation.
In their movement, the Five Phases exhaust one another in turn. The Five Phases, the four seasons, and the twelve months cyclically serve as the basis for one another. The five notes, the six pitch standards, and the twelve pitch pipes cyclically serve as the tonic…

title: 嘉靖二十八年山西鄉試錄
text:
也五味六和十二食還相爲質也五色

廉直勁正莊誠之音作而民肅敬
仁者天下之表也義者天下之制也報者
天下之利也

學者必識聖賢之體

===

擬唐加左僕射房玄齡太子少師誥〔貞觀十三年〕
擬宋宴貢士於迎春苑謝表〔太平興國三年〕
判語〔五條〕

也。五味、六和、十二食，還相爲質也。五色、六章、十二衣，還相爲質也。

論

translation_en:
… The five flavors, six harmonizing ingredients, and twelve foods take turns serving as the basic substance. The five colors, six decorative patterns, and twelve garments take turns serving as the basic substance.
When music expressing integrity, uprightness, strength, rectitude, solemnity, and sincerity arises, the people become solemn and respectful.
Benevolence is the model for all under Heaven; righteousness is the rule for all under Heaven; reciprocity is the benefit of all under Heaven.
Second Session
Discourse
Students must recognize the essential character of sages and worthies.
Edicts, proclamations, and memorials 〔One question to be assigned from among these [?].〕
Compose an edict in the voice of the Han emperor on passing through Zeng [?] and sacrificing to Confucius with a full offering of an ox, a sheep, and a pig. 〔Twelfth year of Emperor Gao.〕
Compose a Tang proclamation conferring the additional title of Junior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent on Fang Xuanling, Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs. 〔Thirteenth year of Zhenguan.〕
Compose a Song memorial of thanks for a banquet given to tribute scholars at Yingchun Garden. 〔Third year of Taiping Xingguo.〕
Legal Judgments 〔Five items.〕
Reviewing case files.
Uncultivated farmland.
Prohibiting ceremonial receptions and send-offs.

title: 嘉靖二十八年山西鄉試錄
text:
聽訟廻避
帶造段疋
第叁場
策五道
問易曰觀乎天文以察時變觀乎人文以
化成天下孔子稱堯曰煥乎其文章文
固君人者不廢也古之哲后明王每注
思焉如畫八卦演九疇解愠之詩盤銘
之詞几杖之戒儀鳳之作昭回于天矣
===
先儒乃謂帝王之學不在文藝何歟若
大風以猛士興歌秋風以佳人發詠登
臺以除兇自寓繪圖以無逸省躬賛孔
顔何見於道眞吟籍田何裨於勸課箴
元良何矯於登封記損齋何至於忍恥
果經綸之迹言行之符乎外至伴侶新
聲斷烟平蕪則藝焉而已人文化成之
意不如是也洪惟我
太祖高皇帝端崇理本明燭化機天才峻發藻
punctuated:
聽訟廻避。
帶造段疋。

第叁場
策五道

問：《易》曰：「觀乎天文，以察時變；觀乎人文，以化成天下。」孔子稱堯曰：「煥乎其文章！」文固君人者不廢也。古之哲后明王，每注思焉。如畫八卦、演九疇、解愠之詩、盤銘之詞、几杖之戒、儀鳳之作，昭回于天矣。先儒乃謂帝王之學不在文藝，何歟？若大風以猛士興歌，秋風以佳人發詠，登臺以除兇自寓，繪圖以無逸省躬，賛孔顔何見於道眞？吟籍田何裨於勸課？箴元良何矯於登封？記損齋何至於忍恥？果經綸之迹、言行之符乎？外至伴侶、新聲、斷烟、平蕪，則藝焉而已，人文化成之意不如是也。洪惟我太祖高皇帝，端崇理本，明燭化機，天才峻發，藻
translation_en:
Recusal in hearing lawsuits.
The concurrent manufacture of bolts of silk [?].

Third Session
Five Policy Questions

Question: The Book of Changes says: “Observe the patterns of Heaven to discern changes in the seasons; observe human culture to transform and perfect all under Heaven.” Confucius praised Yao, saying: “How brilliant was his cultural achievement!” Culture is certainly something that rulers cannot dispense with. The wise sovereigns and enlightened kings of antiquity continually devoted thought to it. Such achievements as drawing the Eight Trigrams, elaborating the Nine Categories, the poem on relieving resentment, the inscription on the basin, the admonitions on the armrest and staff, and the music that brought phoenixes to dance shone and revolved in Heaven. Yet earlier Confucian scholars said that the learning of emperors and kings did not lie in literary arts. Why?

Consider the song of the Great Wind, inspired by mighty warriors; the poem of the Autumn Wind, prompted by a beautiful woman; the ascent of a terrace, expressing the ambition to eliminate the wicked; and the commissioning of a picture on taking no ease, as a means of self-examination. What insight into the truth of the Way appears in the eulogy of Confucius and Yan Hui? What contribution to encouraging agriculture is made by the poem on the imperial ploughing field? What correction of the ascent of Mount Tai for the feng sacrifice is offered by the admonition to the heir apparent [?]? How could the author of the Record of the Studio of Diminishment come to endure humiliation? Are these truly traces of ordering the realm, and evidence that words accorded with deeds? As for such things as companions arriving from outside [?], new melodies, wisps of mist, and level grasslands, these are merely artistic pursuits. This is not what is meant by transforming and perfecting the world through human culture.

We reverently reflect that our Emperor Taizu Gao firmly exalted principle as the foundation and clearly perceived the workings of transformation. His Heaven-given talent rose magnificently, and his literary…

title: 嘉靖二十八年山西鄉試錄
text:
思富逸故其揮灑成文率皆天地之嚮
采當時侍從之臣有稱其雄深宏偉言
近而指遠者有稱其天光昭回赫著簡
素眞所謂天之文者有稱其親染奎翰
意無停機一揮而數千百言羣臣環視
莫不讋服者其所製之文亦可得指其
一二歟抑可因詞而究其歸歟逮我
皇上默契
聖學統一道眞書之三要有釋傳之五箴有註
===
敬一一一箴獨遡心學之源又等羲畫堯文而上
之矣諸士子久沾棫樸之化今復以文
進願鋪張鴻休而鳴其盛焉
問古者因事設官量能授職自伏犧氏以
來未之有易也然名官之制或以龍以
水以火以雲以鳥以民何據而然與或
名以五行或分爲九官或爲三公三孤
六官或爲三公九卿或爲三省九寺或
爲二府臺諫何繁簡之不齊與其諸所
punctuated:
思富逸，故其揮灑成文，率皆天地之嚮采。當時侍從之臣，有稱其雄深宏偉、言近而指遠者，有稱其天光昭回、赫著簡素、眞所謂天之文者，有稱其親染奎翰、意無停機、一揮而數千百言、羣臣環視、莫不讋服者。其所製之文，亦可得指其一二歟？抑可因詞而究其歸歟？逮我皇上默契聖學，統一道眞，書之三要有釋，傳之五箴有註，敬一一一箴獨遡心學之源，又等羲畫堯文而上之矣。諸士子久沾棫樸之化，今復以文進，願鋪張鴻休而鳴其盛焉。

問：古者因事設官，量能授職，自伏犧氏以來，未之有易也。然名官之制，或以龍、以水、以火、以雲、以鳥、以民，何據而然與？或名以五行，或分爲九官，或爲三公三孤六官，或爲三公九卿，或爲三省九寺，或爲二府臺諫，何繁簡之不齊與？其諸所
translation_en:
…his literary imagination was abundant and untrammeled; thus, whenever he wielded his brush to compose, his writings were generally the echoes and radiance of Heaven and Earth. Among the ministers attending him at the time, some praised their force, depth, breadth, and grandeur, saying that their language was accessible but their import far-reaching. Some praised their heavenly light, shining all around and brilliantly manifest upon bamboo slips and silk—truly what might be called the writings of Heaven. Others praised how he personally took up the imperial brush, his thoughts flowing without pause, producing hundreds or thousands of words in a single sweep, while the assembled ministers watched, all awestruck and submissive. Can you identify one or two of the writings he composed? Or can you examine their ultimate purport through their wording?

Coming down to our present emperor, His Majesty has silently comprehended the learning of the sages and unified the truth of the Way. He has provided explanations of the Three Essentials of the Book of Documents and annotations on the Five Admonitions of the commentaries. His Admonition on Holding Fast to Unity in Reverence [the title is garbled in the transcription: 敬一一一箴] uniquely traces the learning of the mind back to its source, placing it on a level with, and indeed above, Fuxi’s diagrams and Yao’s writings. You candidates have long benefited from the transforming influence celebrated in “The Oak Clusters” (Yupu), and now once again seek advancement through literary composition. We hope that you will expound at length upon these magnificent blessings and give voice to their splendor.

Question: In antiquity, offices were established according to the tasks to be done, and appointments were conferred according to ability. Since the time of Fuxi, this has never changed. Yet in the system of naming offices, some used dragons, water, fire, clouds, birds, or the people. On what grounds did they do so? Some named offices after the Five Phases; some divided them into nine offices; some instituted the Three Dukes, Three Junior Dukes, and Six Ministries; some the Three Dukes and Nine Chamberlains; some the Three Departments and Nine Courts; and some the Two Administrations, the Censorate, and remonstrance officials. Why did these arrangements differ so much in complexity and simplicity? As for their respective …

title: 嘉靖二十八年山西鄉試錄
text:
職守可得聞與或又謂陶唐氏以前之
官所治者天事也虞夏以后之官所治
者民事也不知治天事者何以遺民治
民事者何又遺天然與否與我
朝稽古定制其建官皆法乎周官而損益之
具載於諸司職掌者可攷也或謂中間
多所更定或謂多所變易或謂悉復其
舊或謂隨時損益可得聞與不知所職
掌者果皆同於古昔抑其事有輕重之
===
不同與諸士子涵濡
聖化與聞久矣行將服有職掌願詳言之以彰
國家典章之盛
問學猶殖也惰而落焉勤而精焉日出日
中秉燭之喻以時而異趨浸潤冰釋理
順之幾以悟而俱化信斯言也進於聖
人不難矣懷鉛夜寢同於引壁之光抗
疏定禮勳有淺深乎採薪挾經同於春
秋之好不教自課意有異同乎多聞好
punctuated:
職守，可得聞與？或又謂陶唐氏以前之官，所治者天事也；虞夏以后之官，所治者民事也。不知治天事者何以遺民，治民事者何又遺天？然與否與？我朝稽古定制，其建官皆法乎周官而損益之，具載於諸司職掌者可攷也。或謂中間多所更定，或謂多所變易，或謂悉復其舊，或謂隨時損益，可得聞與？不知所職掌者果皆同於古昔，抑其事有輕重之不同與？諸士子涵濡聖化，與聞久矣，行將服有職掌，願詳言之，以彰國家典章之盛。

問：學猶殖也，惰而落焉，勤而精焉。日出、日中、秉燭之喻，以時而異趨；浸潤、冰釋、理順之幾，以悟而俱化。信斯言也，進於聖人不難矣。懷鉛夜寢，同於引壁之光，抗疏定禮，勳有淺深乎？採薪挾經，同於春秋之好，不教自課，意有異同乎？多聞好
translation_en:
…may we hear what duties they held? Some also say that officials before the time of Taotang administered the affairs of Heaven, whereas officials from Yu and Xia onward administered human affairs. Yet why should those administering Heaven’s affairs have neglected the people, and why should those administering human affairs have neglected Heaven? Is this claim true or not? Our dynasty consulted antiquity in establishing its institutions. In creating offices, it took the Offices of Zhou as its model, making additions and reductions; these can be examined in the detailed provisions of the Duties of the Various Offices. Some say that many provisions were subsequently revised; others that many were altered; others that all the old arrangements were restored; and still others that additions and reductions were made as circumstances required. May we hear an account of these matters? Were the responsibilities assigned truly all the same as in antiquity, or did the business entrusted to them differ in importance? You candidates have long been nurtured by the sage influence of the throne and have heard of these matters. Soon you will hold office and assume responsibilities. Explain them fully, so as to make manifest the magnificence of the state’s institutions and statutes.

Question: Learning resembles cultivation: with indolence it declines; with diligence it becomes refined. The analogies of sunrise, midday, and holding a candle indicate different ways of proceeding according to one’s stage of life. Gradual permeation, the melting of ice, and the attainment of coherence in principle are critical moments of transformation through understanding. If these words are true, advancing to sagehood is not difficult. Sleeping at night with a lead writing implement at hand resembles drawing light through a wall [?]; in submitting forthright memorials and settling ritual, did their achievements differ in degree? Gathering firewood while carrying a classic resembles a fondness for the Spring and Autumn Annals; in studying independently without instruction, did their intentions differ or coincide? Hearing much and being prone to…

title: 嘉靖二十八年山西鄉試錄
text:
忘固當取裁於理盡卷不錯江淮所以
立忠也氣味蹊徑固在濳㴱於功專精
不嘗君厚所以通儒也癖左氏則平吳
矣帶耕鉏則立相矣奚不求甚解者所
造反優耶重五十而不窮矣重八九而
稱勝矣奚不知祁招者所實反在耶陜
峻逡巡改其迤邐之步入路住宅誰同
百世之方諸生求端於下帷有司懸衡
於品藻焉
===
問以人事君臣之上也不比不黨昔人稱
之荆伯柳上黨矣子羔西河矣引弓迎
射子其去矣無愧於解狐之舉哉然公
由於己私卽澌也哲懸於秉鑑多昏也
觀前載則又易易然者子師千里二童
二賢不諳仲弓不宿奉高卒不越其裁
量故僑札之分自有神乎管鮑之知若
同天啓因小而揣巨任分麋鹿耿主麋
給其陳孺子之宰乎定交而因親剌則
punctuated:
忘，固當取裁於理；盡卷不錯，江淮所以立忠也。氣味蹊徑，固在濳㴱於功；專精不嘗，君厚所以通儒也。癖左氏則平吳矣，帶耕鉏則立相矣，奚不求甚解者所造反優耶？重五十而不窮矣，重八九而稱勝矣，奚不知祁招者所實反在耶？陜峻逡巡，改其迤邐之步；入路住宅，誰同百世之方？諸生求端於下帷，有司懸衡於品藻焉。

問：以人事君，臣之上也。不比不黨，昔人稱之。荆伯柳上黨矣，子羔西河矣，引弓迎射，子其去矣，無愧於解狐之舉哉？然公由於己，私卽澌也；哲懸於秉，鑑多昏也。觀前載，則又易易然者。子師千里，二童二賢，不諳仲弓，不宿奉高，卒不越其裁量。故僑札之分，自有神乎？管鮑之知，若同天啓。因小而揣巨，任分麋鹿，耿主麋，給其陳孺子之宰乎？定交而因親，剌則
translation_en:
…forgetful, one must certainly judge according to principle. Mastering entire scrolls without error was how Jianghuai established his loyalty [?]. The disposition and path of learning certainly depend upon deeply sustained effort; concentrating so intently that he did not taste his food was how Junhou became a thoroughly learned scholar [?]. One who was devoted to the Zuo Commentary pacified Wu; one who carried his hoe while farming was appointed chief minister. Why, then, did someone who did not seek exhaustive understanding attain still greater things? One repeated his reading fifty times without exhausting its meaning; another repeated it eight or nine times and was acclaimed as outstanding [?]. Why, then, did someone who did not know the song “Qi Zhao” prove instead to possess genuine substance? Hesitating before a narrow, steep ascent, one changes one's winding gait; entering the road and dwelling in the house, who can accord with the enduring way of a hundred generations [?]? You candidates seek the beginnings of understanding behind the lowered study curtain; the responsible officials hold the balance in assessing you.

Question: To serve one's ruler by bringing him worthy men is the highest service of a minister. Neither forming cliques nor acting from factional allegiance: this was praised by men of old. Jing Boli went to Shangdang, and Zigao to Xihe. “Draw the bow and shoot at him as he approaches”; “You should leave!” Was such conduct worthy of Jie Hu's recommendation [?]? Yet impartiality proceeds from oneself, and selfishness then melts away; discernment depends on what one holds fast to, but the mirror of judgment is often clouded [?]. Looking at earlier records, however, some men seem to have accomplished this with ease. Zishi discerned someone a thousand li away; two boys became two worthies [?]. Without knowing Zhonggong well, and without spending a night with Fenggao [?], they nevertheless never exceeded the bounds of sound appraisal. Was there, then, something divinely perceptive in the friendship of Qiao and Zha? The mutual understanding of Guan and Bao seemed like a revelation from Heaven. Inferring great abilities from small signs, assigning responsibilities by distinguishing between milu deer and other deer, and having Geng take charge of the milu deer—was this how Chen Ruzi was supplied with a household steward [?]? Establishing friendship through kinship: as for the visiting card …

title: 嘉靖二十八年山西鄉試錄
text:
漫滅劉則干將亦汝南俗之評乎四奇
有四難之忌四短有四安之報建功之
路不一脩辭之柄多浮欲使青白不眩
真贗罔伏夫子慨於澹臺孔明誤於馬
謖其可無懲哉張輔優劣名士孔融昌
論汝潁朏以狗聲乃皆洞燭諸士平居
雌黃編簡異日稱量天下請聞遠觀之
法以助主司之明
問三晉古冀州地也環以龍門太行紀以
===
大河汾沁風氣所萃靈秀所鍾自古聖
賢應運疊出遐哉邈矣平陽蒲坂堯舜
所都精一執中之傳固本原之地也士
生其間豈無邃於理學者乎即如王通
氏講道河汾銳志希聖明德新民之學
寔拳拳矣何次理學者自孟子之後即
繼以周程張朱而通不與焉不知通於
四子果無可頡頏者歟至於我
朝道化浹洽人文彬彬雖童弁亦能談濂洛
punctuated:
漫滅劉則，干將亦汝南俗之評乎？四奇有四難之忌，四短有四安之報。建功之路不一，脩辭之柄多浮。欲使青白不眩，真贗罔伏，夫子慨於澹臺，孔明誤於馬謖，其可無懲哉？張輔優劣名士，孔融昌論汝潁，朏以狗聲，乃皆洞燭諸士。平居雌黃編簡，異日稱量天下，請聞遠觀之法，以助主司之明。
問：三晉古冀州地也，環以龍門、太行，紀以大河、汾、沁，風氣所萃，靈秀所鍾，自古聖賢應運疊出，遐哉邈矣！平陽、蒲坂，堯舜所都，精一執中之傳，固本原之地也。士生其間，豈無邃於理學者乎？即如王通氏，講道河汾，銳志希聖，明德新民之學，寔拳拳矣。何次理學者，自孟子之後，即繼以周、程、張、朱，而通不與焉？不知通於四子，果無可頡頏者歟？至於我朝，道化浹洽，人文彬彬，雖童弁亦能談濂洛
translation_en:
…obliterating Liu Ze [?]—was Gan Jiang likewise judged according to the customary assessments of Runan [?]? The four exceptional qualities incur the disfavor of the four difficulties; the four shortcomings receive the recompense of the four kinds of security [?]. There is more than one road to achievement, and the grounds of polished discourse are often superficial. We wish to prevent confusion between the worthy and unworthy and to leave neither the genuine nor the counterfeit concealed. Yet the Master regretted his judgment of Tantai, and Kongming erred concerning Ma Su. Can we fail to take warning? Zhang Fu ranked eminent men; Kong Rong spoke expansively about the men of Ru and Ying; Fei judged by the sound of a dog [?]. All these, then, saw penetratingly into the qualities of men. In ordinary life you pass judgment upon written records; someday you will weigh the men of the empire. Please explain the method of assessing men from afar, to assist the chief examiner’s discernment.
Question: The Three Jin territories occupy the lands of ancient Jizhou. Encircled by Longmen and the Taihang Mountains, and marked out by the Yellow River and the Fen and Qin rivers, this is a place where vital influences converge and spiritual excellence gathers. Since antiquity, sages and worthies have arisen here in succession as their times required. How remote and distant those beginnings! Pingyang and Puban were the capitals of Yao and Shun: this is indeed the place of origin of the transmitted teaching to remain discerning and single-minded and hold fast to the Mean. Among scholars born here, can there be none deeply versed in the Learning of Principle? Take Wang Tong: he expounded the Way in the region of the Yellow and Fen rivers, resolutely aspiring to sagehood, and was devoted indeed to the learning of manifesting luminous virtue and renewing the people. Why, then, do those who arrange the succession of the Learning of Principle proceed directly from Mengzi to Zhou, Cheng, Zhang, and Zhu, leaving Tong out? Could Tong truly have nothing to rival these four masters? Under our dynasty, the transforming influence of the Way has spread everywhere, and literary culture flourishes. Even boys wearing their caps can discuss the learning of Lian and Luo…

title: 嘉靖二十八年山西鄉試錄
text:
之學究其成就多寡反出宋儒之下何
也百餘年來論理學者惟重薛瑄氏今
觀其讀書從政二錄眞有與四子相發
明者不知其躬行實踐爲衆論所歸者
亦有與四子相後先者乎茲欲議以王
通薛瑄從祀於
廟庭果可以定衆論乎夫胡元閏位猶有實
行之儒董韓續文尚崇俎豆之列遺薛
子似亢非矣或謂註周禮者續大事記
===
者預集尚書會選者著四書五經私抄
者皆以道鳴也與文清可同祀乎抑獨
有所推尊乎諸士尚友天下況其鄉人
也悉所聞而評之
punctuated: 之學，究其成就多寡，反出宋儒之下，何也？百餘年來，論理學者惟重薛瑄氏。今觀其讀書、從政二錄，眞有與四子相發明者。不知其躬行實踐，爲衆論所歸者，亦有與四子相後先者乎？茲欲議以王通、薛瑄從祀於廟庭，果可以定衆論乎？夫胡元閏位，猶有實行之儒董、韓、續、文，尚崇俎豆之列，遺薛子似亢非矣。或謂註《周禮》者、續《大事記》者、預集《尚書會選》者、著《四書五經私抄》者，皆以道鳴也，與文清可同祀乎？抑獨有所推尊乎？諸士尚友天下，況其鄉人也，悉所聞而評之。
translation_en:
…the learning of those schools. Yet when we examine how many have attained success in it, they fall below the Confucians of the Song. Why is this? For more than a hundred years, those discussing the learning of principle have esteemed only Xue Xuan. Now, examining his two Records, on Reading and on Government Service, we find that they indeed illuminate, and are illuminated by, the teachings of the four masters. As for his personal conduct and practical application, which have won general acclaim, can these likewise rank alongside those of the four masters? If we now propose admitting Wang Tong and Xue Xuan to accompanying sacrifices in the Confucian temple, can this truly settle public opinion?

Even under the alien Yuan, whose rule occupied an intercalary place in the dynastic succession, there were Confucians of genuine practical conduct—Dong, Han, Xu, and Wen—who are still honored among those receiving sacrificial offerings. To leave Master Xue out seems decidedly wrong [?]. Some say that the man who annotated the Rites of Zhou, the man who continued the Record of Major Events, the man who participated in compiling the Collected Selections on the Book of Documents, and the man who wrote the Private Notes on the Four Books and Five Classics all became renowned for the Way. May they receive sacrifices together with Wenqing [Xue Xuan]? Or is there one who deserves particular veneration? You scholars seek worthy friends throughout the realm, including among men of the past; how much more should you do so among men of your own native region! Set out all you have heard and assess them.

title: 嘉靖二十八年山西鄉試錄
text:

punctuated:
中式舉人六十五名。

第一名王崇雅，蒲州學附學生，書。
第二名張四維，蒲州學生，易。
第三名吳國詔，代州學增廣生，詩。
第四名金商賓，平陽府學生，春秋。
第五名郭志仁，澤州學生，禮記。
第六名劉有誠，石州學增廣生，易。
第七名張三宅，盂縣學生，書。
第八名張日庠，代州學生，詩。
第九名王道行，太原府學附學生，易。
第十名武道脩，介休縣學生，春秋。
第十一名桂廷輔，榆次縣學生，詩。
第十二名嚴三省，文水縣學生，易。
第十三名楊元義，交城縣學生，書。
第十四名趙可化，榆次縣學增廣生，詩。
第十五名馮舜漁，蒲州學附學生，禮記。
第十六名楊希哲，忻州學生，詩。
translation_en:
Sixty-five successful provincial graduates (juren).

First: Wang Chongya, an attached student at the Puzhou school. His examination classic was the Book of Documents.
Second: Zhang Siwei, a student at the Puzhou school. His examination classic was the Book of Changes.
Third: Wu Guozhao, an additional-quota student at the Daizhou school. His examination classic was the Book of Odes.
Fourth: Jin Shangbin, a student at the Pingyang Prefectural School. His examination classic was the Spring and Autumn Annals.
Fifth: Guo Zhiren, a student at the Zezhou school. His examination classic was the Book of Rites.
Sixth: Liu Youcheng, an additional-quota student at the Shizhou school. His examination classic was the Book of Changes.
Seventh: Zhang Sanzhai, a student at the Yu County school. His examination classic was the Book of Documents.
Eighth: Zhang Rixiang, a student at the Daizhou school. His examination classic was the Book of Odes.
Ninth: Wang Daoxing, an attached student at the Taiyuan Prefectural School. His examination classic was the Book of Changes.
Tenth: Wu Daoxiu, a student at the Jiexiu County school. His examination classic was the Spring and Autumn Annals.
Eleventh: Gui Tingfu, a student at the Yuci County school. His examination classic was the Book of Odes.
Twelfth: Yan Sansheng, a student at the Wenshui County school. His examination classic was the Book of Changes.

title: 嘉靖二十八年山西鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
能行五者於天下為仁矣請問之曰恭寛
信敏惠
王崇雅
同考試官教諭明　批〔認理之文氣象自別仁至難〕
言是可試矣
考試官教諭朱　批〔詞不尚浮綽有天趣〕
考試官教諭鄭　批〔若親授受孔門者〕
===
聖人示賢者所以為仁因其問而實之焉夫仁
之難成久矣非全體而不息者不能也既明其
幾而復列其目賢者可不勉乎子張問仁於夫
子夫子告之意豈不曰無內無外乃天德之精
純可大可久則求仁之體要蓋仁統天下之善
也而於一則行而未成矣仁體事而無不在也
有所間則成而亦息矣能知理因事而異用行
是五者隨所感以善其應不憚夫率履之功情
因地而易遷行於天下隨所寓以堅其操不阻
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

能行五者於天下，為仁矣。請問之。曰：「恭、寛、信、敏、惠。」

王崇雅

同考試官教諭明，批〔認理之文，氣象自別。仁至難〕言，是可試矣。

考試官教諭朱，批〔詞不尚浮，綽有天趣。〕

考試官教諭鄭，批〔若親授受孔門者。〕

聖人示賢者所以為仁，因其問而實之焉。夫仁之難成久矣，非全體而不息者不能也。既明其幾，而復列其目，賢者可不勉乎？子張問仁於夫子，夫子告之，意豈不曰：無內無外，乃天德之精純；可大可久，則求仁之體要。蓋仁統天下之善也，而於一則行而未成矣；仁體事而無不在也，有所間則成而亦息矣。能知理因事而異用，行是五者，隨所感以善其應，不憚夫率履之功；情因地而易遷，行於天下，隨所寓以堅其操，不阻
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

“To be able to practice five things throughout the world constitutes benevolence.” He asked what they were. The Master said: “Respectfulness, generosity, trustworthiness, diligence, and kindness.”

Wang Chongya

Associate Examiner Ming, Instructor, comments: “An essay that grasps principle has a distinctive bearing. Benevolence is exceedingly difficult to discuss; this may stand the test.”

Examiner Zhu, Instructor, comments: “The wording does not prize superficial embellishment and abounds in natural charm.”

Examiner Zheng, Instructor, comments: “As though he had personally received instruction in the school of Confucius.”

The sage showed the worthy man how to practice benevolence and, in response to his question, gave it concrete substance. Now, the difficulty of achieving benevolence has long been recognized. None can achieve it without embodying it fully and without ceasing. Having explained its subtle workings and then enumerated its particulars, could the worthy man fail to exert himself? Zizhang asked the Master about benevolence. In instructing him, was the Master’s meaning not this: To make no distinction between within and without is the pure essence of Heaven’s virtue; to be capable of greatness and endurance is the essential basis for seeking benevolence. Benevolence encompasses all goodness under Heaven, yet if confined to one aspect [?], it is practiced but not fully achieved. Benevolence embodies every affair and is present everywhere; if there is any interruption, even when achieved, it will cease. If one can understand that principle functions differently according to the affair, and practice these five things, responding well to whatever moves one, without shrinking from the effort of putting them into practice; and, since feelings readily shift with circumstances, practice them throughout the world, maintaining firm conduct wherever one finds oneself, without being obstructed …

title: 嘉靖二十八年山西鄉試錄
text:
夫半塗之廢是可以爲仁矣其爲器重故不器
者舉之耳其爲道遠故致遠者兼之耳子張則
知夫子至敎固寓夫不發之幾憤悱旣通於是
有繼志之問夫子乃悉數而終之曰恭寬信敏
惠禮不可以去身恭則整齊嚴肅撝其謙矣量
不可以絕物寬則含弘光大昭其度矣信不由
衷僞斯載焉无妄而往可也不務時敏疑斯蓄
焉剛建而應可也屯膏未光施斯匱焉德愛而
充周焉可也是五者體立則天下仰之用行則
===
天下應之故所當行於天下者也吁始曰五者
徒陳其數聖人有隱乎善待問者也繼於五者
乃終其物聖人有加乎善答問者也惜乎張之
學竟限於日月至焉之徒夫子之憂莫解其難
並爲仁之失此固分量之限而傳道之難也雖
然道原於一散歸於宗仁人心也恭寬信敏惠
不過存其一心以復其一理耳然寬惠者多不
足於敏恭信者多不足於惠敏決者多不足於
寬故合併乃爲仁
punctuated:
夫半塗之廢，是可以爲仁矣。其爲器重，故不器者舉之耳；其爲道遠，故致遠者兼之耳。子張則知夫子至敎，固寓夫不發之幾，憤悱旣通，於是有繼志之問。夫子乃悉數而終之曰：「恭、寬、信、敏、惠。」禮不可以去身，恭則整齊嚴肅，撝其謙矣；量不可以絕物，寬則含弘光大，昭其度矣。信不由衷，僞斯載焉，无妄而往可也；不務時敏，疑斯蓄焉，剛建而應可也；屯膏未光，施斯匱焉，德愛而充周焉可也。是五者，體立則天下仰之，用行則天下應之，故所當行於天下者也。
吁！始曰五者，徒陳其數，聖人有隱乎？善待問者也。繼於五者，乃終其物，聖人有加乎？善答問者也。惜乎張之學，竟限於日月至焉之徒，夫子之憂莫解，其難並爲仁之失，此固分量之限而傳道之難也。雖然，道原於一，散歸於宗。仁，人心也。恭、寬、信、敏、惠，不過存其一心以復其一理耳。然寬惠者多不足於敏，恭信者多不足於惠，敏決者多不足於寬，故合併乃爲仁。
translation_en:
… the failure of abandoning the course halfway. In this way one can practice benevolence. The burden is heavy; hence only one who is not confined to a single function can bear it. The road is long; hence only one capable of reaching far can embrace all its requirements. Zizhang understood that the Master's supreme teaching contained subtle implications not yet expressed. His eager striving to understand and struggle to articulate his thoughts having found an opening, he asked a further question to carry forward the Master's intent. The Master then enumerated them fully, completing his teaching with the words: “Reverence, generosity, trustworthiness, diligence, and kindness.” Ritual propriety must never depart from one's person: through reverence one becomes orderly, solemn, and dignified, giving expression to humility. One's capacity must not exclude others: through generosity one becomes inclusive, capacious, luminous, and great, displaying the breadth of one's tolerance. If trustworthiness does not come from the heart, falsehood enters in; one should proceed without falsity. If one does not strive for timely diligence, doubts accumulate; one should respond with firmness and vigor. If beneficence is hoarded and has not yet shone forth, giving becomes deficient; one should make virtuous love abundant and all-embracing. When the substance of these five is established, all under Heaven look up to it; when their functions are put into practice, all under Heaven respond. Thus these are what one ought to practice throughout the world.
Ah! At first he spoke of “five,” merely stating their number. Was the sage concealing anything? He knew well how to await a question. Subsequently, concerning these five, he fully disclosed their content. Was the sage adding anything? He knew well how to answer a question. Regrettably, Zizhang's learning ultimately remained limited to that of those who attain benevolence only for a day or a month. The Master's concern remained unresolved: the difficulty lay in the failure to practice all these together as benevolence [?]. This indeed reflects the limits of individual capacity and the difficulty of transmitting the Way. Nevertheless, the Way originates in unity, and its dispersed manifestations return to their source. Benevolence is the human heart. Reverence, generosity, trustworthiness, diligence, and kindness amount simply to preserving the unity of one's heart in order to recover its single principle. Yet those who are generous and kind are often deficient in diligence; those who are reverent and trustworthy are often deficient in kindness; and those who are diligent and decisive are often deficient in generosity. Thus only by bringing them all together does one achieve benevolence.

title: 嘉靖二十八年山西鄉試錄
text:
自誠明謂之性自明誠謂之教誠則明矣
明則誠矣
張四維
同考試官教諭李　批〔中庸奧旨發揮殆盡蓋實用其功而明生焉〕
同考試官教諭姜　批〔不事牽合不煩繩削而聖賢之藴躍如〕
考試官教諭朱　批〔說理文字逈脫言詮〕
考試官教諭鄭　批〔然得而歎章故錄之〕
===
夫賢於天人之道辨其異而歸之同也夫天人
之不同者道也及其成功則一焉未至於至誠
者可不勉乎予子思子意豈不曰聖人之生也不
數斷道之寄者常存故生知之質不可自諉於
難齊而至命之功則實有序而可造耳彼自誠
而明者一理內藴精粹無貳而道之散殊莫不
燭焉是謂之性也蓋人性之中本無一物之或
雜亦無一物之弗照適得吾體固天與之无妄
耳性分之外其容有加乎自明而誠者因物察
punctuated:
自誠明謂之性，自明誠謂之教。誠則明矣，明則誠矣。

張四維

同考試官教諭李　批〔中庸奧旨發揮殆盡，蓋實用其功而明生焉。〕
同考試官教諭姜　批〔不事牽合，不煩繩削，而聖賢之藴躍如。〕
考試官教諭朱　批〔說理文字，逈脫言詮。〕

夫賢於天人之道，辨其異而歸之同也。夫天人之不同者，道也；及其成功，則一焉。未至於至誠者，可不勉乎？予子思子意，豈不曰：聖人之生也不數，斷道之寄者常存，故生知之質不可自諉於難齊，而至命之功則實有序而可造耳。彼自誠而明者，一理內藴，精粹無貳，而道之散殊莫不燭焉，是謂之性也。蓋人性之中，本無一物之或雜，亦無一物之弗照，適得吾體，固天與之无妄耳。性分之外，其容有加乎？自明而誠者，因物察
translation_en:
“To proceed from sincerity to understanding is called nature; to proceed from understanding to sincerity is called instruction. With sincerity comes understanding; with understanding comes sincerity.”

Zhang Siwei

Associate Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: “The profound purport of the Doctrine of the Mean is expounded almost exhaustively. Surely he has truly applied himself to the work, and understanding has arisen from it.”
Associate Examiner Jiang, Instructor, comments: “Without contrived connections or laborious trimming, the inner meaning of the sages and worthies stands vividly revealed.”
Examiner Zhu, Instructor, comments: “Writing that explains principle while rising far beyond verbal exposition.”
Examiner Zheng, Instructor, comments: “An essay that elicits assent and admiration [?]; therefore I have selected it.”

Now, the worthy, in relation to the ways of Heaven and humanity [?], distinguish their differences and bring them back to their common ground. What differs between Heaven and humanity is the path; when their work is accomplished, however, they are one. Can those who have not yet attained utmost sincerity fail to exert themselves? As I understand Master Zisi’s intention [?], does he not mean this: sages are seldom born, yet those in whom the Way is lodged always remain [?]. Thus one cannot excuse oneself on the grounds that the endowment of those born knowing is difficult to equal; the work of attaining one’s Heaven-conferred destiny truly has an ordered progression through which attainment is possible.

For those who proceed from sincerity to understanding, the single principle is contained within, pure and undivided, and none of the Way’s diverse manifestations remains unilluminated. This is called nature. Within human nature there is originally nothing admixed and nothing left unilluminated. One simply realizes one’s own fundamental being: this is the freedom from falsity bestowed by Heaven. Could anything be added beyond what is inherent in one’s nature? Those who proceed from understanding to sincerity examine, through things …

title: 嘉靖二十八年山西鄉試錄
text:
則循序致詳而誠之功用亦允蹈焉是謂之教
也蓋開教之後觸其類而去蔽閑其邪而存誠
不失吾常固下學之善反耳脩道之教其功有
歸乎然自其等而較之似不可以強同要其至
而言之亦曷嘗有終異哉自誠而明者明非待
於強探也有主而虛隨在各足本體之旣純睿
知之自出也其得之非思其中之非勉中孚涵
常覺之妙誠立有明通之幾固其理之不可誣
者矣自明而誠者誠非遂至於懸絕也深造而
===
得不遠而復旣眞知夫善而不淆者必實用其
力而不懈也擇善以致其精固執以全其一是
知幾爲入德之本而知止實能得之基亦其理
之所必至者矣吁性原於天君子有弗性焉敎
由於人君子懼弗習焉此因知勉行所以可聖
而愚明柔強由於此道也子思之言其釋前章
夫子之意乎噫信斯言也則至誠易矣奚不多
見於天下也化物之情昏於感應百倍之力病
於因循故子思作中庸以憂道學也悉厥往來
punctuated: 則，循序致詳，而誠之功用亦允蹈焉，是謂之教也。蓋開教之後，觸其類而去蔽，閑其邪而存誠，不失吾常，固下學之善反耳。脩道之教，其功有歸乎？然自其等而較之，似不可以強同；要其至而言之，亦曷嘗有終異哉？自誠而明者，明非待於強探也，有主而虛，隨在各足，本體之旣純，睿知之自出也。其得之非思，其中之非勉，中孚涵常覺之妙，誠立有明通之幾，固其理之不可誣者矣。自明而誠者，誠非遂至於懸絕也，深造而得，不遠而復，旣眞知夫善而不淆者，必實用其力而不懈也。擇善以致其精，固執以全其一，是知幾爲入德之本，而知止實能得之基，亦其理之所必至者矣。吁！性原於天，君子有弗性焉；敎由於人，君子懼弗習焉。此因知勉行所以可聖，而愚明柔強由於此道也。子思之言，其釋前章夫子之意乎？噫！信斯言也，則至誠易矣，奚不多見於天下也？化物之情昏於感應，百倍之力病於因循，故子思作《中庸》以憂道學也。悉厥往來
translation_en:
…principles, proceeding in order to attain detailed understanding, and thus truly putting sincerity into practice: this is called instruction. Once instruction has begun, one encounters related instances and removes obscurations, guards against what is deviant and preserves sincerity. In keeping our constant nature intact, this is simply the successful return achieved through learning below. Does instruction in cultivating the Way not have an outcome toward which its efforts converge? Yet when these approaches are compared in terms of their respective levels, it seems impossible to force them into sameness; considered in terms of their ultimate attainment, however, how could they ever remain different in the end?

For those who proceed from sincerity to understanding, understanding does not depend upon strenuous investigation. Having an inner master yet remaining open, they are sufficient wherever they find themselves. Once their fundamental nature is pure, sagely wisdom emerges of itself. Their attainment requires no deliberation; their hitting the mark requires no exertion. Inner trustworthiness contains the subtle efficacy of constant awareness; once sincerity is established, it holds the incipient workings of penetrating understanding. This is assuredly a principle that cannot be gainsaid.

For those who proceed from understanding to sincerity, sincerity is not thereby left impossibly remote. Through profound study they attain it; before straying far, they return. Once they truly understand goodness without confusion, they must apply their strength in earnest and without slackening. They choose what is good to attain refinement and hold firmly to it to preserve unity. Thus discerning incipient workings is the root of entering into virtue, while knowing where to rest is truly the foundation for attaining it. This, too, is the necessary outcome of the principle involved.

Ah! Nature originates in Heaven, yet there are things the gentleman does not regard as dictated by his nature. Instruction comes from human beings, and the gentleman fears failing to practice it. This is why knowing through difficulty [?] and acting through effort can lead to sagehood, and why the foolish become discerning and the weak become strong through this Way. Do Zisi’s words not explain the Master’s meaning in the preceding chapter? Alas! If these words are true, perfect sincerity would be easy. Why, then, is it not more frequently seen throughout the world? Our feelings, transformed by external things, become clouded amid stimulus and response; the effort that should be a hundredfold is impaired by habitual inaction. Thus Zisi composed the Doctrine of the Mean out of concern for the learning of the Way. To comprehend fully their comings and goings…

title: 嘉靖二十八年山西鄉試錄
text:
之朋從遂有反鑑之索則岐誠明而卒二之與
者味定性之書然後中庸有從入焉
江漢以濯之秋陽以暴之皜皜乎不可尚
已
金商賀
考試官教諭朱　批〔發曾子之意殆盡〕
考試官教諭鄭　批〔典重清新〕
大賢象聖人之道德極盛而不可加也蓋聖之
盛者難乎其爲繼也大賢極言以形容之其尊
===
師也不亦至乎此曾子之言而孟子述之所以
責陳相也意謂子夏子游子張蘁曾子以事有
若爲其似夫子也曾子旣不以爲可矣復贊之
曰子之所謂不可者非有他也以孔子非有若
之可擬也試言之水之積也不厚吾未與其潔
也江漢則水之會焉濯萬物者莫潔乎此矣夫
子之道德齋戒以洗其心一疵其不存乎陽之
氣也猶微物未見其化也秋陽則氣之烈焉燥
萬物者莫熯乎此矣夫子之道德高朗以成其
punctuated:
之朋從，遂有反鑑之索，則岐誠明而卒二之。與者味定性之書，然後中庸有從入焉。
「江漢以濯之，秋陽以暴之，皜皜乎不可尚已。」
金商賀
考試官教諭朱批〔發曾子之意殆盡〕
考試官教諭鄭批〔典重清新〕
大賢象聖人之道德極盛而不可加也。蓋聖之盛者，難乎其爲繼也。大賢極言以形容之，其尊師也不亦至乎？此曾子之言，而孟子述之，所以責陳相也。意謂子夏、子游、子張蘁曾子以事有若，爲其似夫子也。曾子旣不以爲可矣，復贊之曰：「子之所謂不可者，非有他也，以孔子非有若之可擬也。試言之：水之積也不厚，吾未與其潔也；江漢則水之會焉，濯萬物者莫潔乎此矣。夫子之道德，齋戒以洗其心，一疵其不存乎？陽之氣也猶微，物未見其化也；秋陽則氣之烈焉，燥萬物者莫熯乎此矣。夫子之道德，高朗以成其
translation_en:
…their associated comings and goings, there consequently arose a search for reflective illumination [?], which divided sincerity from understanding and ultimately treated them as two. Those concerned [?] should ponder the Letter on Calming the Nature (Dingxing shu); only then will they find a way into the Doctrine of the Mean.
“Washed in the Jiang and Han rivers, exposed to the autumn sun—so gleaming white that nothing can surpass it!”
Jin Shanghe
Examiner Zhu, Instructor: 〔Brings out Zengzi’s meaning almost exhaustively.〕
Examiner Zheng, Instructor: 〔Dignified and weighty, lucid and fresh.〕
A great worthy depicts the sage’s Way and virtue as supremely flourishing and admitting of no addition. Indeed, the sage’s supreme excellence is difficult to equal. The great worthy employs the strongest language to describe it: does this not show the utmost reverence for his teacher? These are Zengzi’s words, which Mengzi recounts to rebuke Chen Xiang. Their meaning is this: Zixia, Ziyou, and Zizhang urged [?] Zengzi to serve You Ruo because he resembled the Master. Zengzi had already deemed this unacceptable, and further elaborated in praise of the Master, saying: “My reason for declaring it unacceptable is simply that You Ruo cannot be compared with Kongzi. Let me explain. When an accumulation of water lacks depth, I do not concede its purity. But the Jiang and Han are where waters converge; for washing the myriad things, nothing is purer. As for the Master’s Way and virtue, through purification and abstinence he washes his heart: could even a single blemish remain? When the force of yang is still slight, things show no sign of its transforming influence. But in the autumn sun this force is intense; for drying the myriad things, nothing is more parching. As for the Master’s Way and virtue, through loftiness and clarity he brings to completion his…

title: 嘉靖二十八年山西鄉試錄
text:
象萬理其明淨乎濯以江漢濯之潔也真性湛
而物累忘暴以秋陽暴之白也陽明勝而陰濁
微全體之兼該有得乎上律下襲之妙大用之
顯著自神其經天緯地之文世雖有反濁求清
者不過餘波之及耳淵源之盛則探而莫測矣
世雖有昭德塞違者不過容光之被耳離明之
體則仰而彌高矣自生民以來未有能盛雖後
聖有作亦莫之與京豈可得而尚乎哉雖然擬
而非倫者門人矣尚有遺愛焉不忘其師者也
===
知足以知者曾子矣尊無二尚焉不倍其師者
也彼陳良之為師而陳相之為徒何其異於曾
子乎抑至聖難知賢人易識此門人之見所以
眩耳子禽賢子貢西河疑子夏固不徒有若之
似已也夫子之道亘古今莫尚焉乃知曾子所
以不可也雖然以夫子即有若則不可學夫子
而不先之以有若又不可蓋希賢則聖有序當
循也噫有若不可見矣後世美千頃於叔度贊
光霽於茂叔其亦聖人之遺乎
punctuated: 象，萬理其明淨乎！濯以江漢，濯之潔也，真性湛而物累忘；暴以秋陽，暴之白也，陽明勝而陰濁微。全體之兼該，有得乎上律下襲之妙；大用之顯著，自神其經天緯地之文。世雖有反濁求清者，不過餘波之及耳，淵源之盛則探而莫測矣；世雖有昭德塞違者，不過容光之被耳，離明之體則仰而彌高矣。自生民以來，未有能盛，雖後聖有作，亦莫之與京，豈可得而尚乎哉！雖然，擬而非倫者，門人矣，尚有遺愛焉，不忘其師者也；知足以知者，曾子矣，尊無二尚焉，不倍其師者也。彼陳良之為師，而陳相之為徒，何其異於曾子乎！抑至聖難知，賢人易識，此門人之見所以眩耳。子禽賢子貢，西河疑子夏，固不徒有若之似已也。夫子之道亘古今，莫尚焉，乃知曾子所以不可也。雖然，以夫子即有若則不可，學夫子而不先之以有若又不可，蓋希賢則聖，有序當循也。噫！有若不可見矣，後世美千頃於叔度，贊光霽於茂叔，其亦聖人之遺乎？
translation_en:
…manifest form: how luminous and pure are all its principles! Washed in the Jiang and Han rivers, one is cleansed: the true nature becomes limpid, and the burdens of external things are forgotten. Exposed to the autumn sun, one is bleached white: brightness and clarity prevail, while darkness and turbidity diminish. The comprehensiveness of his whole being embodies the subtlety of taking Heaven above as his rule and following Earth below; the manifest greatness of his activity wondrously displays the patterned order by which he orders Heaven and Earth. Though some in the world turn from turbidity and seek purity, they merely receive the reach of his remaining ripples; probe the abundance of their source, and its depth cannot be fathomed. Though some illuminate virtue and restrain wrongdoing, they merely receive his light as it penetrates a small opening; look up to the very substance of his radiance, and it grows ever higher. Since humankind first existed, none has been able to surpass him [?]. Even should a later sage arise, none could equal him. How could anyone surpass him?

Nevertheless, those who compared him with someone not of his order were his disciples. They still cherished their lingering affection and had not forgotten their teacher. The one whose wisdom sufficed to recognize him was Zengzi. In his reverence there could be no second object of supreme esteem: he did not betray his teacher. How different from Zengzi was the relationship between Chen Liang as teacher and Chen Xiang as disciple! Yet the supreme sage is difficult to understand, while a worthy man is easy to recognize; this is why the disciples’ judgment became confused. Ziqin considered Zigong the worthier, and the people of Xihe were uncertain about Zixia’s standing relative to Confucius. Certainly, such confusion was not confined to You Ruo’s resemblance to the Master. The Master’s Way extends through past and present, with none above it. Thus we understand why Zengzi would not consent.

Nevertheless, while it is unacceptable to equate the Master with You Ruo, it is also unacceptable to study the Master without first taking You Ruo as one’s model. For aspiring to worthiness leads to sagehood: there is a sequence that must be followed. Alas! You Ruo can no longer be seen. In later ages, people praised Shudu as a thousand-qing expanse of water and commended Maoshu as sunlight and clear skies after rain. Might these, too, be a legacy of the sage?

title: 嘉靖二十八年山西鄉試錄
text:
易
恒亨无咎利貞利有攸往
劉有誠
同考試官教諭姜　批
〔此篇場中上子頗能言之但於恒亨无咎處便涉用上講至利貞利往處多重疊相悖殊失明體適〕
同考試官教諭李　批
〔用之序獨此作從義理上發揮體認明白深爲有見宜錄以爲式〕
考試官教諭朱　批
〔此題上句重恒字下句重貞字註中道字且泛言至利貞方歸重於道此作下字精確殆邃於易者〕
〔議理之文典實可佳〕
===
考試官教諭鄭　批
〔費書〕
聖以具理之常者名夫卦俾聖以得理之常
者善其占蓋常以得正而爲善也否則乖其常
矣而何善之有哉且内巽外震伏羲何以命卦
曰恒蓋恒者常也其爲卦也震上巽下則上下
之位奠矣而震雷巽風二物又相與焉巽順震
動則素履之往若矣而二體六爻陰陽各相應
焉四者皆理之常名卦之義不在兹乎文王係
辭以爲君子之自脩也上達之機原於下學之
punctuated:
易

恒亨，无咎，利貞，利有攸往。

劉有誠

同考試官教諭姜批
〔此篇場中上子頗能言之，但於恒亨无咎處便涉用上講，至利貞利往處多重疊相悖，殊失明體適〕

同考試官教諭李批
〔用之序。獨此作從義理上發揮，體認明白，深爲有見，宜錄以爲式。〕

考試官教諭朱批
〔此題上句重恒字，下句重貞字。註中道字且泛言，至利貞方歸重於道。此作下字精確，殆邃於易者。〕
〔議理之文，典實可佳。〕

考試官教諭鄭批
〔費書。〕

聖以具理之常者名夫卦，俾聖以得理之常者善其占，蓋常以得正而爲善也。否則乖其常矣，而何善之有哉？且内巽外震，伏羲何以命卦曰恒？蓋恒者，常也。其爲卦也，震上巽下，則上下之位奠矣；而震雷巽風，二物又相與焉。巽順震動，則素履之往若矣；而二體六爻，陰陽各相應焉。四者皆理之常，名卦之義不在兹乎？文王係辭，以爲君子之自脩也，上達之機原於下學之
translation_en:
Book of Changes

“Constancy: success, no blame. It is beneficial to remain correct; it is beneficial to have somewhere to go.”

Liu Youcheng

Comment by Associate Examiner Jiang, Instructor:
〔The leading candidates [?] in the examination were quite capable of discussing this topic. But when explaining “Constancy: success, no blame,” they already ventured into its application; on reaching “beneficial to remain correct” and “beneficial to have somewhere to go,” they frequently repeated and contradicted themselves, badly disrupting the sequence of clarifying substance and appropriately…〕

〔…applying it. This composition alone develops the topic through moral principle, showing clear understanding and profound insight. It should be recorded as a model.〕

Comment by Examiner Zhu, Instructor:
〔In this topic, the first clause places emphasis on “constancy,” and the following clause on “correctness.” The word “Way” in the commentary is initially used in a general sense; only at “beneficial to remain correct” does the emphasis fall upon the Way. This composition uses words precisely; its author must have a profound understanding of the Changes.〕
〔A discussion of principle that is classically grounded and substantial: commendable.〕

Comment by Examiner Zheng, Instructor:
〔A waste of writing [?].〕

The sage named this hexagram for its embodiment of the constancy of principle, causing the sage [?] to pronounce its divination auspicious through attaining the constancy of principle. For constancy is good when it attains correctness. Otherwise, it departs from its proper constancy: what goodness could there be in that?

With Xun within and Zhen without, why did Fuxi name the hexagram Heng? Heng means constancy. In the constitution of this hexagram, Zhen is above and Xun below, so the positions of above and below are established; moreover, Zhen is thunder and Xun is wind, and these two things assist one another. Xun is yielding and Zhen is movement, so progress in one's customary conduct is smooth [?]; and within the two component trigrams and their six lines, yin and yang correspond to one another. All four features embody the constancy of principle. Does not the significance of the hexagram's name lie here?
