title: 嘉靖二十八年山西鄉試錄
text:
不專一簣之虧未免九仞之盡棄欲亨與无咎
難矣占者苟能久於其道而孜孜不遑恒於其
業而亹亹不倦則是志以帥氣勵自强不息之
操積習之下義理頓爾其開明思若啓之也行
若翼之也足於此而達於彼將有日進无疆之
休矣其亨何如勞以制逸嚴苦難則止之戒强
作之餘精神倍爾其淬銳无頻復之厲也无怠
勝之凶也修於己而孚於人且有夙夜永終之
譽矣其咎何有夫恒固有獲亨寡過之理使不
===
以正則道岸先迷徒恒何益必也擇善之審講
之平居者盡天德王道之純且信之愈篤小道
无能惑焉析理之精聞之師友者悉民彝物則
之粹且持之彌堅曲學莫之亂焉如此則一貞
之道既修萬應之途自順由是而發於事業則
義精而用自利國家可均也而天下亦可平也
諸艱歷試何往而不善乎由是而見之設施則
靜專而動自直天地可位也而萬物亦可育也
庶績咸凞何用而不神乎所謂亨與无咎至是
punctuated: 不專，一簣之虧，未免九仞之盡棄，欲亨與无咎難矣。占者苟能久於其道而孜孜不遑，恒於其業而亹亹不倦，則是志以帥氣，勵自强不息之操。積習之下，義理頓爾其開明，思若啓之也，行若翼之也。足於此而達於彼，將有日進无疆之休矣，其亨何如！勞以制逸，嚴苦難則止之戒。强作之餘，精神倍爾其淬銳，无頻復之厲也，无怠勝之凶也。修於己而孚於人，且有夙夜永終之譽矣，其咎何有！夫恒固有獲亨寡過之理，使不以正，則道岸先迷，徒恒何益？必也擇善之審，講之平居者盡天德王道之純，且信之愈篤，小道无能惑焉；析理之精，聞之師友者悉民彝物則之粹，且持之彌堅，曲學莫之亂焉。如此，則一貞之道既修，萬應之途自順。由是而發於事業，則義精而用自利，國家可均也，而天下亦可平也。諸艱歷試，何往而不善乎？由是而見之設施，則靜專而動自直，天地可位也，而萬物亦可育也。庶績咸凞，何用而不神乎？所謂亨與无咎，至是
translation_en:
…lack of single-minded dedication: falling short by a single basketful means abandoning the entire work of building a mound nine fathoms high. It would then be difficult to attain success and freedom from blame. If the diviner can long persist in his way, working diligently without respite, and remain constant in his undertaking, exerting himself tirelessly, then his resolve will command his vital energies and strengthen his commitment to unceasing self-improvement. Through accumulated practice, moral principles will suddenly become clear: his thinking will seem to receive illumination, and his conduct to be given wings. With a firm footing here, he will reach there, enjoying the blessing of daily progress without limit. How great his success will be! Through exertion he will restrain indolence, strictly heeding the warning against stopping when hardship arises. Through sustained effort, his spirit will become doubly tempered and keen. There will be neither the peril of repeatedly turning back nor the misfortune of being overcome by indolence. Cultivating himself and winning others’ trust, he will also earn praise for persevering morning and night to the very end. What blame could there be?

Constancy certainly contains the principle by which one attains success and reduces errors. But if it does not accord with correctness, one will lose sight of the shore of the Way from the outset. What benefit is there in mere persistence? One must choose the good with discrimination: what one studies in everyday life must consist entirely of the purity of Heaven’s virtue and the kingly Way. As one’s faith in these grows ever firmer, lesser ways will be unable to lead one astray. One must analyze principles precisely: what one learns from teachers and friends must consist entirely of the essence of the enduring human norms and the standards inherent in things. As one holds to these ever more firmly, distorted learning will be unable to cause confusion. Thus, once the way of steadfast correctness has been cultivated, the paths of responding to myriad circumstances will naturally run smoothly. When this finds expression in undertakings, moral understanding will be refined and its application naturally effective. The state can be equitably ordered, and all under Heaven can likewise be brought to peace. Tested successively through every difficulty, where could one go without doing well? When this is manifested in practical measures, one will be concentrated in stillness and naturally upright in action. Heaven and earth can take their proper places, and all things can likewise be nourished. With every undertaking flourishing, what application could fail to be wondrously efficacious? As for the success and freedom from blame spoken of, at this point…

title: 嘉靖二十八年山西鄉試錄
text:
其益驗矣恒可以不貞哉抑嘗因是而論之君
子之學進於恒而退於速天下之化成於久而
貞於一故伏羲命之以恒文王係之以貞夫子
他日論學易亦曰假我數年論行仁則曰王者
必世而又有思恒之嘆无非覺其迷以示其趨
也以此防世猶有欲速而甘於不違自畫而安
於小成者其亦不占而已矣噫
生生之謂易
王道行
===
同考試官教諭姜　批〔典實中有新奇取之〕
同考試官教諭李　批〔天命所以流行而不已者變而〕
〔已此作得之結尾及之人心尤達於理〕
考試官教諭朱　批〔說理文字錄以式諸士〕
考試官教諭鄭　批〔理明辭達究心易者〕
大傳指氣機之迭運者爲易之所由名焉夫陰
陽者氣也而有理以主之斯迭運而不窮矣非
天下之至變其孰能與於此且夫道之體用固
不外乎陰陽而變通之理則何嘗倚於陰陽彼
punctuated:
其益驗矣。恒可以不貞哉？抑嘗因是而論之：君子之學進於恒而退於速，天下之化成於久而貞於一。故伏羲命之以恒，文王係之以貞。夫子他日論學易，亦曰：「假我數年。」論行仁，則曰：「王者必世。」而又有思恒之嘆，无非覺其迷以示其趨也。以此防世，猶有欲速而甘於不違、自畫而安於小成者，其亦不占而已矣。噫！
生生之謂易
王道行
同考試官教諭姜，批〔典實中有新奇取之〕。
同考試官教諭李，批〔天命所以流行而不已者變而〕〔已此作得之結尾及之人心尤達於理〕。
考試官教諭朱，批〔說理文字錄以式諸士〕。
考試官教諭鄭，批〔理明辭達究心易者〕。
大傳指氣機之迭運者，爲易之所由名焉。夫陰陽者，氣也，而有理以主之，斯迭運而不窮矣。非天下之至變，其孰能與於此？且夫道之體用，固不外乎陰陽，而變通之理，則何嘗倚於陰陽？彼
translation_en:
…this is all the more clearly borne out. Can constancy dispense with correctness? I have also reflected on this: the learning of the gentleman advances through constancy and regresses through haste; the transformation of the world is accomplished through long duration and made steadfast through unity. Thus Fuxi named the hexagram Constancy, and King Wen appended to it the requirement of correctness. On another occasion, when discussing study of the Changes, the Master likewise said, “Give me a few more years.” Discussing the practice of benevolence, he said, “A true king would require a generation.” He also lamented the lack of constancy. All these sayings awaken people from their confusion and show them the course to follow. Yet even with these safeguards for the world, there are still those who seek quick results and are content with “not departing” [?], who set limits upon themselves and rest satisfied with small achievements. Such people simply do not consult the omens! Alas!

“Unceasing Generation Is What Is Called Change”
Wang Daoxing

Associate Examiner Jiang, Instructor, comments: “Amid its solid grounding in classical sources there is novelty. Accept it.”

Associate Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: “What makes Heaven’s mandate circulate without cease is change, and nothing more. This composition grasps that point. Its conclusion extends the discussion to the human mind, showing an especially penetrating understanding of principle.”

Examiner Zhu, Instructor, comments: “An essay that explains principle; recorded as a model for the scholars.”

Examiner Zheng, Instructor, comments: “Its principles are clear and its language expressive: the work of someone who has devoted himself to studying the Changes.”

The Great Commentary identifies the alternating movement of the workings of vital energy as the reason the Changes bears its name. Yin and yang are vital energy, but principle governs them; thus they alternate in their operation without exhaustion. Were this not the utmost transformation in the world, what could participate in such a process? Moreover, the substance and functioning of the Way assuredly do not lie outside yin and yang. Yet when has the principle of change and free passage ever depended upon yin and yang? That…

title: 嘉靖二十八年山西鄉試錄
text:
時乎陰也寂然不動太極之體於是乎立也然
體無定體惟變是體故靜極而陽生焉時乎陽
也有感遂通太極之用於是乎行也然用無定
用惟化是用故動極而陰生焉陰之生者陽之
化者為之也已往者過而來者禪其功冲漠無
朕之中若有使之者而自不容於不生也陽之
生者陰之變者為之也成功者退而進者代其
用太虛不言之表實有主之者而自不容於或
違也陰陽之相生如此易不即此而在乎蓋易
===
者變也理主夫氣者也動靜者時也道具於陰
不離乎靜而非靜之所可拘道行乎陽不外乎
動而非動之所能囿故變化而不窮為感遇為
聚散一皆此易之流行有定體者無定機夫豈
得而盡之耶成變化行鬼神莫非此理之昭著
有專能者無專功夫豈得而執之耶吁此天地
之道所以恒久而不已也卦爻之德所以推盪
而無窮者皆此變以為之耳造化也易書也不
均謂之易而何哉抑此心學也寂然不動者吾
punctuated: 時乎陰也，寂然不動，太極之體於是乎立也。然體無定體，惟變是體，故靜極而陽生焉。時乎陽也，有感遂通，太極之用於是乎行也。然用無定用，惟化是用，故動極而陰生焉。陰之生者，陽之化者為之也。已往者過，而來者禪其功，冲漠無朕之中，若有使之者，而自不容於不生也。陽之生者，陰之變者為之也。成功者退，而進者代其用，太虛不言之表，實有主之者，而自不容於或違也。陰陽之相生如此，易不即此而在乎？蓋易者，變也；理，主夫氣者也；動靜者，時也。道具於陰，不離乎靜，而非靜之所可拘；道行乎陽，不外乎動，而非動之所能囿。故變化而不窮，為感遇，為聚散，一皆此易之流行。有定體者無定機，夫豈得而盡之耶？成變化，行鬼神，莫非此理之昭著。有專能者無專功，夫豈得而執之耶？吁！此天地之道所以恒久而不已也。卦爻之德所以推盪而無窮者，皆此變以為之耳。造化也，易書也，不均謂之易而何哉？抑此心學也，寂然不動者，吾
translation_en:
…In the phase of yin, there is stillness without movement, and thus the substance of the Supreme Ultimate is established. Yet this substance has no fixed substance: change alone constitutes its substance. Thus, when stillness reaches its utmost, yang is born. In the phase of yang, stimulation brings responsive penetration, and thus the functioning of the Supreme Ultimate proceeds. Yet this functioning has no fixed functioning: transformation alone constitutes its functioning. Thus, when movement reaches its utmost, yin is born. The birth of yin is brought about by the transformation of yang. What has gone before passes away, and what comes after succeeds to its achievement. Amid utter emptiness and stillness, where no trace is apparent, it is as though something impels this process, so that generation cannot of itself fail to occur. The birth of yang is brought about by the change of yin. What has completed its achievement withdraws, and what advances takes over its function. Beyond the wordlessness of the Great Void, something truly governs this process, so that it cannot of itself deviate.

Such is the mutual generation of yin and yang. Is not change to be found precisely here? For change means alteration; principle governs material force; movement and stillness are successive phases. The Way is embodied in yin, inseparable from stillness, yet cannot be confined by stillness. The Way operates in yang, never apart from movement, yet cannot be circumscribed by movement. Thus change and transformation are inexhaustible: whether as stimulation and encounter or as gathering and dispersal, all are the flowing operation of this change. What has a determinate substance has no determinate workings—how could one exhaust it? Bringing transformations to completion and setting ghosts and spirits in motion: all are manifestations of this principle. What has a particular capacity has no exclusive achievement—how could one grasp it as something fixed?

Ah! This is why the Way of Heaven and Earth endures perpetually without ceasing. That the powers of the hexagrams and their lines impel and stir one another without limit is entirely the work of this change. The creative transformations of nature and the Book of Changes: what could both be called, if not ‘change’? Moreover, this is also the learning of the mind. That which is still and unmoving is my…

title: 嘉靖二十八年山西鄉試錄
text:
心之靜而生陰也感而遂通者吾心之動而生
陽也靜虛動直明通公溥則人與造化參矣彼
仁者見之謂之仁則往而不返知者見之謂之
知則物而不化是皆非生生之義也故張子曰
客感客形與無感無形惟盡性者能一之
書
惟皇上帝降衷于下民若有恒性克綏厥
猷惟后
張三宅
===
同考試官教諭明　批〔成湯以綏猷自任典中肩　道敎之意似同而異作者多昧此篇體認精切詞語春容錄之〕
考試官教諭朱　批〔形容聖學之純無踰於此〕
考試官教諭鄭　批〔意精辭達〕
商王原人性賦乎天成之則待於君焉蓋天能
賦人以性而已使之各安其道則天有不能與
矣謂非君人者之責乎成湯首揭此以告萬方
見君道之重也若曰天命之受予未敢用以爲
安君道所關蓋不敢不自以爲懼爾萬方亦知
punctuated:
心之靜而生陰也；感而遂通者，吾心之動而生陽也。靜虛動直，明通公溥，則人與造化參矣。彼仁者見之謂之仁，則往而不返；知者見之謂之知，則物而不化。是皆非生生之義也。故張子曰：「客感客形與無感無形，惟盡性者能一之。」
書
惟皇上帝降衷于下民，若有恒性，克綏厥猷，惟后。
張三宅
同考試官教諭明批〔成湯以綏猷自任，典中肩道敎之意似同而異，作者多昧。此篇體認精切，詞語春容，錄之。〕
考試官教諭朱批〔形容聖學之純，無踰於此。〕
考試官教諭鄭批〔意精辭達。〕
商王原人性賦乎天，成之則待於君焉。蓋天能賦人以性而已，使之各安其道，則天有不能與矣。謂非君人者之責乎？成湯首揭此以告萬方，見君道之重也。若曰：「天命之受，予未敢用以爲安；君道所關，蓋不敢不自以爲懼。爾萬方亦知」
translation_en:
…the stillness of my heart, which generates yin; responding to stimuli and thereby penetrating all things is the movement of my heart, which generates yang. Empty in stillness and upright in movement, lucid and comprehending, impartial and all-embracing—then a person participates alongside the transforming powers of Heaven and Earth. Those who are benevolent see it and call it benevolence, but proceed without returning; those who are wise see it and call it wisdom, but become bound to things without transformation. Neither grasps the meaning of ceaseless generation. Thus Master Zhang said: “Transient responses and transient forms, together with the absence of response and form—only those who fully realize their nature can unite them.”
Book of Documents
“August Heaven, the Lord on High, bestowed an inner moral norm upon the people below. To guide them in accordance with their constant nature and enable them to rest secure in their proper way is the ruler’s task.”
Zhang Sanzhai
Associate Examiner Ming, Instructor, comments: 〔Cheng Tang took securing the people in their proper way as his own responsibility. The meaning of ‘典中肩’ [?] and of the Way and its teaching appears similar but differs; writers often fail to understand this. This essay grasps the matter precisely and incisively, and its language has a springlike ease. Selected for inclusion.〕
Examiner Zhu, Instructor, comments: 〔Nothing surpasses this in portraying the purity of sagely learning.〕
Examiner Zheng, Instructor, comments: 〔The ideas are refined and the language expressive.〕
The king of Shang traced human nature to its endowment by Heaven, while its fulfillment depends upon the ruler. Heaven can only endow people with their nature; enabling each to rest secure in the proper way is something Heaven cannot itself accomplish. Can this be said not to be the responsibility of the ruler of men? Cheng Tang placed this point first in his proclamation to the myriad regions, revealing the weight of the ruler’s responsibility. It was as though he said: “Having received Heaven’s mandate, I have not dared to take it as grounds for resting at ease. Considering what the ruler’s duty entails, I dare not fail to regard it with apprehension. Do you in the myriad regions also know…”

title: 嘉靖二十八年山西鄉試錄
text:
之乎惟天於穆之命默降於蒸民資始之時無
所偏倚理隨形而自賦也天然自有之中陰隲
於萬物化醇之際純粹至善命與化而同流也
人惟順其自然適得夫繼善之始隨處發見是
固爲成性之良然清濁純雜氣之所禀者難齊
剛柔善惡情之交物者易動則恒性淆於客感
降衷異於天載矣若夫因性以牖民親義序別
信之見於事者比類以成其行緣理以設教仁
義禮智信之受於帝者盡職以叙其倫則惟后
===
也左右有道而觀感繫焉故殊途可同其歸矣
否則天道無心而成化百姓日用而不知何以
自綏其猷乎範圍不過而風俗同焉故從王而
歸於極矣蓋有其位而萬物覩有其德而身教
先實爲大君之宜乎吁民之盡性天猶不能究
其功而待君以成能一人之身關係如此其重
也成湯初有天下即以自任可謂知君師之職
矣嗣後秉彝之言繼發性善之理愈明接堯舜
禹心法之微而開萬世性學之原豈非聖人之
punctuated: 之乎？惟天於穆之命，默降於蒸民資始之時，無所偏倚，理隨形而自賦也。天然自有之中，陰隲於萬物化醇之際，純粹至善，命與化而同流也。人惟順其自然，適得夫繼善之始，隨處發見，是固爲成性之良。然清濁純雜，氣之所禀者難齊；剛柔善惡，情之交物者易動。則恒性淆於客感，降衷異於天載矣。若夫因性以牖民，親義序別信之見於事者，比類以成其行；緣理以設教，仁義禮智信之受於帝者，盡職以叙其倫，則惟后也。左右有道，而觀感繫焉，故殊途可同其歸矣。否則天道無心而成化，百姓日用而不知，何以自綏其猷乎？範圍不過，而風俗同焉，故從王而歸於極矣。蓋有其位而萬物覩，有其德而身教先，實爲大君之宜乎！吁！民之盡性，天猶不能究其功，而待君以成能。一人之身，關係如此其重也。成湯初有天下，即以自任，可謂知君師之職矣。嗣後秉彝之言繼發，性善之理愈明，接堯舜禹心法之微，而開萬世性學之原，豈非聖人之
translation_en:
…this? Heaven’s profound and silent mandate descends unseen when the people first receive their existence. Without partiality or deviation, principle is naturally bestowed along with bodily form. The mean inherent in nature is silently established as the myriad things undergo transformation and attain fullness. Pure and supremely good, the mandate flows together with the process of transformation. If people simply follow what is natural to them, they attain that beginning in which goodness is carried forward; wherever it manifests, it is indeed the goodness of their constituted nature. Yet the vital force they receive varies in clarity and turbidity, purity and admixture, and is difficult to make uniform. Their feelings, whether firm or yielding, good or bad, are easily stirred through contact with things. Thus their constant nature becomes confused by external impressions, and the moral core bestowed upon them diverges from Heaven’s workings.

To enlighten the people in accordance with their nature, bringing their conduct to completion by drawing together kindred instances of affection, righteousness, precedence, distinction, and trustworthiness as these appear in affairs; to establish instruction according to principle, fully discharging one’s duties so as to order human relationships through the benevolence, righteousness, ritual propriety, wisdom, and trustworthiness received from the Lord on High—this falls to the sovereign alone. When he guides and assists them according to the Way, their response to the example they behold depends upon him; thus different paths may lead to the same destination. Otherwise, since Heaven’s Way accomplishes transformation without deliberate intent, and the common people practice it daily without understanding it, how could they themselves bring their course into settled order? By encompassing them within bounds that do not transgress the proper measure, he brings their customs into accord; thus they follow the king and return to the supreme standard. Occupying his position, he stands before the eyes of all things; possessing his virtue, he leads through personal example. These are indeed the fitting responsibilities of the great ruler!

Ah! Even Heaven cannot complete the work of enabling the people to realize their nature fully, but awaits the ruler to bring its powers to fulfillment. So weighty are the responsibilities bound up in the person of a single man! When Cheng Tang first possessed All under Heaven, he immediately took this responsibility upon himself. He may truly be said to have understood the duties of ruler and teacher. Thereafter, statements about the people’s enduring moral norms continued to emerge, and the principle that human nature is good became ever clearer. Carrying forward the subtle teaching of the mind transmitted by Yao, Shun, and Yu, and opening the source of learning about human nature for all ages—was this not the sage’s …

title: 嘉靖二十八年山西鄉試錄
text:
訓哉雖然聖敬日躋制以禮義自綏其猷非一
日矣故觀湯誥者又當觀于盤銘
惟德惟義時乃大訓
楊元義
同考試官教諭明　批〔整而不滯質而有文〕
考試官教諭朱　批〔發盡周家忠厚之意〕
考試官教諭鄭　批〔是本色語〕
以性爲教者天下之至教也蓋德義者人性之
同有也以是爲訓非天下之至教乎康王命畢
===
公保釐東郊此則探本之論也若曰富而後教
固可使從善之輕然教外於性又何以盡感通
之道故毋曰殷民已染於陵蕩之習德不可以
與有爲也惟當訓之以德使悟其旣往之非未
殄夫怙侈之風義不可與有言也惟當訓之以
義使知夫立人之道或倡之躬行與必以德爲
履也以義爲路也正已而率物者不出乎天命
人心之正或演之敷言與曰爾惟尊德也爾惟
樂義也章好以示人者務發其秉彝好德之良
punctuated:
訓哉！雖然，聖敬日躋，制以禮義，自綏其猷非一日矣。故觀湯誥者，又當觀于盤銘。
惟德惟義，時乃大訓。
楊元義
同考試官教諭明，批〔整而不滯，質而有文〕
考試官教諭朱，批〔發盡周家忠厚之意〕
考試官教諭鄭，批〔是本色語〕
以性爲教者，天下之至教也。蓋德義者，人性之同有也。以是爲訓，非天下之至教乎？康王命畢公保釐東郊，此則探本之論也。若曰：富而後教，固可使從善之輕，然教外於性，又何以盡感通之道？故毋曰殷民已染於陵蕩之習，德不可以與有爲也，惟當訓之以德，使悟其旣往之非；未殄夫怙侈之風，義不可與有言也，惟當訓之以義，使知夫立人之道。或倡之躬行與？必以德爲履也，以義爲路也。正已而率物者，不出乎天命人心之正。或演之敷言與？曰爾惟尊德也，爾惟樂義也。章好以示人者，務發其秉彝好德之良
translation_en:
…instruction of a sage! Nevertheless, his sagely reverence rose daily; he regulated himself through ritual propriety and righteousness, and had long secured his own course. Thus, those who read the Announcement of Tang should also examine the inscription on his bathing basin.
“Virtue and righteousness alone: these are the great instruction.”
Yang Yuanyi
Associate Examiner Ming, Instructor, comments: “Orderly without being stiff; substantial yet refined.”
Examiner Zhu, Instructor, comments: “Fully brings out the spirit of loyalty and generosity of the house of Zhou.”
Examiner Zheng, Instructor, comments: “These are authentic, unadorned words.”
To teach through human nature is the highest teaching under Heaven. Virtue and righteousness are common possessions of human nature. Is making these the basis of instruction not the highest teaching under Heaven? When King Kang commanded the Duke of Bi to safeguard and govern the eastern suburbs, this was an argument that probed the roots. It was as though he said: Enriching the people before teaching them can indeed make it easy for them to follow goodness; but if teaching is external to their nature, how can it fully realize the way of moving them and eliciting a response? Thus, do not say that the people of Yin have already become steeped in overbearing and dissolute habits, so that nothing can be accomplished with them through virtue. Rather, instruct them through virtue, so that they recognize their past errors. Nor say that the tendency to indulge in extravagance has not yet been eradicated, so that righteousness cannot be discussed with them. Rather, instruct them through righteousness, so that they understand the way to establish themselves as human beings. Would you lead them through your own conduct? Then you must make virtue your practice and righteousness your path. Those who rectify themselves [?] and lead others remain within the rectitude of Heaven’s mandate and the human heart. Would you expound it through extended discourse? Say: ‘You must honor virtue; you must delight in righteousness.’ Those who make manifest what is good to guide others must strive to awaken their innate goodness in holding fast to their constant nature and loving virtue…

title: 嘉靖二十八年山西鄉試錄
text:
若此者不謂之大訓矣乎蓋教不可以範俗者
固不足以爲訓訓或出於己私者亦不可以爲
大令也訓以人所同得之德則本大道以爲公
而非分我之有執範於此者固可推之四海而
皆準訓以人所固有之義則因民性以爲牖而
非強彼之無振舉於此者固可徵諸庶民而皆
從以帝道率天下者雖不無繁簡之異制也然
而垂世立教之典不能求於彝倫之外以王道
先天下者雖不無因革之異宜也然而神化宜
===
民之術亦惟若乎人道之常信乎和衷之外無
餘理綏猷之外無善教矣公往保釐亦惟從事
於此焉可也噫康王可謂深得化民之本者與
抑於此而知周室享國之永也區區殷士初之
以謹始繼之以和中亦云厚矣而其背戾猶故
也雖加殄滅夫誰爲過康王之命畢公者亦惟
教之而已德義之外刑罰無聞焉孟子曰先王
有不忍人之心斯有不忍人之政矣康王之心
即不忍人之心也故造周業者文王也定周業
punctuated:
若此者，不謂之大訓矣乎？蓋教不可以範俗者，固不足以爲訓；訓或出於己私者，亦不可以爲大令也。訓以人所同得之德，則本大道以爲公，而非分我之有；執範於此者，固可推之四海而皆準。訓以人所固有之義，則因民性以爲牖，而非強彼之無；振舉於此者，固可徵諸庶民而皆從。以帝道率天下者，雖不無繁簡之異制也，然而垂世立教之典，不能求於彝倫之外；以王道先天下者，雖不無因革之異宜也，然而神化宜民之術，亦惟若乎人道之常。信乎和衷之外無餘理，綏猷之外無善教矣！公往保釐，亦惟從事於此焉可也。
噫！康王可謂深得化民之本者與！抑於此而知周室享國之永也。區區殷士，初之以謹始，繼之以和中，亦云厚矣，而其背戾猶故也。雖加殄滅，夫誰爲過？康王之命畢公者，亦惟教之而已，德義之外，刑罰無聞焉。孟子曰：「先王有不忍人之心，斯有不忍人之政矣。」康王之心，即不忍人之心也。故造周業者，文王也；定周業
translation_en:
Would instruction such as this not be called great instruction? Teaching that cannot serve as a model for popular customs is certainly unworthy of being called instruction; instruction that proceeds from personal selfishness likewise cannot constitute a great command [?]. To instruct through the virtue that all people alike possess is to take the Great Way as the basis of impartiality, rather than to parcel out something belonging to oneself. The standards established on this basis can surely be extended throughout the realm and hold true everywhere. To instruct through the righteousness inherent in people is to enlighten them in accordance with their nature, rather than to force upon them something they lack. What is promoted on this basis can surely be tested among the common people and win their universal adherence. Those who lead the world through the Way of the sage emperors may differ in the complexity or simplicity of their institutions, yet the canons by which they establish teaching for posterity cannot be sought outside the enduring human relationships. Those who guide the world through the Kingly Way may differ in what they appropriately retain or change, yet their means of transforming people imperceptibly and securing their well-being likewise accord only with the constant principles of human conduct. Truly, beyond harmonizing people's innermost dispositions there is no further principle, and beyond establishing the Way there is no good teaching! When you, Duke, go forth to pacify and govern, you need only devote yourself to this.
Ah! King Kang may indeed be said to have profoundly grasped the foundation of transforming the people! Here, too, we can understand why the house of Zhou enjoyed its rule for so long. Toward those few former officers of Yin, care was first taken to ensure a proper beginning, followed by efforts to bring their hearts into harmony. This was surely generous treatment, yet their rebellious perversity remained unchanged. Even had they been exterminated, who would have considered it a fault? Yet King Kang's charge to the Duke of Bi concerned only teaching them. Beyond virtue and righteousness, nothing was heard of punishments. Mencius said: “The former kings had hearts that could not bear the suffering of others, and thus had governments that could not bear the suffering of others.” King Kang's heart was just such a heart. Thus, it was King Wen who founded Zhou's enterprise; as for securing Zhou's enterprise …

title: 嘉靖二十八年山西鄉試錄
text:
者武王也衍周業者非康王乎卜年八百卜世
三十其以此夫
詩
大田多稼既種既戒既備乃事以我覃耜
俶載南畝播厥百穀既庭且碩曾孫是
若
吳國詔
同考試官教諭黃　批〔寫盛世氣象如在目前盡洒陳言矣〕
===
同考試官教授錢　批〔氣昌大而辭清婉深於詩者也〕
考試官教諭朱　批〔典麗而有天趣〕
考試官教諭鄭　批〔鏘鏘金石之音〕
農功備而美利豐君上獲有秋之望矣夫治人
者食於人治於人者食人分固各有攸當也周
之農夫服田而孚上之心焉可謂能盡小人之
義者矣想昔大田詩人荅前篇之意若曰君以
農爲心民亦以君之心爲心食農人而進髦士
君既無逸於稼穡之勤矣凡我農人烏可不服
punctuated:
者武王也，衍周業者非康王乎？卜年八百，卜世三十，其以此夫！

詩

大田多稼，既種既戒，既備乃事。以我覃耜，俶載南畝，播厥百穀，既庭且碩，曾孫是若。

吳國詔

同考試官教諭黃　批〔寫盛世氣象如在目前，盡洒陳言矣。〕
同考試官教授錢　批〔氣昌大而辭清婉，深於詩者也。〕
考試官教諭朱　批〔典麗而有天趣。〕
考試官教諭鄭　批〔鏘鏘金石之音。〕

農功備而美利豐，君上獲有秋之望矣。夫治人者食於人，治於人者食人，分固各有攸當也。周之農夫服田而孚上之心焉，可謂能盡小人之義者矣。想昔大田詩人荅前篇之意，若曰：君以農爲心，民亦以君之心爲心。食農人而進髦士，君既無逸於稼穡之勤矣，凡我農人烏可不服
translation_en:
…was King Wu; and was it not King Kang who extended the Zhou achievement? The divination foretold eight hundred years and thirty generations: surely this was the reason!

Book of Odes

“The great fields have abundant crops. Having selected the seed and put things in readiness, we have prepared for the work. With our sharp plowshares we begin work in the southern fields, sowing the hundred grains. They grow straight and tall; the great-grandson approves.”

Wu Guozhao

Associate Examiner Huang, Instructor, comments: 〔He depicts the flourishing age as though it were before our eyes, entirely sweeping away stale expressions.〕
Associate Examiner Qian, Professor, comments: 〔The spirit is expansive and the language lucid and graceful: he has a profound understanding of the Odes.〕
Examiner Zhu, Instructor, comments: 〔Classically elegant, with a natural charm.〕
Examiner Zheng, Instructor, comments: 〔The ringing tones of bronze bells and stone chimes.〕

When agricultural work is fully accomplished and its fine benefits are abundant, the ruler gains the prospect of a good harvest. Those who govern others are fed by others; those governed by others feed others. Each role certainly has its proper duties. The farmers of Zhou worked their fields and fulfilled their ruler’s wishes: they may be said to have discharged fully the obligations of the common people.

I imagine that the poet of “The Great Fields,” responding to the meaning of the preceding ode, was saying: The ruler sets his heart on agriculture, and the people likewise make the ruler’s concerns their own. Feeding the farmers and advancing outstanding men, the ruler has allowed himself no ease in his concern for the toil of sowing and reaping. How, then, could any of us farmers fail to work…

title: 嘉靖二十八年山西鄉試錄
text:
田力穡而驟廼事哉是故百畝之不易恒切終
歲之憂矣況茲一成之廣爲田也大惴惴焉有
三時不能以自已者可不知所務乎五穀之未
熟常懷不給之嘆矣況茲甫田之禾爲稼也多
恐恐然有百日不能以自休者又可不知所力
乎時維冬月百穀告成若可以少逸也尤必先
事而飭厥備焉擇嘉種以自殖利鎡基以待時
凡舉之於今歲之冬以充來歲之用者無有乎
遺慮者矣時維二月土膏方興似可以少緩也
===
又必及時而治廼事焉秉耒耜以戴耕取黃茂
而穀之耕之也勤而種之也時無有乎餘力者
矣由是人力齊矣地利所由盛焉禾易長畝稷
翼翼而黍與與也天時和矣物產所由豐焉自
天降康實堅好而實穎栗也雖未卽薦宗廟而
供粢盛也豐年穰穰明備之禋祀可成取足以
供無有後艱之虞矣君心有不悅者哉亦未卽
辦歲額而充君需也純嘏是錫安侑之昭格有
道用之不竭庶免匱乏之憂矣曾孫有不順者
punctuated:
田力穡而驟廼事哉？是故百畝之不易，恒切終歲之憂矣。況茲一成之廣，爲田也大，惴惴焉有三時不能以自已者，可不知所務乎？五穀之未熟，常懷不給之嘆矣。況茲甫田之禾，爲稼也多，恐恐然有百日不能以自休者，又可不知所力乎？
時維冬月，百穀告成，若可以少逸也，尤必先事而飭厥備焉。擇嘉種以自殖，利鎡基以待時，凡舉之於今歲之冬以充來歲之用者，無有乎遺慮者矣。時維二月，土膏方興，似可以少緩也，又必及時而治廼事焉。秉耒耜以戴耕，取黃茂而穀之，耕之也勤，而種之也時，無有乎餘力者矣。
由是人力齊矣，地利所由盛焉。禾易長畝，稷翼翼而黍與與也。天時和矣，物產所由豐焉。自天降康，實堅好而實穎栗也。雖未卽薦宗廟而供粢盛也，豐年穰穰，明備之禋祀可成，取足以供，無有後艱之虞矣。君心有不悅者哉？亦未卽辦歲額而充君需也，純嘏是錫，安侑之昭格有道，用之不竭，庶免匱乏之憂矣。曾孫有不順者
translation_en:
…work the fields, labor at cultivation, and hasten to your tasks [?]? Thus, the difficulty of tending a hundred mu constantly presses upon them with anxiety for the entire year. How much more so with this expanse of one cheng: the fields are vast, and they remain apprehensive, unable to let up throughout the three farming seasons. Could they fail to know where to direct their efforts? Before the five grains ripen, they constantly lament the prospect of insufficient provisions. How much more so with the grain in these broad fields: the crops are plentiful, and they remain fearful, unable to rest throughout the hundred days. Could they likewise fail to know where to exert themselves?
In the winter months, when all the grains have been harvested, it might seem permissible to take a little ease. Yet they must especially make preparations before the work begins. They select good seed for planting and sharpen their hoes to await the season. In all that they undertake this winter to meet the needs of the coming year, nothing is left out of their reckoning. In the second month, when the soil’s fertility is just stirring, it might seem permissible to relax a little. Yet they must again attend to their tasks at the proper time. They take up their plowing implements to begin plowing [?], and take seed from the yellow, luxuriant grain to sow. They plow diligently and sow at the proper time, sparing none of their strength.
Through this, human effort is fully brought to bear, and the benefits of the soil consequently abound. The grain grows in orderly rows along the long field ridges; the millet stands luxuriant, and the glutinous millet flourishes. The seasons are harmonious, and the produce consequently becomes abundant. Heaven sends down well-being: the kernels are firm and fine, the ears full and substantial. Although the grain has not yet been presented in the ancestral temple as sacrificial offerings, the bountiful year yields abundance, and the fully prepared rites of pure sacrifice can be accomplished [?]. Enough can be drawn upon to supply them, with no fear of subsequent difficulty. How could the ruler’s heart fail to rejoice? Nor has the annual quota yet been made ready to meet the ruler’s needs; yet great blessings are bestowed, and there is a way to secure the manifest arrival of the spirits through rites of repose and assistance [?]. The supplies will not be exhausted by use, and the anxiety of shortage may thus be averted. How could the royal descendant fail to be content…

title: 嘉靖二十八年山西鄉試錄
text:
哉不然墮乃力則為弊農時不亨則君違欲民
將胥戕而君之心有不安其所者矣周之農其
眞治世之民歟抑是詩也見君民之分焉見上
下之交焉見政治之脩焉見太和之盛焉見無
疆之業焉安於職而忠愛以貢其上者分也有
孚惠心而樂以天下者情也民安物阜者政也
人悅而天意得者時也久而不厭與道相安者
勢也勢則不息時則可常政則可通情則不流
分則不褻其周之民乎傳曰見禮知政聞樂知
德則是詩也不但觀農事之成而又知周之所
以盛
===
載見辟王曰求厥章龍旂陽陽和鈴央央
鞗革有鶬休有烈光
張曰庠
同考試官教諭黃　批〔總本平易而士子率爲所窘此作明白純正可以爲式矣〕
同考試官教授錢　批〔說休有烈光良是〕
考試官教諭朱　批〔作者多以求厥章備車服對講〕
punctuated:
哉？不然，墮乃力，則為弊農；時不亨，則君違欲。民將胥戕，而君之心有不安其所者矣。周之農，其眞治世之民歟！抑是詩也，見君民之分焉，見上下之交焉，見政治之脩焉，見太和之盛焉，見無疆之業焉。安於職而忠愛以貢其上者，分也；有孚惠心而樂以天下者，情也；民安物阜者，政也；人悅而天意得者，時也；久而不厭，與道相安者，勢也。勢則不息，時則可常，政則可通，情則不流，分則不褻。其周之民乎！傳曰：「見禮知政，聞樂知德。」則是詩也，不但觀農事之成，而又知周之所以盛。

載見辟王，曰求厥章。龍旂陽陽，和鈴央央。鞗革有鶬，休有烈光。
張曰庠
同考試官教諭黃，批〔總本平易，而士子率爲所窘。此作明白純正，可以爲式矣。〕
同考試官教授錢，批〔說「休有烈光」良是。〕
考試官教諭朱，批〔作者多以「求厥章」、「備車服」對講〕
translation_en:
…could he fail to be content? Otherwise, if you slacken your efforts, you become negligent farmers; if the seasons fail to prosper, the ruler’s wishes go unfulfilled. The people will then harm one another, and the ruler’s heart will find no peace in his position. Were not Zhou’s farmers truly the people of a well-governed age! Moreover, this ode reveals the respective stations of ruler and people, the intercourse between those above and those below, the cultivation of government, the fullness of supreme harmony, and an enduring enterprise without limit. Being content in their duties and offering tribute to their superiors with loyalty and affection expresses their proper station. Having a sincere and benevolent heart and sharing joy with all under Heaven expresses their feelings. Peace among the people and abundance of goods express good government. Human satisfaction and the fulfillment of Heaven’s intent express a favorable age. Enduring without weariness and resting at ease with the Way express an abiding tendency. Such a tendency does not cease; such an age can endure; such government can operate freely; such feelings do not run to excess; such distinctions of station are not treated irreverently. Surely this describes the people of Zhou! The Commentary says: “By observing ritual, one knows government; by hearing music, one knows virtue.” Thus, in this ode we see not only the successful completion of agricultural work, but also why Zhou flourished.

They come to audience with their sovereign king, seeking his established rules. Dragon banners fly brightly; carriage bells ring in harmony. The leather reins have gleaming metal fittings: splendid indeed is their brilliant radiance.
Zhang Yuexiang.
Associate Examiner Huang, Instructor, comments: 〔The topic [?] is straightforward, yet candidates generally find themselves stymied by it. This composition is clear, pure, and correct, and may serve as a model.〕
Associate Examiner Qian, Professor, comments: 〔The explanation of “splendid indeed is their brilliant radiance” is very sound.〕
Examiner Zhu, Instructor, comments: 〔Writers commonly discuss “seeking his established rules” and “providing the full array of carriages and robes” as paired themes …〕

title: 嘉靖二十八年山西鄉試錄
text:
殊非詩意此作得之
考試官教諭鄭　批　〔不費斧鑿意思完足蓋讀詩而有得者〕
詩人叙諸侯修覲君之禮備儀衛之盛蓋儀衛
不盛非所以覲君也諸侯來朝稟法有如此其
忠敬不可見乎此諸侯助祭於武王廟之詩也
蓋謂以時奉祭者君人孝享之誠修職助祭者
臣子敬君之義令也清廟載啓羣后畢集但見
公侯伯子男列爵有崇卑也皆竭其朝宗之誠
===
而儼一人於利見甸侯綏要荒分封有遠近也
皆傾夫就日之念而望五位以致恭亦曰典章
法度規畫於宸衷者所當求也于是來咨來茹
以探夫微意之所在庶所行之不昧焉禮法政
令裁决於睿見者所當稟也于是載謀載惟務
得乎旨趣之攸存庶所施之不戾焉斯時也其
儀衛果何如哉是故車上所建有旂也畫以交
龍而屈伸以尚其象飛揚飄緲耀日月而爭光
旌軾之載有飾也繫以和鈴而央央以昭其聲
punctuated:
殊非詩意，此作得之。
考試官教諭鄭批〔不費斧鑿，意思完足，蓋讀詩而有得者。〕
詩人叙諸侯修覲君之禮，備儀衛之盛。蓋儀衛不盛，非所以覲君也。諸侯來朝稟法有如此，其忠敬不可見乎？此諸侯助祭於武王廟之詩也。蓋謂以時奉祭者，君人孝享之誠；修職助祭者，臣子敬君之義。令也，清廟載啓，羣后畢集。但見公侯伯子男，列爵有崇卑也，皆竭其朝宗之誠，而儼一人於利見；甸侯綏要荒，分封有遠近也，皆傾夫就日之念，而望五位以致恭。亦曰典章法度，規畫於宸衷者，所當求也。于是來咨來茹，以探夫微意之所在，庶所行之不昧焉。禮法政令，裁决於睿見者，所當稟也。于是載謀載惟，務得乎旨趣之攸存，庶所施之不戾焉。斯時也，其儀衛果何如哉？是故車上所建有旂也，畫以交龍，而屈伸以尚其象；飛揚飄緲，耀日月而爭光。旌軾之載有飾也，繫以和鈴，而央央以昭其聲。
translation_en:
…is quite contrary to the poem’s meaning; this composition captures it.
Examiner Zheng, an Instructor, comments: 〔Without labored embellishment, its meaning is fully expressed. The author has evidently gained insight from reading the Odes.〕
The poet describes the regional lords performing the rites of audience with their ruler and displaying the full magnificence of their ceremonial escort. Without such magnificence, their escort would be unfit for an audience with the ruler. When the regional lords come to court to receive his ordinances in this fashion, is their loyalty and reverence not evident? This is a poem about the regional lords assisting at sacrifices in King Wu’s temple. It means that offering sacrifices at the proper seasons expresses a ruler’s sincere filial devotion, while fulfilling their duties by assisting at sacrifices fulfills his subjects’ obligation to revere their ruler. Now [?], the pure ancestral temple is opened, and all the lords assemble. One sees dukes, marquises, earls, viscounts, and barons: although their ranks differ in dignity, all devote their utmost sincerity to attending court and reverently approach the sovereign in an auspicious audience. Their fiefs lie at varying distances, in the dian, hou, sui, yao, and huang zones; yet all pour out their longing to approach the sun—the sovereign—and look toward the five positions [?] to render homage. They also say that the institutions and laws devised in the sovereign’s mind are what they must seek. Thus they come to consult and deliberate, probing where his subtle intentions lie, so that their conduct may not be unenlightened. The ritual rules and governmental commands determined by his sagacious judgment are what they must receive. Thus they take counsel and reflect, striving to grasp the purport of his intentions, so that their actions may not run counter to them. At this moment, what indeed is their ceremonial escort like? There are banners erected upon their carriages, painted with intertwined dragons whose bending and stretching give prominence to their forms. Flying and fluttering aloft, they gleam against the sun and moon, vying with them in brilliance. There are ornaments borne upon the banners and carriage crossbars [?], hung with he and ling bells, whose harmonious ringing makes their sound manifest…

title: 嘉靖二十八年山西鄉試錄
text:
駜駓動溢協隆韋而有鷸錦繡輝煌雜沓於公
門之外而瞻者敬畏所謂邦家之光在是矣金
革響應震驚於道路之間而聞者稱嗟所謂殿
天子之邦是已豈不休有烈光矣乎是則諸侯
一念忠赤之忱已著於來朝稟法之日則夫率
之以祭先也寧無感格之休歟抑論雍之詩祭
文王也則曰相維辟公天子穆穆載見之詩祭
武王也則曰率見昭考以孝以享蓋合萬國之
歡心以事其先王此所以爲尊祖敬宗之至冠
===
百王而獨盛也奈何至於後世菀柳興尚息之
嘆齊桓勤包茅之問匪風曰誰將西歸懷之好
音其有以夫
春秋
秋七月庚午宋公齊侯衛侯盟于瓦屋〔隱〕
公八年
武道脩
考試官教諭朱　批〔本傳意成章得謹嚴體〕
考試官教諭鄭　批〔旨明詞從〕
punctuated:
駜駓動溢，協隆韋而有鷸，錦繡輝煌，雜沓於公門之外，而瞻者敬畏，所謂邦家之光在是矣。金革響應，震驚於道路之間，而聞者稱嗟，所謂殿天子之邦是已，豈不休有烈光矣乎？是則諸侯一念忠赤之忱，已著於來朝稟法之日，則夫率之以祭先也，寧無感格之休歟？抑論《雍》之詩，祭文王也，則曰：「相維辟公，天子穆穆。」《載見》之詩，祭武王也，則曰：「率見昭考，以孝以享。」蓋合萬國之歡心，以事其先王，此所以爲尊祖敬宗之至，冠百王而獨盛也。奈何至於後世，《菀柳》興尚息之嘆，齊桓勤包茅之問，《匪風》曰：「誰將西歸？懷之好音。」其有以夫！
春秋
秋七月庚午，宋公、齊侯、衛侯盟于瓦屋。〔隱〕公八年。
武道脩
考試官教諭朱，批〔本傳意成章，得謹嚴體。〕
考試官教諭鄭，批〔旨明詞從。〕
translation_en:
…The horses move vigorously [?], in harmony with “long wei” and with kingfisher feathers [?]. Brilliant brocades crowd together outside the ducal gate, and those who behold them feel reverent awe: here indeed is what is called “the glory of the realm.” Bells and drums answer one another, resounding startlingly along the roads, and those who hear them exclaim in admiration: this is what is meant by “securing the Son of Heaven’s realm.” Is this not splendid, possessed of radiant glory? Thus the feudal lords’ wholehearted sincerity and loyalty have already become manifest on the day they come to court to receive the prescribed rules. When they are then led to sacrifice to the ancestors, could there fail to be the blessing of moving the spirits to respond?
Moreover, the ode “Yong” concerns sacrifice to King Wen and says: “Assisting are the feudal lords; the Son of Heaven is solemn and reverent.” The ode “Zai Jian” concerns sacrifice to King Wu and says: “Led to appear before the illustrious deceased father, with filial devotion they present offerings.” By uniting the joyful allegiance of the myriad states in service to his former kings, he brought honoring ancestors and revering the ancestral line to its utmost fulfillment, surpassing all other kings in singular magnificence. How was it that, in later ages, “Wan Liu” gave rise to the lament about finding rest, and Duke Huan of Qi pressed his inquiry about the bundled thatching grass owed as tribute? “Fei Feng” says: “Who will go west? I would greet him with glad tidings.” Surely there was reason for this!
Spring and Autumn Annals
“In autumn, in the seventh month, on the gengwu day, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Qi, and the Marquis of Wei made a covenant at Wawu.” Eighth year of Duke 〔Yin〕.
Wu Daoxiu.
Examiner Zhu, an Instructor, comments: 〔The composition develops the meaning of the commentary and achieves a careful, disciplined style.〕
Examiner Zheng, an Instructor, comments: 〔The purport is clear, and the wording follows it aptly.〕

title: 嘉靖二十八年山西鄉試錄
text:
諸侯參盟而春秋謹之將以志大道之公也夫
大道之世無盟也瓦屋之盟亂斯啓矣春秋書
日以謹之其作事而謀始乎且瓦屋何盟也宋
鄭交惡東門積憾齊僖爲鄭平以求宋宋衛納
齊交以絶鄭于是兩黨合而瓦屋之盟參焉然
則何以乎君子曰繳信之爭盛于天下爲公之世
誓誥之作起于大道既隱之餘况盟誓雖設於
周官亦聖人不得已之事况乎衰世固非以有盟爲足貴
也何三國於此不能釋義以爲脩睦之本顧乃
===
尚口以發參黨之端公祀刑政首肇傾危何爲
也哉其在宋衛必曰齊侯既來鄭黨孤矣吾何
恤夫用盟曾不思盟所以釋疑心不自諒而言
焉是質疑之招也其何以釋其在齊侯必曰茍
得宋平鄭怨釋矣吾何憚於從盟曾不思盟所
以示信人不自諭而神焉是要信之蠹也其誰
適從噫大道隱而誓誥作已非盛世之事况乎
其特盟也忠信薄而離盟起已爲再降之風况
乎其參盟也卒之風成而弊益滋流遠而禍愈
punctuated: 諸侯參盟而春秋謹之，將以志大道之公也。夫大道之世無盟也，瓦屋之盟，亂斯啓矣。春秋書日以謹之，其作事而謀始乎？且瓦屋何盟也？宋鄭交惡，東門積憾，齊僖爲鄭平以求宋，宋衛納齊交以絶鄭，于是兩黨合而瓦屋之盟參焉。然則何以乎？君子曰：繳信之爭，盛于天下爲公之世？誓誥之作，起于大道既隱之餘。况盟誓雖設於周官，亦聖人不得已之事，况乎衰世，固非以有盟爲足貴也。何三國於此不能釋義以爲脩睦之本，顧乃尚口以發參黨之端？公祀刑政，首肇傾危，何爲也哉？其在宋衛必曰：齊侯既來，鄭黨孤矣，吾何恤夫用盟？曾不思盟所以釋疑，心不自諒而言焉，是質疑之招也，其何以釋？其在齊侯必曰：茍得宋平，鄭怨釋矣，吾何憚於從盟？曾不思盟所以示信，人不自諭而神焉，是要信之蠹也，其誰適從？噫！大道隱而誓誥作，已非盛世之事，况乎其特盟也！忠信薄而離盟起，已爲再降之風，况乎其參盟也！卒之風成而弊益滋，流遠而禍愈
translation_en:
The feudal lords entered into a three-party covenant, and the Spring and Autumn Annals treated it with caution, intending thereby to record the impartiality of the Great Way. In the age of the Great Way there were no covenants; with the covenant at Wawu, disorder began. The Spring and Autumn Annals records the day to convey caution: is this not to consider the beginning when undertaking an affair? What, then, was the covenant at Wawu? Song and Zheng were at odds, with resentment accumulating over the Eastern Gate. Duke Xi of Qi sought an accommodation with Song on Zheng’s behalf, while Song and Wei accepted friendly relations with Qi in order to isolate Zheng. Thus the two parties came together, forming the three-party covenant at Wawu. What, then, are we to make of this? The gentleman says: Could contests over exacting trust [?] have flourished in the age when all under Heaven was held in common? Oaths and proclamations arose only after the Great Way had become obscured. Moreover, although sworn covenants were provided for in the Offices of Zhou, even these were measures to which the sages resorted only out of necessity. How much more so in an age of decline: the mere existence of covenants certainly does not deserve esteem. Why could these three states not expound righteousness [?] as the foundation for cultivating harmony, but instead esteem mere words and initiate a three-party faction? In public sacrifices, punishments, and government [?], they first brought about instability and peril. Why did they do so?

For their part, Song and Wei must have said: Now that the lord of Qi has come over, Zheng’s party is isolated. Why should we worry about making a covenant? They never considered that a covenant serves to dispel suspicion. If their hearts are not themselves sincere, yet they make declarations, this invites entrenched suspicion [?]; how could it dispel it? For his part, the lord of Qi must have said: If only peace with Song can be secured, Zheng’s resentment will be resolved. Why should I hesitate to join the covenant? He never considered that a covenant serves to demonstrate trustworthiness. If people do not reach an understanding among themselves but appeal to the spirits, this is a corrosive attempt to exact trust. Whom, then, should anyone follow?

Alas! When the Great Way became obscured and oaths and proclamations arose, this was already no longer the practice of a flourishing age. How much more so with covenants between two states! When loyalty and trustworthiness weakened and separate covenants arose, this already marked a further decline in customary conduct. How much more so with three-party covenants! In the end, as the practice became established, its abuses multiplied; as its influence spread farther, the calamities grew ever …

title: 嘉靖二十八年山西鄉試錄
text:
大口血未乾食言卽至交質以子心且不孚矣
必不作俑于今日也聖人因其防之始潰知其
敝之所終故作春秋而于瓦屋之盟特書庚午
之日以謹之蓋欲華薄從忠以易傾危之俗著
誠去僞以回淳朴之風世道雖衰而期以古道
人心雖私而待以公心將變周制而厚望當時
也豈得已哉夫子嘗曰大道之行丘未之逮也
而有志焉於此益足徵矣抑孔子之在春秋匹
夫而在下位者且生丁末世而瓦屋之事乃所
===
傳聞於此而謹之無乃託之空言而無及乎曰
不然古今之人心一也得於古者法于今失于
前者鑒于後聖人之作春秋非特爲當時慮也
爲後世人心慮也撥亂反正之書雖無及于瓦
屋之諸侯獨不得垂于萬世之人心乎讀是經
者要當識聖人之心
叔孫州仇帥師墮郈　季孫斯仲孫何忌
帥師墮費　十有二月公圍成公至自
圍成〔俱定公十有二年〕
punctuated:
大。口血未乾，食言卽至；交質以子，心且不孚矣。必不作俑于今日也。聖人因其防之始潰，知其敝之所終，故作《春秋》，而于瓦屋之盟特書庚午之日以謹之。蓋欲華薄從忠，以易傾危之俗；著誠去僞，以回淳朴之風。世道雖衰，而期以古道；人心雖私，而待以公心。將變周制而厚望當時也，豈得已哉？夫子嘗曰：「大道之行，丘未之逮也，而有志焉。」於此益足徵矣。抑孔子之在春秋，匹夫而在下位者，且生丁末世，而瓦屋之事乃所傳聞，於此而謹之，無乃託之空言而無及乎？曰：不然。古今之人心一也，得於古者法于今，失于前者鑒于後。聖人之作《春秋》，非特爲當時慮也，爲後世人心慮也。撥亂反正之書，雖無及于瓦屋之諸侯，獨不得垂于萬世之人心乎？讀是經者，要當識聖人之心。

叔孫州仇帥師墮郈。季孫斯、仲孫何忌帥師墮費。十有二月，公圍成。公至自圍成。〔俱定公十有二年〕
translation_en:
…greater. Before the covenant blood on their lips had dried, they were already breaking their word; even when they exchanged their sons as hostages, their hearts lacked mutual trust. Surely such a precedent ought not to be set today. From the first breach of these safeguards, the Sage discerned the ultimate consequences of their failure. Thus, in composing the Spring and Autumn Annals, he expressly recorded the gengwu day of the covenant at Wawu, treating it with particular caution. His purpose was to turn superficiality and insincerity toward loyalty, thereby changing treacherous customs, and to manifest sincerity and eliminate deceit, thereby restoring an honest and simple ethos. Though the ways of the world had declined, he held them to the expectations of the ancient Way; though people’s hearts were selfish, he approached them with an impartial heart. He intended to change the institutions of Zhou and held high hopes for his own age. How could he have done otherwise? The Master once said: “I, Qiu, have not lived to see the Great Way practiced, yet I aspire to it.” Here we find still further confirmation of this.

Yet Confucius, living in the Spring and Autumn period, was a commoner of low station. Moreover, he was born in an age of decline, and the affair at Wawu was something he knew only through transmitted accounts. In treating it with such caution, was he not entrusting his purpose to empty words, too late to have any effect? The answer is: not so. Human hearts are the same in antiquity and today. What was done well in antiquity serves as a model for the present; earlier failures serve as warnings to later generations. In composing the Spring and Autumn Annals, the Sage was concerned not merely for his own age, but for the hearts of people in later generations. Though this book, which dispels disorder and restores proper order, could no longer reach the feudal lords at Wawu, could it not be handed down to influence human hearts for ten thousand generations? Those who read this classic must above all understand the Sage’s heart.

Shusun Zhouqiu led an army to demolish the fortifications of Hou. Jisun Si and Zhongsun Heji led an army to demolish the fortifications of Bi. In the twelfth month, the duke besieged Cheng. The duke returned from the siege of Cheng. 〔All are from the twelfth year of Duke Ding.〕

title: 嘉靖二十八年山西鄉試錄
text:
楊天賜
考試官教諭朱　批〔意在言外事寫目前有一〕〔倡〕
三嘆之音
考試官教諭鄭　批〔作春秋義當如此〕
春秋送紀私邑之順逆有驗聖人爲國之兆者
有見聖人得政之淺者蓋神化之妙其機固甚
速而其有不盡如意者勢爲之也何疑於聖人
哉且郈費者何叔季之強都也封植既久勢將
不可動矣廼今定之中年斯忌悟而送毀焉撤
===
私家之保障壯公室之輿圖人皆謂二子順也
不知所以能感其順者有聖人以爲國也何也
回姦化暴莫大於禮禮以爲國國何有哉當時
孔子之行乎季孫也三月不違家不甲兵之藏
於是乎踰之邑無百雉之城於是乎踰之樹風
聲章物采夫固有不言而信不怒而感者存乎
其間矣况家臣屢叛而叔季方以爲憂迎其機
而感之能無動乎是以聲色不大而植根膠固
之患俄頃而除亦其理之所宜然者也以此行
punctuated:
楊天賜

考試官教諭朱批〔意在言外，事寫目前，有一〕〔倡〕三嘆之音。
考試官教諭鄭批〔作春秋義當如此。〕

春秋送紀私邑之順逆，有驗聖人爲國之兆者，有見聖人得政之淺者。蓋神化之妙，其機固甚速，而其有不盡如意者，勢爲之也。何疑於聖人哉？且郈費者何？叔季之強都也。封植既久，勢將不可動矣。廼今定之中年，斯忌悟而送毀焉。撤私家之保障，壯公室之輿圖，人皆謂二子順也。不知所以能感其順者，有聖人以爲國也。何也？回姦化暴，莫大於禮。禮以爲國，國何有哉？當時孔子之行乎季孫也，三月不違。家不甲兵之藏，於是乎踰之；邑無百雉之城，於是乎踰之。樹風聲，章物采，夫固有不言而信、不怒而感者存乎其間矣。况家臣屢叛，而叔季方以爲憂，迎其機而感之，能無動乎？是以聲色不大，而植根膠固之患俄頃而除，亦其理之所宜然者也。以此行
translation_en:
Yang Tianci

Comment by Examiner Zhu, Instructor: “The meaning lies beyond the words; the events are depicted before our eyes. It has the resonance of one voice leading and three responding.”
Comment by Examiner Zheng, Instructor: “This is how an essay interpreting the Spring and Autumn Annals should be written.”

The Spring and Autumn Annals records [?] the obedience and resistance of privately held towns: some events attest to signs of the sage’s efficacy in governing a state; others show how briefly the sage held political authority. The wondrous workings of his transforming influence were indeed swift. Where things did not entirely accord with his wishes, circumstances were responsible. What grounds are there for doubting the sage?

What, then, were Hou and Fei? They were the fortified towns of the Shusun and Jisun families. Long established and strengthened, they seemed beyond anyone’s power to dislodge. Yet now, in the middle years of Duke Ding’s reign, Si and Ji came to their senses and proceeded [?] to demolish them. They removed the defenses of private families and strengthened the territorial domain of the ducal house. Everyone said that these two men were obedient. They did not understand that what inspired their obedience was the presence of a sage governing the state.

Why was this so? Nothing surpasses ritual propriety in turning back the wicked and transforming the violent. With ritual propriety used to govern a state, what difficulty could there be? At that time, when Confucius’s principles were put into practice by Jisun, there was no departure from them for three months. The rule that a great officer’s household should not maintain stores of armor and weapons was here transgressed [?]; the rule that a town should not possess walls measuring a hundred zhi was here transgressed [?]. He established an exemplary influence and made manifest the forms and adornments of ritual. Within these actions there was assuredly a power to inspire trust without speaking and to move others without anger. Moreover, household retainers had repeatedly rebelled, and the Shusun and Jisun families were then troubled by this. Meeting this opportunity and moving them accordingly, how could he fail to stir them?

Thus, without raising his voice or assuming a stern expression, he removed in an instant a deeply rooted and firmly entrenched danger. This, too, was the natural outcome of the principles at work. By putting this into practice …

title: 嘉靖二十八年山西鄉試錄
text:
諸魯國而準則將使諸侯大夫各謹於禮上下
相安而王政可行豈惟郈費之墮而遽已哉觀
其自言曰朞月而可茲其見諸行事也若成者
何孟氏之私邑也郈費既墮勢若無可爲矣廼
今定往闈之處父横而徒還焉肆貿圖之邪謀
貽莫掉之深慮人皆謂成之强也不知所以莫
制其强者任聖人之未專也何也殄惡除姦莫
先于政政之未得於國何哉當時孔子之仕於
定公也朞月未逺相國之事尚未之攝國政之
===
大尚未之與居無位操無權夫固有力之不早
反之不易者存乎其間矣况少正阻疑而懿子
僞爲不知當其衝而制之夫豈易乎是以兵威
徒褻而發蒙振槁之邑敢爾雄據亦其勢之所
必至者也向使得乎魯政而專則將使朝廷百
官罔敢弗式逺近悅服而境内晏然奚必干戈
之加而後率哉觀其自言曰三年有成諒非姑
爲退託也由是言之聖人之有益于人國也大
矣而益之不大固有任之者而非聖人責也抑
punctuated: 諸魯國而準，則將使諸侯大夫各謹於禮，上下相安，而王政可行，豈惟郈費之墮而遽已哉？觀其自言曰：「朞月而可。」茲其見諸行事也。若成者何？孟氏之私邑也。郈費既墮，勢若無可爲矣。廼今定往闈之，處父横而徒還焉。肆貿圖之邪謀，貽莫掉之深慮，人皆謂成之强也，不知所以莫制其强者，任聖人之未專也。何也？殄惡除姦，莫先于政。政之未得，於國何哉？當時孔子之仕於定公也，朞月未逺，相國之事尚未之攝，國政之大尚未之與，居無位，操無權，夫固有力之不早、反之不易者存乎其間矣。况少正阻疑，而懿子僞爲不知，當其衝而制之，夫豈易乎？是以兵威徒褻，而發蒙振槁之邑敢爾雄據，亦其勢之所必至者也。向使得乎魯政而專，則將使朝廷百官罔敢弗式，逺近悅服，而境内晏然，奚必干戈之加而後率哉？觀其自言曰：「三年有成。」諒非姑爲退託也。由是言之，聖人之有益于人國也大矣，而益之不大，固有任之者，而非聖人責也。抑
translation_en:
…in the state of Lu as a standard, then the feudal lords and grandees would each have been scrupulous in observing ritual propriety. Those above and below would have lived peacefully together, and kingly government could have been implemented. How could the achievement have stopped merely at dismantling the fortifications of Hou and Fei? Consider his own words: “Within a full year, it could be made workable.” Here this was demonstrated in his actions.

What, then, of Cheng? It was the Meng lineage’s private town. Once Hou and Fei had been dismantled, it seemed that Cheng could do nothing to resist. Yet when Duke Ding went to besiege it [?], Chufu defied him, and he returned empty-handed. Chufu freely pursued his wicked scheme of reckless designs [?], leaving grave concern over a power grown too great to control. Everyone attributed this to Cheng’s strength; they did not understand that its strength could not be checked because the sage had not been entrusted with undivided authority. Why? Nothing takes precedence over governmental authority in eradicating evil and removing treachery. Without obtaining that authority, what could he do for the state?

At that time, Confucius had served Duke Ding for little more than a full year. He had not yet assumed the duties of chief minister or participated in the great affairs of state. He held no effective position and wielded no authority. There were indeed circumstances in which force could not readily be brought to bear and the situation could not easily be reversed [?]. Moreover, Shaozheng obstructed matters and sowed doubts, while Yizi pretended to know nothing. How could it have been easy to confront and restrain them? Thus military power was merely brought into contempt, while a town that should have been as easy to overcome as removing a covering or shaking down withered leaves dared to hold its ground defiantly. This, too, was the inevitable outcome of the circumstances.

Had Confucius obtained undivided control of Lu’s government, he would have ensured that none of the court’s officials dared fail to conform to the proper standards. Those near and far would gladly have submitted, and all within the borders would have been at peace. Why would force of arms have been necessary before they obeyed? Consider his own words: “In three years, there would be accomplishments.” Surely this was no mere excuse for withdrawing from responsibility. From this we may say that the benefit a sage brings to a ruler’s state is great indeed. If that benefit is not great, responsibility rests with those who employ him; it is not the sage’s fault. Yet…

title: 嘉靖二十八年山西鄉試錄
text:
尤有說焉魯國三家之強季氏尤甚而孔子得
政之淺在叔季亦然乃爲國之禮能北于尤強
之季叔而不能及于學道之懿子何也蓋南蒯
侯犯方爲叔季子孫憂而孟氏之於公斂則無
所於嫌而方籍以爲用此所以叔季悟而孟不
之改也如以不能服成爲孔子累然則三苗逆
命有崇弗降亦足爲舜禹文王累乎噫孔之不
舜禹文王無足異也而魯不能不納齊樂用孔
不終至使無以成脩德自格之績良可惜也夫
===
禮記
五行之動迭相竭也五行四時十二月還
相爲本也五聲六律十二管還相爲宮
也五味六和十二食還相爲質也五色
六章十二衣還相爲質也
郭志仁
同考試官教授蔡　批〔詞理明潔氣象渾厚〕
考試官教諭朱　批〔純雅之文鋪敘亦整〕
考試官教諭鄭　批〔安妥莊重可謂守禮者也〕
punctuated:
尤有說焉：魯國三家之強，季氏尤甚，而孔子得政之淺，在叔季亦然。乃爲國之禮，能北于尤強之季叔，而不能及于學道之懿子，何也？蓋南蒯、侯犯方爲叔季子孫憂，而孟氏之於公斂，則無所於嫌，而方籍以爲用。此所以叔季悟而孟不之改也。如以不能服成爲孔子累，然則三苗逆命、有崇弗降，亦足爲舜禹文王累乎？噫！孔之不舜禹文王，無足異也，而魯不能不納齊樂，用孔不終，至使無以成脩德自格之績，良可惜也夫！

禮記

五行之動，迭相竭也。五行、四時、十二月，還相爲本也；五聲、六律、十二管，還相爲宮也；五味、六和、十二食，還相爲質也；五色、六章、十二衣，還相爲質也。

郭志仁

同考試官教授蔡　批〔詞理明潔，氣象渾厚。〕
考試官教諭朱　批〔純雅之文，鋪敘亦整。〕
考試官教諭鄭　批〔安妥莊重，可謂守禮者也。〕
translation_en:
…There is a further explanation. Of the three powerful houses in Lu, the Ji house was especially strong; and Confucius’s limited hold on governmental authority applied equally to the Shu and Ji houses. Why, then, could the rites for governing a state prevail over [?] the especially powerful Ji and Shu houses, yet fail to reach Yizi, who had studied the Way? Nank uai [Nankuai] and Hou Fan were then a source of anxiety to the descendants of the Shu and Ji houses, whereas the Meng house harbored no suspicion toward Gonglian and was relying on him for service. This explains why the Shu and Ji houses came to understand, while the Meng house did not change. If the failure to bring Cheng into submission is counted against Confucius, should the Sanmiao’s defiance of commands and Chong’s refusal to submit likewise be counted against Shun, Yu, and King Wen? Alas! That Confucius was not Shun, Yu, or King Wen [?] is nothing to wonder at. But Lu could not refrain from accepting the musicians of Qi and failed to employ Confucius to the end, thus preventing him from accomplishing the work of cultivating virtue and bringing others to submit of their own accord. This is truly lamentable!

Record of Rites

“As the Five Phases move, they successively exhaust one another. The Five Phases, the four seasons, and the twelve months take turns serving as the foundation. The five notes, the six pitch standards, and the twelve pitch pipes take turns serving as the gong, or principal note. The five flavors, the six harmonizations, and the twelve foods take turns serving as the basic substance. The five colors, the six patterns, and the twelve garments take turns serving as the basic substance.”

Guo Zhiren

Associate Examiner Cai, Professor, comments: “The wording and reasoning are clear and clean; the overall manner is ample and substantial.”
Examiner Zhu, Instructor, comments: “A pure and elegant composition, with an orderly exposition as well.”
Examiner Zheng, Instructor, comments: “Assured, composed, and dignified: he may be called one who observes ritual propriety.”

title: 嘉靖二十八年山西鄉試錄
text:
氣之運於天時者無息而達之人事皆同也蓋
天下之物莫非氣之所爲也氣之運於四時者
旣無息矣則其寓於人事也寧有不同乎記禮
運者以爲自夫太極判而爲陰陽於是木火金
水土之五行以具五行播而爲四時於是春夏
秋冬十二月以分五行之動莫不有終也當其
旺者旣進成其功者自退已往竭於見在更迭
而不已也五行四時十二月莫不有始也主令
者托其始效用者繼其後見在本乎方來循環
===
而無端也夫陰陽還動靜之機而天人合俯仰
之妙天下之物孰有外於此五行哉故其感而
爲五聲也有六律十二管之異莫不還相爲宮
如黃鍾首之則林鍾次之太蔟姑洗之類皆然
如此人之樂不可勝用矣滋而爲五味也有六
和十二食之殊莫不還相爲質如春主於酸則
夏主於苦曰辛曰鹹之類皆然如此人之食不
可勝用矣及其形而爲五色也有六章十二衣
焉如青主於春則赤主於夏曰黃曰白之類各
punctuated: 氣之運於天時者無息，而達之人事皆同也。蓋天下之物，莫非氣之所爲也。氣之運於四時者旣無息矣，則其寓於人事也，寧有不同乎？記禮運者以爲：自夫太極判而爲陰陽，於是木火金水土之五行以具；五行播而爲四時，於是春夏秋冬十二月以分。五行之動，莫不有終也。當其旺者旣進，成其功者自退，已往竭於見在，更迭而不已也。五行四時十二月，莫不有始也。主令者托其始，效用者繼其後，見在本乎方來，循環而無端也。夫陰陽還動靜之機，而天人合俯仰之妙，天下之物，孰有外於此五行哉？故其感而爲五聲也，有六律十二管之異，莫不還相爲宮。如黃鍾首之，則林鍾次之，太蔟姑洗之類皆然。如此，人之樂不可勝用矣。滋而爲五味也，有六和十二食之殊，莫不還相爲質。如春主於酸，則夏主於苦，曰辛曰鹹之類皆然。如此，人之食不可勝用矣。及其形而爲五色也，有六章十二衣焉。如青主於春，則赤主於夏，曰黃曰白之類各
translation_en:
The movement of qi through the seasons of Heaven never ceases, and its extension into human affairs follows the same pattern throughout. For nothing in the world is other than a product of qi. Since qi moves unceasingly through the four seasons, how could its presence in human affairs follow a different pattern? The author of “The Conveyance of Rites” held that once the Supreme Ultimate divided into yin and yang, the five phases—wood, fire, metal, water, and earth—were constituted. As the five phases spread out to form the four seasons, spring, summer, autumn, and winter, with their twelve months, became differentiated. The movements of the five phases all have an end. What is flourishing advances; what has accomplished its work naturally withdraws. What has passed exhausts itself in what is present, and the alternation never ceases. The five phases, four seasons, and twelve months all have a beginning. What governs the season establishes its beginning, and what gives effect to it follows thereafter. What is present serves as the basis for what is coming, in a cycle without an endpoint. Yin and yang cycle through the workings of movement and stillness, while Heaven and humanity unite in the subtle workings of bending down and looking up. What thing in the world could lie outside these five phases?
Thus, when their resonances produce the five notes, there are distinctions among the six pitch standards and twelve pitch pipes, yet all take turns serving as the gong, or fundamental note. If Huangzhong comes first, Linzhong follows; the same applies to Taicu, Guxian, and the others. In this way, the musical resources available to people are inexhaustible. When their nourishing activity produces the five flavors, there are distinctions among the six blends and twelve foods, yet all take turns serving as the basis. For example, sour predominates in spring and bitter in summer; the same applies to pungent, salty, and the other flavors. In this way, the foods available to people are inexhaustible. When they take visible form as the five colors, there are the six patterns and twelve garments. For example, blue-green predominates in spring and red in summer, while yellow, white, and the others each…

title: 嘉靖二十八年山西鄉試錄
text:
隨其時而主之服之在人又可得而勝用哉夫
五行流行於庶類以見一本散於萬殊庶類咸
資於五行以見萬殊原於一本可見有天道則
有比人事矣惡可以差殊觀之哉考之易曰天
地設位聖人成能五行之達於人事固天人默
契之理也而其經制之法不有頼於聖人則事
物之理將何所據而舉行哉意天地無言之聖
人而聖人有言之天地也民之有生不可以不
知天尤不可以不知聖
===
仁者天下之表也義者天下之制也〔報者〕
天下之利也
馮舜漁
同考試官教授蔡　批〔認理親切形容宛然〕
考試官教諭朱　批〔理足詞暢〕
考試官教諭鄭　批〔說得三善透徹〕
聖人於所性之三德而表章之所以覺天下也
夫人孰無德而知之者鮮矣聖人於是而表章
之正欲道之明於天下者歟且夫天之生人也
punctuated:
隨其時而主之，服之在人，又可得而勝用哉？夫五行流行於庶類，以見一本散於萬殊；庶類咸資於五行，以見萬殊原於一本。可見有天道則有比人事矣，惡可以差殊觀之哉？考之《易》曰：「天地設位，聖人成能。」五行之達於人事，固天人默契之理也。而其經制之法，不有頼於聖人，則事物之理將何所據而舉行哉？意天地無言之聖人，而聖人有言之天地也。民之有生，不可以不知天，尤不可以不知聖。

仁者，天下之表也；義者，天下之制也；〔報者〕天下之利也。
馮舜漁
同考試官教授蔡批〔認理親切，形容宛然。〕
考試官教諭朱批〔理足詞暢。〕
考試官教諭鄭批〔說得三善透徹。〕

聖人於所性之三德而表章之，所以覺天下也。夫人孰無德，而知之者鮮矣。聖人於是而表章之，正欲道之明於天下者歟？且夫天之生人也，
translation_en:
…each takes precedence in its proper season. Could people ever exhaust their uses in clothing? The Five Phases circulate through the myriad kinds of things, showing how a single root branches into countless manifestations; the myriad kinds all draw upon the Five Phases, showing how countless manifestations originate in a single root. We can thus see that where there is the Way of Heaven, there are corresponding human affairs [?]. How could these be regarded as disparate? Consulting the Book of Changes, we find: “Heaven and Earth establish their positions; the sage brings their capacities to fulfillment.” That the Five Phases extend into human affairs is indeed the principle of the tacit accord between Heaven and humanity. Yet unless the methods of ordering and regulating them depend upon the sage, on what basis could the principles of affairs and things be put into practice? Surely Heaven and Earth are a sage without speech, while the sage is Heaven and Earth endowed with speech. People, in living their lives, must understand Heaven; still more must they understand the sage.

“Benevolence is the exemplar for all under Heaven; righteousness is the standard for all under Heaven; 〔repayment [?]〕 is the benefit of all under Heaven.”
By Feng Shunyu.
Associate Examiner Cai, Professor, comments: 〔“His grasp of principle is intimate and precise; his depiction is vivid.”〕
Examiner Zhu, Instructor, comments: 〔“The reasoning is ample and the language fluent.”〕
Examiner Zheng, Instructor, comments: 〔“He explains the three virtues thoroughly.”〕

The sage brings to light the three virtues inherent in human nature, thereby awakening all under Heaven. Who among human beings lacks virtue? Yet few understand it. Is it not precisely because the sage desires that the Way be made clear to all under Heaven that he thus brings these virtues to light? Now, when Heaven gives birth to human beings…

title: 嘉靖二十八年山西鄉試錄
text:
氣以成形理以成性故人得天地生物之心斯
有仁焉煦煦爲仁者或視之爲一德而並之以
四端恐非體仁道之全者也殊不知是仁也賦
命方初首衆善而倡之啓其鑰也秉彝旣備會
衆善而統之提其綱也仁之體可謂大矣體大
而尊人心視之巍巍然猶之儀則立於上而瞻
望於下者不動而自敬焉仁非天下之表乎得
天地成物之心斯有義焉孑孑爲義者或執適
莫之偏而乖毀合之正恐非得義理之眞者也
===
殊不知是義也事有不一執此以栽戌之截然
其不爽物有不齊據此以割正之確乎其莫移
義之體可謂方矣體方而嚴人心視之凜凜然
猶之法度一於上而範圍於中者不怒而自威
焉義非天下之制乎自夫貴德之風絶於太上
而施報之禮始於三王是報也其原本乎天理
其利達之天下能使交際之間此往彼來有文
以相接肅肅乎其敬也彼感此應有恩以相愛
雍雍乎其和也雖嚴而泰分不至於相離旣和
punctuated: 氣以成形，理以成性，故人得天地生物之心，斯有仁焉。煦煦爲仁者，或視之爲一德，而並之以四端，恐非體仁道之全者也。殊不知是仁也，賦命方初，首衆善而倡之，啓其鑰也；秉彝旣備，會衆善而統之，提其綱也。仁之體可謂大矣！體大而尊，人心視之巍巍然，猶之儀則立於上，而瞻望於下者，不動而自敬焉。仁非天下之表乎？得天地成物之心，斯有義焉。孑孑爲義者，或執適莫之偏，而乖毀合之正，恐非得義理之眞者也。殊不知是義也，事有不一，執此以栽戌之，截然其不爽；物有不齊，據此以割正之，確乎其莫移。義之體可謂方矣！體方而嚴，人心視之凜凜然，猶之法度一於上，而範圍於中者，不怒而自威焉。義非天下之制乎？自夫貴德之風絶於太上，而施報之禮始於三王，是報也，其原本乎天理，其利達之天下。能使交際之間，此往彼來，有文以相接，肅肅乎其敬也；彼感此應，有恩以相愛，雍雍乎其和也。雖嚴而泰，分不至於相離；旣和
translation_en:
…vital energy gives them form, and principle gives them their nature. Thus, when people receive Heaven and Earth’s life-generating heart, they possess benevolence. Those who practice benevolence as mere kindly solicitude may regard it as a single virtue and rank it alongside the four beginnings; they probably do not embody the Way of benevolence in its entirety. They fail to understand that, at the very beginning of the endowment of life, benevolence leads all forms of goodness and calls them forth, turning the key that opens them; once the constant moral endowment is complete, it gathers all forms of goodness and unifies them, taking hold of their governing thread. The substance of benevolence may indeed be called great! Great and exalted in substance, it appears lofty to the human heart. It is like a standard established above: those gazing up from below spontaneously feel reverence, though it makes no movement. Is benevolence not the exemplar for all under Heaven?

When people receive Heaven and Earth’s heart that brings things to completion, they possess righteousness. Those who practice righteousness with rigid exclusiveness may cling to partiality in favoring or rejecting, departing from what is proper in rejection and association [?]; they probably do not grasp the true principle of righteousness. They fail to understand that, diverse as affairs may be, one holds to righteousness to adjudicate them [?], making clear distinctions without error; unequal as things may be, one relies on it to discriminate and rectify them, remaining firm and unshakable. The substance of righteousness may indeed be called square! Square and stern in substance, it inspires awe in the human heart. It is like laws and standards unified above, with people encompassed within their bounds: without anger, it naturally commands awe. Is righteousness not the regulating standard for all under Heaven?

After the custom of esteeming virtue came to an end with highest antiquity, the rites of giving and reciprocating began with the Three Kings. Such reciprocation has its source in Heaven’s principle, and its benefits extend to all under Heaven. It enables people in their dealings with one another to give and receive, meeting through forms of courtesy—how solemn their respect! One moves the other, and the other responds; kindness enables them to cherish one another—how gracious their harmony! Although strict, their relations remain at ease, so distinctions of station do not lead to estrangement; being harmonious…

title: 嘉靖二十八年山西鄉試錄
text:
而節情不至於相褻報也者又非天下之刹乎
吁道體無爲人心有覺聖人惓惓於性分之内
者蓋憫其人心之喪而致斯道之不明也抑論
之仁也義也報也三者各爲其用若不能以相
須也蓋仁者本心之全德義不由之則私無以
酌事理之宜報不由之則私無以平交際之道
端本澄源仁其要矣但私意難克故鮮此仁孔
子曰人莫不飮食也鮮能知味也爲善者當本
於仁躬行者當致其察
===
第貳場
論
學者必識聖賢之體
趙可化
同考試官教諭黄　批〔程子化工巧工狀聖賢之體此〕
則觀其深者
同考試官教授錢　批〔開闢有度而去陳言識道體非〕
隨人說妍媸者此也
考試官教諭朱　批〔程子能知聖賢此篇能知程子〕
punctuated:
而節，情不至於相褻。報也者，又非天下之刹乎？吁！道體無爲，人心有覺。聖人惓惓於性分之内者，蓋憫其人心之喪，而致斯道之不明也。抑論之，仁也、義也、報也，三者各爲其用，若不能以相須也。蓋仁者，本心之全德；義不由之則私，無以酌事理之宜；報不由之則私，無以平交際之道。端本澄源，仁其要矣。但私意難克，故鮮此仁。孔子曰：「人莫不飮食也，鮮能知味也。」爲善者當本於仁，躬行者當致其察。
第貳場
論
學者必識聖賢之體
趙可化
同考試官教諭黄，批〔程子化工巧工狀聖賢之體，此〕則觀其深者。
同考試官教授錢，批〔開闢有度，而去陳言，識道體，非〕隨人說妍媸者，此也。
考試官教諭朱，批〔程子能知聖賢，此篇能知程子。〕
translation_en:
…yet regulated, so that feelings do not lead to undue familiarity. Is reciprocity, then, not also a restraint upon the world [?]?
Ah! The substance of the Way acts without contrivance, while the human mind possesses awareness. The sages’ unremitting concern with what lies within our inherent nature arises from their distress that people lose their original minds, thereby obscuring this Way. To consider the matter further: benevolence, righteousness, and reciprocity each have their own function, seemingly unable to depend upon one another. Yet benevolence is the complete virtue of the original mind. Unless righteousness proceeds from it, righteousness becomes selfish, unable to weigh what is appropriate to the circumstances. Unless reciprocity proceeds from it, reciprocity becomes selfish, unable to bring fairness to human dealings. In setting the root straight and clarifying the source, benevolence is the essential thing. But selfish intentions are difficult to overcome, so this benevolence is rare. Confucius said: “Everyone eats and drinks, but few can discern the flavor.” Those who practice goodness should ground themselves in benevolence; those who put it into practice should exercise their discernment to the utmost.
Second Session
Discourse
“Students Must Recognize the Essential Character of Sages and Worthies”
By Zhao Kehua
Associate Examiner Huang, Instructor, comments: “Master Cheng used the creative work of nature and the work of a skilled artisan to describe the essential character of sages and worthies. This essay examines the depths of that description.”
Associate Examiner Qian, Professor, comments: “Its exposition opens new ground with proper measure and avoids stale expressions. Here is someone who understands the substance of the Way, who does not merely follow others in pronouncing things beautiful or ugly.”
Examiner Zhu, Instructor, comments: “Master Cheng understood the sages and worthies; this essay understands Master Cheng.”

title: 嘉靖二十八年山西鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭鄭　批
無踰此矣
〔辨理之論最易鋪〕〔張化腐爲奇〕
君子之於道也察其分之所以異而不可不要
其歸之同夫天下之道出於一無容於異也以
爲有二焉者是有見於支流餘裔而不以原焉
非立本之學也然道本不異於人而人不能不
異於道非道之弊也則亦性生之判淺深之殊
誠明之幾天人之所由分也夫何病於道哉是
故君子察其分之異而要其歸之同不以其異
===
也而阻於分之所不能不以其同也而安於力
之所未到則賢可幾而聖可入矣非天下之至
精其孰能與於斯學者必識聖賢之體子程子
之言其眞知道者哉今夫道也者原於天會於
聖幾於賢泯泯焉無得者則亦庸衆焉耳學者
苟無志於聖賢之道則亦已矣如有志焉烏可
以庸衆自諉乎是故探其原則性同焉察其分
則造異焉會其歸則學極焉以立本者存乎性
以辨異者存乎學以達聖者存乎志志立而聖
punctuated:
考試官教諭鄭，批：無踰此矣。〔辨理之論最易鋪〕〔張化腐爲奇〕

君子之於道也，察其分之所以異，而不可不要其歸之同。夫天下之道出於一，無容於異也。以爲有二焉者，是有見於支流餘裔，而不以原焉，非立本之學也。然道本不異於人，而人不能不異於道，非道之弊也，則亦性生之判、淺深之殊，誠明之幾，天人之所由分也。夫何病於道哉？是故君子察其分之異，而要其歸之同，不以其異也而阻於分之所不能，不以其同也而安於力之所未到，則賢可幾而聖可入矣。非天下之至精，其孰能與於斯？「學者必識聖賢之體」，子程子之言，其眞知道者哉！今夫道也者，原於天，會於聖，幾於賢，泯泯焉無得者，則亦庸衆焉耳。學者苟無志於聖賢之道，則亦已矣；如有志焉，烏可以庸衆自諉乎？是故探其原，則性同焉；察其分，則造異焉；會其歸，則學極焉。以立本者存乎性，以辨異者存乎學，以達聖者存乎志。志立而聖
translation_en:
Examiner Zheng, Instructor, comments: Nothing surpasses this. 〔Discourses distinguishing principles most readily lapse into expansive〕〔elaboration; this transforms the stale into the remarkable.〕

In his approach to the Way, the gentleman examines why its distinct manifestations differ, yet must also grasp the unity toward which they converge. The Way throughout the world issues from a single source and admits no divergence. Those who suppose that there are two Ways see only its tributaries and offshoots, without tracing them to their source; theirs is not learning that establishes a foundation. Yet although the Way is fundamentally no different from what is in human beings, human beings cannot but diverge from the Way. This is no defect in the Way. Rather, it concerns the distinction between nature and birth-endowment [?], differences of depth and shallowness, and the subtle workings of sincerity and understanding through which Heaven and humanity are distinguished. What fault, then, can be found with the Way?

Thus the gentleman examines the differences among its distinct manifestations while grasping the unity toward which they converge. He does not let their differences leave him thwarted by the limitations of his endowment, nor does their sameness make him content when his efforts have yet to reach their goal. Then worthiness can be approached and sagehood entered. Without the utmost discernment in the world, who could participate in this? “Learners must recognize the essential character of sages and worthies”: in saying this, Master Cheng truly understood the Way!

Now the Way originates in Heaven, finds its full convergence in sages, and is approached by worthies. Those who remain benighted and attain nothing are merely the ordinary multitude. If learners have no aspiration toward the Way of sages and worthies, there is nothing more to say. But if they do aspire to it, how can they excuse themselves as merely ordinary people? Thus, when we investigate its source, human nature is the same; when we examine its distinctions, attainment differs; when we comprehend its ultimate convergence, learning reaches its culmination. Establishing the foundation rests upon human nature; discerning differences rests upon learning; attaining sagehood rests upon aspiration. Once aspiration is established, sagehood…

title: 嘉靖二十八年山西鄉試錄
text:
可幾矣性盡而道可極矣學辨而體可識矣識
其體則其分不能以無異要其歸則其會不容
以無同道有本原學有優劣歸有止宿焉學者
可不知所力哉道之原也匪特聖人會其全賢
者亦勿喪耳冉求之藝子由之果子貢之才智
雖聖人亦所深許焉匪不可以若是班也然
久大之業終不可以擬神化之全事功之巧有
難以及造化之妙矣謂之與聖人之道則可謂
之爲聖人之聖則不可要之達不可以爲藝猶
===
之藝不可以爲果也其下孔子也亦遠矣孔子
者聖也之三子者賢也原其道未始不同別其
分未始不異譬諸天焉四時五行迭相運也日
月星辰代晦明也萬物隱顯互生植也形色昭
其能有無妙其迹道化彰其用焉耳矣三子者
四時之一氣五行之一用日月星辰萬物隱顯
肖像之一二彷彿之末逺耳人矣而非天也迹
矣而非化也賢矣而非聖也孔子其天乎三子
亦人道而已矣此聖賢之體所以不同學者所
punctuated: 可幾矣，性盡而道可極矣，學辨而體可識矣。識其體，則其分不能以無異；要其歸，則其會不容以無同。道有本原，學有優劣，歸有止宿焉，學者可不知所力哉？道之原也，匪特聖人會其全，賢者亦勿喪耳。冉求之藝，子由之果，子貢之才智，雖聖人亦所深許焉，匪不可以若是班也。然久大之業，終不可以擬神化之全；事功之巧，有難以及造化之妙矣。謂之與聖人之道則可，謂之爲聖人之聖則不可。要之，達不可以爲藝，猶之藝不可以爲果也。其下孔子也，亦遠矣。孔子者，聖也；之三子者，賢也。原其道，未始不同；別其分，未始不異。譬諸天焉，四時五行迭相運也，日月星辰代晦明也，萬物隱顯互生植也。形色昭其能，有無妙其迹，道化彰其用焉耳矣。三子者，四時之一氣，五行之一用，日月星辰萬物隱顯肖像之一二，彷彿之末逺耳。人矣，而非天也；迹矣，而非化也；賢矣，而非聖也。孔子其天乎？三子亦人道而已矣。此聖賢之體所以不同，學者所
translation_en: …sagehood can be approached; when one fully realizes one’s nature, the Way can be attained to its utmost; when distinctions in learning are discerned, the essential character of sages and worthies can be understood. Once their essential character is understood, their respective stations cannot be without differences; when their ultimate destination is considered, their convergence cannot be without common ground. The Way has its fundamental source, learning has higher and lower attainments, and the destination has its final resting place. Can learners fail to know where to direct their efforts? As for the source of the Way, it is not only that sages comprehend it in its entirety: worthies, too, do not lose it. Ran Qiu’s accomplishments, Ziyou’s resoluteness [?], and Zigong’s talent and intelligence were all deeply commended even by the Sage. It is not that they cannot be ranked in this way [?]. Yet achievements of enduring greatness ultimately cannot match the completeness of spiritual transformation; skill in practical accomplishments can scarcely attain the subtlety of nature’s creative transformations. One may say that they participate in the Sage’s Way, but not that they possess the sageliness of the Sage. In essence, discernment cannot be equated with accomplishment, just as accomplishment cannot be equated with resoluteness. They fall far below Confucius. Confucius was a sage; these three masters were worthies. Tracing their Way to its source, it was never different; distinguishing their respective stations, they were never the same. Consider Heaven as an analogy: the four seasons and five phases operate in succession; the sun, moon, and stars alternate between darkness and light; the myriad things, hidden or manifest, grow and flourish in turn. Form and color reveal its capacities; being and nonbeing render its traces subtle; the transformations of the Way display its functioning. These three masters represent but one vital influence among the four seasons, one operation among the five phases, one or two likenesses among the sun, moon, stars, and myriad things, hidden or manifest—merely faint and remote resemblances [?]. They are human, not Heaven; traces, not transformation; worthies, not sages. Is Confucius not Heaven itself? The three masters remain within the human Way alone. This is why the essential character of sages and worthies differs, and what learners…

title: 嘉靖二十八年山西鄉試錄
text:
宜明辨也故曰聖人者化工也賢人者巧工也
化工之妙渾於無跡巧工之能肖而未大雖然
巧工不足擬矣不有天下之拙工乎昏於道而
無得觀其象而未肖其去賢人也亦遠矣三子
不皆聖人若矣天下能如三子者幾何人哉學
者誠能要其原則性未始不一也會其歸則學
未始不可至也是故于其原見性之始焉于其
歸見道之終焉合始終於一致會聖賢於同歸
則人可天明可誠跡可神賢可聖而化工巧工
===
之妙有不足言矣此聖賢之體學者不可不識
程子所以分聖賢之體之意學者又不可不知
也歟抑又論之會道之極本於聖希聖之功由
於賢孔子吾不得而見矣得見三子斯可矣若
然則賢人固不可輕擬聖人亦可易知耶以孔
子之大而見詆於武叔以公孫丑之徒而以既
聖歸軻氏則當時非惟不知賢而亦不知聖矣
不特丑氏與武叔也子游子夏子張皆得聖人
之一體及孔子既沒尤以有若似聖人而欲以
punctuated:
宜明辨也。故曰：「聖人者，化工也；賢人者，巧工也。」化工之妙，渾於無跡；巧工之能，肖而未大。雖然，巧工不足擬矣，不有天下之拙工乎？昏於道而無得，觀其象而未肖，其去賢人也亦遠矣。三子不皆聖人若矣，天下能如三子者幾何人哉？學者誠能要其原，則性未始不一也；會其歸，則學未始不可至也。是故于其原見性之始焉，于其歸見道之終焉。合始終於一致，會聖賢於同歸，則人可天，明可誠，跡可神，賢可聖，而化工巧工之妙有不足言矣。此聖賢之體，學者不可不識；程子所以分聖賢之體之意，學者又不可不知也歟！
抑又論之，會道之極，本於聖；希聖之功，由於賢。孔子吾不得而見矣，得見三子斯可矣。若然，則賢人固不可輕擬，聖人亦可易知耶？以孔子之大，而見詆於武叔；以公孫丑之徒，而以既聖歸軻氏，則當時非惟不知賢，而亦不知聖矣。不特丑氏與武叔也，子游、子夏、子張皆得聖人之一體，及孔子既沒，尤以有若似聖人，而欲以
translation_en:
…is something students ought clearly to distinguish. Thus it is said: “The sage is a craftsman of transformation; the worthy is a skilled craftsman.” The marvel of the craftsman of transformation is an undivided wholeness that leaves no trace; the ability of the skilled craftsman achieves a likeness but falls short of greatness. Even so, although the skilled craftsman cannot be compared with the former, are there not also clumsy craftsmen in the world? Benighted concerning the Way and attaining nothing, they observe its outward form but fail to reproduce its likeness. They are very far indeed from the worthy. The three masters were not all the sage’s equal; yet how many people in the world can match these three? If students can truly grasp their source, they will see that their nature has never been other than one; if they comprehend their ultimate destination, they will see that learning has never been incapable of reaching it. Thus, in their source one sees the beginning of human nature, and in their destination one sees the culmination of the Way. Unite beginning and end in a single coherence, and bring sage and worthy together at their common destination: then the human can become heavenly, understanding can become sincerity, manifest traces can become spiritual efficacy, and the worthy can become a sage. The marvels of the craftsman of transformation and the skilled craftsman would then scarcely need discussing. Students must recognize these constitutive distinctions between sage and worthy; must they not also understand Master Cheng’s intention in distinguishing them?
Let us consider the matter further. Comprehending the utmost reach of the Way is grounded in sagehood; the work of aspiring to sagehood proceeds through worthiness. I cannot meet Confucius; it would suffice to meet the three masters. If so, since even the worthy cannot lightly be judged, can the sage readily be understood? Great as Confucius was, he was disparaged by Wushu; and a man such as Gongsun Chou credited Master Ke—that is, Meng Ke—with already being a sage. Thus people at that time understood neither worthiness nor sagehood. Nor was this confined to Gongsun Chou and Wushu. Ziyou, Zixia, and Zizhang each possessed one constituent part of the sage’s character. After Confucius died, they especially considered You Ruo to resemble the sage and wished to…

title: 嘉靖二十八年山西鄉試錄
text:
所事孔子事之則得聖人之一體而名爲賢者
亦且不知聖賢之體矣況其下者乎則夫遊程
子之門而深慕程子之道如游楊者亦鮮矣此
又程氏子之所慮也噫孔子遠矣游夏諸人不
可復矣然欲察其體之分而會其道之同當自
夫程氏子始
同前
劉有誠
同考試官教諭姜　批〔聖人隨時處中無有方體故爲〕
〔全體賢人不能時中故止爲一體生熟安勉之分全在於此此作得之〕
===
同考試官教諭李　批〔平實可取〕
考試官教諭宋　批〔歸重孔子則賢人之體自明良是〕
考試官教諭鄭　批〔分別聖賢之體最有根據〕
聖賢之體不可以形迹求也求聖賢之體於形
迹之外斯可以識聖賢矣夫聖賢不世出也不
可以見而知千載之下無傳焉又不可以聞而
知然則其體孰爲大而孰爲小孰爲偏而孰爲
全其孰從而辯之雖然此以世之先後論也若
punctuated:
所事孔子事之，則得聖人之一體而名爲賢者，亦且不知聖賢之體矣，況其下者乎？則夫遊程子之門而深慕程子之道如游楊者，亦鮮矣。此又程氏子之所慮也。噫！孔子遠矣，游夏諸人不可復矣。然欲察其體之分而會其道之同，當自夫程氏子始。

同前。
劉有誠。
同考試官教諭姜，批〔聖人隨時處中，無有方體，故爲〕〔全體；賢人不能時中，故止爲一體。生熟安勉之分，全在於此。此作得之。〕
同考試官教諭李，批〔平實可取。〕
考試官教諭宋，批〔歸重孔子，則賢人之體自明，良是。〕
考試官教諭鄭，批〔分別聖賢之體，最有根據。〕

聖賢之體，不可以形迹求也。求聖賢之體於形迹之外，斯可以識聖賢矣。夫聖賢不世出也，不可以見而知；千載之下，無傳焉，又不可以聞而知。然則其體孰爲大而孰爲小，孰爲偏而孰爲全，其孰從而辯之？雖然，此以世之先後論也。若
translation_en:
…serve him as they had served Confucius, then even those who had attained one aspect of the sage’s substance and were called worthies did not understand the substance of sages and worthies. How much less could those beneath them! Thus even men like You and Yang, who studied under Master Cheng and deeply admired his Way, were rare. This, too, was Master Cheng’s concern. Alas! Confucius is far removed from us, and men such as Ziyou and Zixia cannot return. Yet if we wish to discern the distinctions in their substance and comprehend the unity of their Way, we must begin with Master Cheng.

Same topic as above.
Liu Youcheng.
Associate Examiner Jiang, Instructor, comments: 〔The sage accords with the Mean as circumstances change, without any fixed form, and thus embodies〕〔the whole substance. Worthies cannot always accord with the Mean as circumstances require, and therefore embody only one aspect. The distinction between incomplete and mature mastery, between acting with ease and acting through effort, lies entirely here. This essay grasps it.〕
Associate Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: 〔Straightforward and sound; worthy of acceptance.〕
Examiner Song, Instructor, comments: 〔By placing the emphasis on Confucius, the substance of worthies becomes clear of itself. Very true.〕
Examiner Zheng, Instructor, comments: 〔The distinction drawn between the substance of sages and that of worthies is exceptionally well grounded.〕

The substance of sages and worthies cannot be sought in outward forms and traces. Only by seeking their substance beyond outward forms and traces can one understand sages and worthies. Sages and worthies do not appear in every age, so one cannot know them through seeing them. A thousand years later, without transmitted accounts, neither can one know them through hearing of them. How, then, can one distinguish whose substance is great and whose is small, whose is partial and whose is complete? Nevertheless, this is to discuss the matter in terms of earlier and later ages.
