title: 嘉靖二十八年山西鄉試錄
text:
理之在天下則何嘗有古今殊吾能誦其書以
論其世據其迹以考其心因其用以採其體得
其精於形迹語言之外則聖賢之體孰爲大而
孰爲小孰爲偏而孰爲全則固可以心識而神
解矣故邵子曰以一心觀萬心一身觀萬身一
世觀萬世非以其理而何哉先儒有言曰惟聖
人能知聖人吾何人斯而敢妄議聖人乎則請
以古聖人之評聖人者而窺測之可乎孔子以
大哉贊堯君哉贊舜謂韶爲盡善謂武止盡美
===
則雖生知之聖固自有不同矣而况於學知者
乎雖然此主於君道也若主於爲學則又請以
古賢人之評聖賢者而窺測之可乎夫夷尹柳
下惠皆古聖人也孟子謂伯夷爲清伊尹爲任
柳下惠爲和是三聖之體又自有不同矣而况
於賢人乎故由求止長於政事予賜止長於言
語子游子夏則止長於文學孟子謂爲得聖人
之一體冉牛閔子顔淵以德行稱故具體而微
焉蓋誠不可以一律觀也夫三聖數賢孟子嘗
punctuated: 理之在天下，則何嘗有古今殊？吾能誦其書以論其世，據其迹以考其心，因其用以採其體，得其精於形迹語言之外，則聖賢之體孰爲大而孰爲小，孰爲偏而孰爲全，則固可以心識而神解矣。故邵子曰：「以一心觀萬心，一身觀萬身，一世觀萬世。」非以其理而何哉？先儒有言曰：「惟聖人能知聖人。」吾何人斯，而敢妄議聖人乎？則請以古聖人之評聖人者而窺測之，可乎？孔子以「大哉」贊堯，「君哉」贊舜，謂韶爲盡善，謂武止盡美，則雖生知之聖，固自有不同矣，而况於學知者乎？雖然，此主於君道也。若主於爲學，則又請以古賢人之評聖賢者而窺測之，可乎？夫夷、尹、柳下惠，皆古聖人也。孟子謂伯夷爲清，伊尹爲任，柳下惠爲和，是三聖之體又自有不同矣，而况於賢人乎？故由、求止長於政事，予、賜止長於言語，子游、子夏則止長於文學。孟子謂爲得聖人之一體。冉牛、閔子、顔淵以德行稱，故具體而微焉。蓋誠不可以一律觀也。夫三聖數賢，孟子嘗
translation_en: …as for principle as it exists throughout the world, when has it ever differed between antiquity and the present? If we can recite their writings to discuss their times, examine their deeds to investigate their minds, and trace their essential constitution through its manifestations, grasping their essence beyond outward deeds and spoken words, then we can surely recognize in our hearts and intuitively comprehend whose constitution among the sages and worthies was great or small, partial or complete. Thus Master Shao said: “Through one mind, observe the myriad minds; through one person, observe the myriad persons; through one age, observe the myriad ages.” By what could this be done, if not by their shared principle? An earlier Confucian said: “Only a sage can know a sage.” Who am I to venture rash judgments about sages? May I therefore try to discern this through the judgments that ancient sages made about other sages? Confucius praised Yao with “Great indeed!” and Shun with “Truly a ruler!” He called the Shao music perfectly good, but said that the Wu music was only perfectly beautiful. Thus even sages born with knowledge differed from one another; how much more must those who acquire knowledge through study differ! These judgments, however, chiefly concern the Way of rulership. If we turn instead to learning, may I try to discern this through the judgments that ancient worthies made about sages and worthies? Bo Yi, Yi Yin, and Liu Xiahui were all ancient sages. Mengzi characterized Bo Yi by purity, Yi Yin by taking responsibility, and Liu Xiahui by harmony. These three sages thus differed in their essential constitution; how much more must worthies differ! Thus Zhong You and Ran Qiu excelled only in government affairs, Zai Yu and Duanmu Ci only in speech, and Ziyou and Zixia only in literary learning. Mengzi described them as having attained one part of the sage’s constitution. Ran Niu, Minzi, and Yan Yuan were renowned for virtuous conduct, and so possessed the sage’s constitution in its entirety, though on a smaller scale. Truly, they cannot all be viewed by a single standard. As for these three sages and several worthies, Mengzi once…

title: 嘉靖二十八年山西鄉試錄
text:
舍而不欲居乃所願則學孔子然則孔子之體
果有可指而見者乎夫觀乎聖人則見賢人苟
能識孔子之體則其心如持權衡以較物三聖
數賢之輕重可不辯而自知矣吾嘗觀顏子之
學孔子矣仰彌高則其體不可以高盡也鑽彌
堅則其體不可以堅窮也在前在後則其體又
不可以一定拘也然則顏子也果何據而曰卓
爾孟子也果何見而曰願學乎夫觀水有術必
觀其瀾日月有明容光必照焉故觀其用斯識
===
其體矣考其迹斯得其心矣雖然觀其用考其
迹又有道焉夫聖人之體與用合而用未嘗不
分也心與迹合而迹未嘗不判也所以合者理
之同也所以分所以判者時之變也體用心迹
之間有權存故千變萬化而不窮所謂神無方
易無體者是也惟無體故爲聖人之全體惟無
方故爲聖人之大用而非賢人有方體者之可
擬也是故兼清任和而有之而非清任和所能
拘也總四科而條貫之而非四科所能盡也意
punctuated:
舍而不欲居，乃所願則學孔子。然則孔子之體，果有可指而見者乎？夫觀乎聖人，則見賢人。苟能識孔子之體，則其心如持權衡以較物，三聖數賢之輕重，可不辯而自知矣。吾嘗觀顏子之學孔子矣。仰彌高，則其體不可以高盡也；鑽彌堅，則其體不可以堅窮也；在前在後，則其體又不可以一定拘也。然則顏子也，果何據而曰卓爾？孟子也，果何見而曰願學乎？夫觀水有術，必觀其瀾；日月有明，容光必照焉。故觀其用，斯識其體矣；考其迹，斯得其心矣。

雖然，觀其用、考其迹，又有道焉。夫聖人之體與用合，而用未嘗不分也；心與迹合，而迹未嘗不判也。所以合者，理之同也；所以分、所以判者，時之變也。體用心迹之間，有權存，故千變萬化而不窮。所謂神無方、易無體者，是也。惟無體，故爲聖人之全體；惟無方，故爲聖人之大用，而非賢人有方體者之可擬也。是故兼清任和而有之，而非清任和所能拘也；總四科而條貫之，而非四科所能盡也。意
translation_en:
…set them aside, unwilling to rest in their attainments; what he wished instead was to learn from Confucius. Can the essential substance of Confucius, then, actually be pointed out and perceived? By contemplating the sage, one comes to understand the worthies. If one can recognize Confucius’s essential substance, one’s mind is like someone holding a balance to weigh things: the relative weight of the three sages and the several worthies becomes apparent without argument. I have considered how Master Yan learned from Confucius. “The more I look up, the higher he seems”: his substance cannot be fully expressed in terms of height. “The more I bore into it, the harder it becomes”: his substance cannot be fathomed in terms of hardness. “Before me, then behind me”: his substance cannot be confined to any fixed position. On what grounds, then, did Master Yan say that it “stands towering”? What did Mencius perceive when he said that he wished to learn from Confucius? There is a method for observing water: one must observe its waves. The sun and moon possess radiance, and even the smallest opening admitting light is illuminated. Thus, by observing his functioning, one recognizes his substance; by examining the traces of his conduct, one apprehends his mind.

Nevertheless, there is also a way to observe his functioning and examine the traces of his conduct. The sage’s substance is united with his functioning, yet his functioning invariably takes differentiated forms; his mind is united with the traces of his conduct, yet those traces invariably remain distinct. What unites them is the sameness of principle; what differentiates and distinguishes them is the variation of circumstances. Discretionary judgment operates among substance, functioning, mind, and the traces of conduct; hence their transformations are inexhaustible. This is what is meant by “the numinous has no fixed direction, and change has no fixed form.” Precisely because there is no fixed form, there is the sage’s complete substance; precisely because there is no fixed direction, there is the sage’s great functioning. These cannot be equaled by worthies who have fixed directions and forms. Thus he possesses purity, responsibility, and harmony together, yet cannot be confined by any of them. He encompasses the four disciplines and orders them into a coherent whole, yet the four disciplines cannot exhaust him. Conjecture…

title: 嘉靖二十八年山西鄉試錄
text:
必固我之不存仕止久速之當可而渾然無迹
之可見也言人之所言行人之所行不離乎理
而神不可以致思也不離乎事而化不可以助
長也及門之徒親炙其道者由求得之而爲政
事予賜得之而爲言語游與夏得之而爲文學
各有其一體而不可以言全顏淵閔子冉伯牛
仲弓則具其體而不可以言化而聖人之體猶
夫故爲未嘗有加損也不可以一善稱不可以
偏長目不可以始終窮譬如天地之無不持載
===
無不覆幬譬如四時之錯行日月之代明三聖
數賢者譬之覆載照臨中之一物太和元氣中
之一各一其時也然則其體孰爲大而孰爲小孰
爲偏而孰爲全豈不粲可見哉程子取化工巧
工以爲喻豈非以其生熟之不同安勉之或異
所見有偏全故所造有大小體人人殊不可以
强而同乎先儒有言曰孔子無迹顏子微有迹
孟子其迹著皆此意也苟求其理於心而不泥
於形迹言語之末久而貫通焉則孔子之體所
punctuated: 必固我之不存，仕止久速之當可，而渾然無迹之可見也。言人之所言，行人之所行，不離乎理，而神不可以致思也；不離乎事，而化不可以助長也。及門之徒親炙其道者，由、求得之而爲政事，予、賜得之而爲言語，游與夏得之而爲文學，各有其一體，而不可以言全。顏淵、閔子、冉伯牛、仲弓則具其體，而不可以言化。而聖人之體猶夫故，爲未嘗有加損也。不可以一善稱，不可以偏長目，不可以始終窮。譬如天地之無不持載，無不覆幬；譬如四時之錯行，日月之代明。三聖數賢者，譬之覆載照臨中之一物，太和元氣中之一各一其時也。然則其體孰爲大而孰爲小，孰爲偏而孰爲全，豈不粲可見哉？程子取化工、巧工以爲喻，豈非以其生熟之不同，安勉之或異，所見有偏全，故所造有大小，體人人殊，不可以强而同乎？先儒有言曰：「孔子無迹，顏子微有迹，孟子其迹著。」皆此意也。苟求其理於心，而不泥於形迹言語之末，久而貫通焉，則孔子之體所
translation_en: …insistence, rigidity, and self-centeredness are absent; taking office or withdrawing, remaining long or departing quickly, are all fitting, with no discernible traces in the seamless whole. He says what others say and does what others do. He never departs from principle, yet his spiritual efficacy cannot be fathomed by thought; he never departs from affairs, yet his transforming activity cannot be made to grow by forcing it. Among the disciples who personally received his teaching, You and Qiu attained it in government; Yu and Ci attained it in speech; and You and Xia attained it in literary learning. Each possessed one aspect of his integral character, but none could be called complete. Yan Yuan, Master Min, Ran Boniu, and Zhonggong possessed its essential constitution, but could not be said to have reached its transforming perfection. Yet the sage’s integral character remained as before, never increased or diminished. It cannot be characterized by a single excellence, designated by a particular strength, or exhausted by tracing its beginning and end. It is like Heaven and Earth, which sustain and bear everything, shelter and cover everything; like the four seasons proceeding in succession, and the sun and moon taking turns to shine. The three sages and the several worthies are, by comparison, each a single thing among all that is covered and borne, illuminated and shone upon—each a particular manifestation [?] within the primordial vital energy of supreme harmony, each having its own season. Is it not therefore plainly evident whose integral character is great and whose small, whose partial and whose complete? When Master Cheng used the work of natural transformation and that of a skilled artisan as analogies, was it not because of differences between the unpracticed and the fully practiced, and between effortless attainment and strenuous effort? Their understanding is partial or complete, and hence their attainment is lesser or greater; their integral character differs from person to person and cannot forcibly be made the same. An earlier Confucian said: “Kongzi leaves no traces; Master Yan leaves faint traces; Mengzi’s traces are conspicuous.” All this expresses the same idea. If one seeks this principle in one’s own mind and does not become mired in the incidental details of outward conduct and speech, then, after sustained effort, one will comprehend it throughout. title: 嘉靖二十八年山西鄉試錄
text:
謂巧力全而聖智備者不外乎時中而已矣顏
子之卓爾孟子之願學皆此也豈有他哉雖然
談聖賢之體於空言者易求聖賢之體於實踐
者難亞聖如顏子竭力於博約之餘見道於卓
爾之後及其見之於躬行尚有末由也已之嘆
況其下者乎故學必行而後知其難也今不力
於行而惟口耳皮膚之是務言必曰古之人古
之人吾恐聖門之賢得片善以自鳴雖所謂狂
者亦藐乎終身其不可及也況其上者乎故學
者宜學顏子之所學苟學顏子之所學則時中
之言明賢希聖聖希天不難矣
表
擬宋宴貢士於迎春苑謝表〔太平興國三年〕
金商質
考試官教諭朱　批〔命意既高夕秀自發〕
考試官教諭鄭　批〔因題命時而景與意會〕
太平興國三年秋九月日伏蒙
punctuated:
謂巧力全而聖智備者，不外乎時中而已矣。顏子之卓爾，孟子之願學，皆此也，豈有他哉？雖然，談聖賢之體於空言者易，求聖賢之體於實踐者難。亞聖如顏子，竭力於博約之餘，見道於卓爾之後，及其見之於躬行，尚有末由也已之嘆，況其下者乎？故學必行而後知其難也。今不力於行，而惟口耳皮膚之是務，言必曰古之人、古之人，吾恐聖門之賢得片善以自鳴，雖所謂狂者，亦藐乎終身其不可及也，況其上者乎？故學者宜學顏子之所學。苟學顏子之所學，則時中之言明，賢希聖，聖希天，不難矣。

考試官教諭鄭，批〔因題命時，而景與意會。〕
太平興國三年秋九月日，伏蒙
translation_en:
…what is called the full possession of skill and strength, and the completeness of sageliness and wisdom, amounts to nothing beyond attaining the mean appropriate to the time. This is what Yanzi saw standing loftily before him, and what Mengzi wished to learn. Could there be anything else? Nevertheless, discussing the embodied attainment of sages and worthies in empty words is easy; seeking it through actual practice is difficult. Even Yanzi, a sage of the second rank, after exerting himself fully in broad learning and restraint through ritual, and after perceiving the Way standing loftily before him, still sighed, when it came to embodying it in his own conduct, that he had no means of proceeding. How much more must this be true of those below him! Thus, only after putting learning into practice does one know its difficulty. Those today who make no effort in practice, but concern themselves solely with superficial learning passed from mouth to ear, invariably say, “The ancients! The ancients!” I fear that even those worthies of the Sage’s school who proclaimed some partial excellence they had attained—the so-called impetuously aspiring—remain so far above such people that they cannot reach them in an entire lifetime. How much more so those of still higher attainment! Learners should therefore learn what Yanzi learned. If they do so, the meaning of attaining the mean appropriate to the time will become clear; for the worthy to aspire to sagehood, and for the sage to aspire to Heaven, will then not be difficult.

title: 嘉靖二十八年山西鄉試錄
text:
聖恩
賜宴於迎春苑者　等誠懽誠忭稽首頓首
稱
謝伏以秋成萬寶時光協西陸之清春扃
上林淑氣隨東皇之馭白藏敷於八簋青陽
肇於六符
秘苑不入蟄寒
宮花方茂仙杯細浮芳郁籬菊爭開布武
玉墀捫心
===
瑶席翠雲崇靄度鳥曲於箕風碧水涵虛湛
星橋於桂露雲觴飲德撫景搖蒐盻脩徑
之交枝猶存清角依層樓之結樹增麗素
商眷凜慄於高天被
惠慈於
禁地竊惟饗燕親乎賓客周制夂隱歡洽限
乎堂簾漢儀太恪舉緣三物
濬哲右文禮重百朋謙撝下士奈鹿鳴之歌
徒肄鴻磐之漸難逢李唐設貢士之科雖
punctuated:
聖恩賜宴於迎春苑者，等誠懽誠忭，稽首頓首稱謝。伏以秋成萬寶，時光協西陸之清；春扃上林，淑氣隨東皇之馭。白藏敷於八簋，青陽肇於六符。秘苑不入蟄寒，宮花方茂；仙杯細浮芳郁，籬菊爭開。布武玉墀，捫心瑶席。翠雲崇靄，度鳥曲於箕風；碧水涵虛，湛星橋於桂露。雲觴飲德，撫景搖蒐，盻脩徑之交枝，猶存清角；依層樓之結樹，增麗素商。眷凜慄於高天，被惠慈於禁地。
竊惟饗燕親乎賓客，周制夂隱；歡洽限乎堂簾，漢儀太恪。舉緣三物，濬哲右文；禮重百朋，謙撝下士。奈鹿鳴之歌徒肄，鴻磐之漸難逢。李唐設貢士之科，雖
translation_en:
…having received your sacred favor in being granted a banquet at Yingchun Garden, we rejoice and exult, bowing our heads to the ground again and again in thanks. We humbly reflect: autumn brings the myriad precious crops to maturity, and the season accords with the clarity of the western heavens; spring closes its gates upon Shanglin Park [?], and gentle warmth follows the chariot of the Sovereign of the East. Autumn’s bounty fills the eight ritual grain vessels; spring’s vitality begins among the Six Tallies, the celestial emblems. Hibernation’s chill does not enter the secluded imperial garden, where palace flowers are flourishing. Delicate fragrance floats upon the wine in immortal cups, while chrysanthemums beside the fence vie in bloom. We advance along the jade steps and search our hearts at the jeweled banquet mats. Kingfisher-green clouds gather in lofty banks of mist; birdsong travels upon the wind of the Winnowing Basket constellation. Blue waters embrace the empty sky, reflecting a starry bridge amid dew on the cassia trees. From cloud-adorned goblets we drink in your virtue; contemplating the scene, we are stirred [?]. Gazing at branches interlaced along the long paths, we find that the clear jue musical mode still lingers; trees clustered beside storied towers lend added beauty to autumn’s shang mode. We look toward the lofty heavens with awe and trembling, receiving your kindness within the imperial precincts.
We venture to consider that ceremonial feasts and banquets brought hosts close to their guests, yet the institutions of Zhou have long lain obscure [?]; convivial fellowship was confined by the curtains of the hall, for Han ceremonial was overly strict. Selection rested upon the three categories of instruction—virtue, conduct, and practical arts—as profound wisdom honored literary culture. Courtesies were weighty as a hundred strings of cowries, as sovereigns humbly deferred to men of learning. Yet the song “Deer Calling” was merely rehearsed, while the happy stage of “the wild goose advancing to the rock” was seldom encountered. The Li house of Tang established the examination category for tribute scholars, although…

title: 嘉靖二十八年山西鄉試錄
text:
崇俎豆郡縣薦賓興之誼猶遠爐熏化工
有待而啓燬
睿意不嚴而並育
廣筵清酤金石發響於秋聲
靈囿嘉名葵藿紓榮於春色誠
下濟之殊遇而邃古之同遊也茲蓋伏遇
===
秉資文武給九經於鹿洞藝極揚暉復兩稅
全體陰陽
於麟原睦親先務既仁育而義正當小往
而大來謂養民莫要養賢菁莪久潤惇化
尤先惇德梁棟咸收集伊人於一方蒹葭
屆候隨計偕於萬國鵬鷃初翔閶闔
大苑以逕衡膺禮羅而置酒律中無射簪騰
玉斝之茱萸地取寅賓身備紺園之桃李
太昊啓節既鼓動乎羣芳蓐收司藋更陶
鎔乎庶實顧二義之並蓄窺一德之旁流
荆疊長虹暖律吹噓於白帝味分仙掌霞
punctuated:
崇俎豆，郡縣薦賓興之誼猶遠，爐熏化工，有待而啓燬。睿意不嚴而並育，廣筵清酤，金石發響於秋聲；靈囿嘉名，葵藿紓榮於春色。誠下濟之殊遇，而邃古之同遊也。
茲蓋伏遇秉資文武，給九經於鹿洞，藝極揚暉，復兩稅，全體陰陽。於麟原睦親先務，既仁育而義正，當小往而大來。謂養民莫要養賢，菁莪久潤；惇化尤先惇德，梁棟咸收。集伊人於一方，蒹葭屆候；隨計偕於萬國，鵬鷃初翔。閶闔大苑以逕衡，膺禮羅而置酒。律中無射，簪騰玉斝之茱萸；地取寅賓，身備紺園之桃李。太昊啓節，既鼓動乎羣芳；蓐收司藋，更陶鎔乎庶實。顧二義之並蓄，窺一德之旁流。荆疊長虹，暖律吹噓於白帝；味分仙掌，霞
translation_en:
…honored the sacrificial vessels and rites, the prefectures and counties remained far from realizing the ideal of recommending worthy men and raising them up as honored guests. The incense furnace of transforming influence awaited its kindling [?]. Your sagacious intent nurtures all without severity. At the ample banquet, with clear wine, bells and chimestones resound amid the sounds of autumn; in the auspiciously named Numinous Park, sunward-turning mallows unfold their splendor amid spring colors. Truly, this is an extraordinary favor bestowed from above, a shared pleasure such as was known in remote antiquity.
This is because we have reverently encountered you, endowed with both civil and martial accomplishments, supplying the Nine Classics to Ludong, the Deer Grotto. Your attainments shine forth in their utmost brilliance; you remit the two taxes [?] and fully embody yin and yang. At Linyuan, the Qilin Plain, you give precedence to maintaining affection among your kin, nurturing them with benevolence and setting them right with righteousness, at a time when the petty departs and the great arrives. You hold that nothing is more essential to nourishing the people than nourishing the worthy: the luxuriant mugwort of scholarly talent has long received your moisture. In deepening moral transformation, you give foremost place to deepening virtue: all who can serve as pillars and beams are gathered in. You assemble these worthy men in one region when the season of reeds and rushes arrives; accompanying the tribute missions from the myriad lands, the great peng and the little quail alike first take flight. The Gate of Heaven and the great park provide a path and a balance [?]; those gathered into the net of ritual hospitality are entertained with wine. The pitch-pipe accords with Wuyi, the pitch of the ninth month; sprays of dogwood rise upon hatpins beside jade wine cups [?]. The place is chosen for reverently welcoming guests, and we ourselves rank among the peach and plum trees of the violet garden [?]. Taihao, the spirit of spring, opens the season and stirs the many blossoms; Rushou, the spirit of autumn, presides over the di plant [?] and further molds the many fruits. Considering how these two principles are embraced together, we glimpse the far-reaching diffusion of a single virtue. Thorn branches pile up into a long rainbow [?]; the warm musical pitch breathes upon the White Emperor of autumn. Flavors are shared from the immortal's palm, and rosy clouds…

title: 嘉靖二十八年山西鄉試錄
text:
光蕩漾乎蒼龍幸沐昌期抱兢惶而隕落
豈圖寒素承
禮遇之休明伏念臣等枚本雕蟲窮同下葉
爬梳毛羽戰健翮於層霄焚竭膏油咸鳴
聲於冷帳自知緜菲徒負歲華欽
元氣之絪緼受勾萌於殘朽仰
晶陽之觸灼悟貞固於敷榮撫明媚而拳拳
恥作遊空之飛絮處淒清而矯矯不負覆
幷之孤綢
===
臣列羣材報深寸草樞趨
大内休誇張宴於曲江陟降
重闈寧獨珍名於鴈塔敢不俯慶素履上荅
洪鈞習擊鷹鸇雖鳴鸑鳳
河宿奕奕更續學以昭回緣蕚輝輝當培根
而暢達伏願
道融闓闢
治勑時幾誕敷四德之元遠近丕冒盡布天下
之利小大曲成取天籟以和
punctuated:
光蕩漾乎蒼龍，幸沐昌期，抱兢惶而隕落。豈圖寒素，承禮遇之休明！伏念臣等枚本雕蟲，窮同下葉；爬梳毛羽，戰健翮於層霄；焚竭膏油，咸鳴聲於冷帳。自知緜菲，徒負歲華。欽元氣之絪緼，受勾萌於殘朽；仰晶陽之觸灼，悟貞固於敷榮。撫明媚而拳拳，恥作遊空之飛絮；處淒清而矯矯，不負覆幷之孤綢。
臣列羣材，報深寸草；樞趨大内，休誇張宴於曲江；陟降重闈，寧獨珍名於鴈塔？敢不俯慶素履，上荅洪鈞！習擊鷹鸇，雖鳴鸑鳳；河宿奕奕，更續學以昭回；緣蕚輝輝，當培根而暢達。
伏願道融闓闢，治勑時幾，誕敷四德之元，遠近丕冒；盡布天下之利，小大曲成；取天籟以和
translation_en:
…radiance ripples about the Azure Dragon. Fortunate to bathe in this flourishing age, we tremble with apprehension, as though about to fall. How could men of humble station have imagined receiving such splendid and gracious treatment! We, your servants, humbly reflect that our abilities amount only to the petty craft of literary ornament [?], and our straitened circumstances resemble the lowest leaves. Preening our feathers, we pit our vigorous wings against the lofty heavens; burning our lamp oil to exhaustion, we all give voice in our chilly studies. We know our own meagerness and frailty, and that we have merely let the years pass fruitlessly. Reverently receiving the mingling of the primal vital forces, we sprout anew from withered decay; looking up to the brilliant sun’s warming rays, we apprehend steadfast constancy amid burgeoning growth. Encountering fair and radiant days, we remain devoted, ashamed to become willow fluff drifting through the void; dwelling amid chill desolation, we stand resolute, never betraying the shelter bestowed upon us [?].
Your servants stand among the assembled talents; like inch-high grass, we feel profoundly our obligation to repay nurturing kindness. Hastening toward the imperial palace [?], we would not boast of a lavish banquet at Qujiang; passing through the successive examination precincts, would we prize only the inscription of our names on the Wild Goose Pagoda? How could we fail to cherish our accustomed upright conduct below and requite the great cosmic potter above! We practice striking like hawks and falcons, though we cry like phoenixes [?]. The stars of the Celestial River shine resplendently: we must further our learning so that its light spreads all around. The surrounding calyxes gleam [?]: we must nourish the roots so that growth may flourish freely.
We humbly wish that the Way may pervade all opening and unfolding, and that governance may be ordered in timely attention to the incipient workings of affairs; that the originating virtue, foremost of the four virtues, may be abundantly extended, sheltering near and far alike; that benefits may be distributed throughout the realm, bringing great and small alike to fulfillment according to their circumstances; and that the sounds of Heaven may be drawn upon to harmonize…

title: 嘉靖二十八年山西鄉試錄
text:
東宮商自應爲春酒以介
壽
福祿攸同臣等無任感
天荷
聖激切屏營之至謹奉
表稱
謝以
聞
第叁場
===
策
第一問　張四維
同考試官教諭姜　批
〔稽聖人之文如天知之難言之尤難此作莊誦而有悟者〕
同考試官教諭李　批　〔考隆古而知列代且備悉〕
〔是文所以爲文高出義畫墳典其功深學熟者歟〕
考試官教諭朱　批　〔能揄揚〕

punctuated:
東，宮商自應；爲春酒以介壽，福祿攸同。臣等無任感天荷聖、激切屏營之至，謹奉表稱謝以聞。
第叁場
策
第一問　張四維
同考試官教諭姜　批〔稽聖人之文如天，知之難，言之尤難。此作莊誦而有悟者。〕
同考試官教諭李　批〔考隆古而知列代，且備悉。〕〔是文所以爲文，高出義畫墳典，其功深學熟者歟？〕

translation_en:
…the east [?], with the gong and shang notes responding of themselves; to brew spring wine to wish you longevity, with blessings and emoluments shared by all. We, your servants, are overwhelmed with gratitude to Heaven and indebtedness to Your Majesty, profoundly moved and trembling with reverence. We respectfully submit this memorial expressing our thanks for your hearing.
Third Session
Policy Essays
First Question — Zhang Siwei
Comment by Associate Examiner Jiang, Instructor: 〔Upon examining the sage’s writings, one finds them like Heaven: difficult to comprehend and still more difficult to describe. This composition is the work of someone who has gained insight through reverent recitation.〕
Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Instructor: 〔He examines high antiquity and understands the successive dynasties, comprehensively and in detail.〕〔What makes this writing true literature places it far above the diagrams of Yi [?] and the ancient canonical writings. title: 嘉靖二十八年山西鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭鄭　批〔迥異諸作〕
天以精垂象而四時成聖人以道垂訓而
萬世定夫懸象著明天非有意示人以精
也然日月之代明經緯之錯布則天道之
昭明而不可掩者象之著也經世作則聖
人亦非有意示人以道也然範圍而曲成
彌綸而不過則聖道之丕顯而不容息者
文之至也是故天象以運經世而帝道神
聖人以經法天而皇德敷夫惟帝道神也
則天下仰其明而莫測其終始夫惟皇德
敷也則萬世近其光而莫究其淵源故觀
象可以察天之運而不可以窮天之道也
觀文可以探聖之蘊而不可以盡聖之能
也聖人其天乎觀天道則知聖人矣執事
當文教大行之世而以文進士諸士子固
習於章句而未探聖道者矣雖然敢不竭
粉藻之誠以昭明黼黻之萬一乎請備述
前代既往之迹而莊誦
punctuated:
考試官教諭鄭批〔迥異諸作〕

天以精垂象而四時成，聖人以道垂訓而萬世定。夫懸象著明，天非有意示人以精也；然日月之代明，經緯之錯布，則天道之昭明而不可掩者，象之著也。經世作則，聖人亦非有意示人以道也；然範圍而曲成，彌綸而不過，則聖道之丕顯而不容息者，文之至也。是故天象以運，經世而帝道神；聖人以經，法天而皇德敷。夫惟帝道神也，則天下仰其明而莫測其終始；夫惟皇德敷也，則萬世近其光而莫究其淵源。故觀象可以察天之運，而不可以窮天之道也；觀文可以探聖之蘊，而不可以盡聖之能也。聖人其天乎？觀天道則知聖人矣。執事當文教大行之世，而以文進士，諸士子固習於章句而未探聖道者矣。雖然，敢不竭粉藻之誠，以昭明黼黻之萬一乎？請備述前代既往之迹，而莊誦
translation_en:
Comment by Examiner Zheng, Instructor: 〔Entirely different from the other compositions.〕

Heaven displays celestial patterns through its vital essence, and the four seasons come to completion; the sage transmits teachings through the Way, and the myriad ages are settled. In suspending its patterns and making their brilliance manifest, Heaven does not deliberately seek to show people its essence. Yet the alternating light of sun and moon and the interwoven disposition of the celestial warp and weft make the Way of Heaven so luminous that it cannot be concealed: this is the manifestation of its patterns. In ordering the world and establishing standards, the sage likewise does not deliberately seek to show people the Way. Yet he encompasses all things and brings each to fulfillment, embracing and ordering everything without overstepping. Thus the Way of the sage is grandly manifest and cannot cease to operate: this is the highest attainment of cultural expression. Hence Heaven’s patterns, through their movement, order the world, and the Way of the Divine Ruler is wondrous; the sage, through the canonical writings, models himself on Heaven, and august virtue spreads abroad. Precisely because the Way of the Divine Ruler is wondrous, all under Heaven look up to its brilliance, yet none can fathom its beginning or end. Precisely because august virtue spreads abroad, the myriad ages draw near to its radiance, yet none can plumb its profound source. Thus, by observing the celestial patterns, one may discern Heaven’s workings, but cannot exhaust the Way of Heaven; by examining cultural expression, one may explore what the sage holds within, but cannot comprehend the full extent of his powers. Is the sage, then, like Heaven? Observe the Way of Heaven, and you will understand the sage. You, honored examiners, live in an age when cultural instruction flourishes widely, and you advance scholars through their compositions. We candidates are admittedly practiced in textual divisions and phrases, yet have not explored the Way of the sage. Even so, dare we fail to exhaust our sincere efforts at literary embellishment, to illuminate even one ten-thousandth of the splendor of imperial culture? Permit me to recount fully the past achievements of preceding ages and reverently recite …

title: 嘉靖二十八年山西鄉試錄
text:
今日之盛令夫求天地於未有物之先則道寄
無形求天地於旣有物之后則道爲有象
象立而天地之奥不容以自秘形分而性
命之源不容於不判象者理之著也形者
氣之興也文者道之顯也是故至治之世
太和以興河圖出而龍馬不得不呈聖王
有作文明以肇洛書布而神龜不得不錫
聖人者仰則觀象於天俯則觀法於地中
以盡物之情陰陽奇偶之象畫大衍四十
===
有九五十有五之數敘此至理之冲言語
文字之所由興也天且不能自隱而况於
人乎况於聖人乎由是運開中天而堯出
焉德協重華而舜繼焉堯舜之聖固必有
至德以先天下顧其道化之盛適開萬世
之源大畜之極而焕至德之光此允執厥
中惟精惟一所以更相受授而颺言之歌
解愠之詩有不足盡其聖者矣史臣贊之
曰文思安安又曰乃聖乃文堯舜何容心
punctuated: 今日之盛。令夫求天地於未有物之先，則道寄無形；求天地於旣有物之后，則道爲有象。象立而天地之奥不容以自秘，形分而性命之源不容於不判。象者，理之著也；形者，氣之興也；文者，道之顯也。是故至治之世，太和以興，河圖出而龍馬不得不呈；聖王有作，文明以肇，洛書布而神龜不得不錫。聖人者，仰則觀象於天，俯則觀法於地，中以盡物之情。陰陽奇偶之象畫，大衍四十有九、五十有五之數敘，此至理之冲，言語文字之所由興也。天且不能自隱，而况於人乎？况於聖人乎？由是運開中天而堯出焉，德協重華而舜繼焉。堯舜之聖，固必有至德以先天下，顧其道化之盛，適開萬世之源；大畜之極，而焕至德之光。此「允執厥中」、「惟精惟一」所以更相受授，而颺言之歌、解愠之詩，有不足盡其聖者矣。史臣贊之曰：「文思安安。」又曰：「乃聖乃文。」堯舜何容心
translation_en:
…the flourishing age of today. Now [?], if one seeks Heaven and Earth before things existed, the Way resides in the formless; if one seeks Heaven and Earth after things have come into being, the Way possesses images. Once images are established, the mysteries of Heaven and Earth cannot remain concealed; once forms are differentiated, the source of nature and destiny cannot remain undistinguished. Images are principle made manifest; forms are vital energy arising; cultural expression is the Way revealed. Thus, in an age of perfect government, supreme harmony arises: the River Chart appears, and the dragon-horse cannot but present it. When a sage king arises, cultural brilliance begins: the Luo Writing is revealed, and the divine tortoise cannot but bestow it. Looking upward, the sage observes images in Heaven; looking downward, he observes patterns on Earth; between them, he fully comprehends the true conditions of things. The images of yin and yang, odd and even, are drawn, and the numbers of the Great Expansion—forty-nine and fifty-five—are set in order [?]. This is the profound working of ultimate principle, from which speech and writing arise. If even Heaven cannot conceal itself, how much less can human beings? How much less can sages?

Thus, as the movement of destiny opened an age of heavenly ascendancy, Yao appeared; and Shun succeeded him, his virtue according with the renewed brilliance of his predecessor. Sages such as Yao and Shun surely possessed consummate virtue with which to lead all under Heaven. Yet the flourishing of their transformation through the Way opened a source for ten thousand generations; the utmost accumulation of their virtue shone forth in its consummate radiance. This is why they successively transmitted and received the teachings, “Sincerely hold fast to the Mean” and “Be discerning; be single-minded.” Yet the song in which voices were raised and the poem about dispelling resentment could not fully express their sageliness. The court historian praised them, saying, “Cultured and thoughtful, naturally at ease,” and again, “Both sagely and cultured.” How could Yao and Shun have harbored any deliberate intention…

title: 嘉靖二十八年山西鄉試錄
text:
哉由是而夏而周則盤銘自警聖敬之所
以日躋也几杖致戒敬勝怠者所以爲吉
也鳳凰儀而卷阿咏學有緝熙於光明也
追琢修巧雲漢爲章文則顯矣其入聖不
有間乎又由是而下焉則風氣漸漓而時
非三代入文漸下而學有純駁英君義辟
非不可開一代之統而揮張辭翰非不可
以號一時之雄也然猛士歌而羣雄伯之
傳秋風詠而成輪臺之悔登臺自寫遷左
===
無功無逸圖壁何救河朔孔顏贊似知首
務而未正其始籍田賦亦知重本而未正
其終元良有箴矣何補彌文之侈損齋有
記矣何救於國勢之安言不由衷業非經
世謂之銳意於文則可其於道均未有得
也回視三代之君且不可比擬一二況堯
舜乎夫三代以上文本乎道者也三代以
下文事乎末者也伴侶新聲斷烟平蕪則
其叛道亦遠矣何足與議哉詩不云乎維
punctuated:
哉！由是而夏而周，則盤銘自警，聖敬之所以日躋也；几杖致戒，敬勝怠者所以爲吉也；鳳凰儀而卷阿咏，學有緝熙於光明也。追琢修巧，雲漢爲章，文則顯矣，其入聖不有間乎？
又由是而下焉，則風氣漸漓而時非三代，入文漸下而學有純駁。英君義辟，非不可開一代之統；而揮張辭翰，非不可以號一時之雄也。然猛士歌而羣雄伯之傳，秋風詠而成輪臺之悔；登臺自寫，遷左無功；無逸圖壁，何救河朔？孔顏贊似知首務，而未正其始；籍田賦亦知重本，而未正其終。元良有箴矣，何補彌文之侈？損齋有記矣，何救於國勢之安？言不由衷，業非經世，謂之銳意於文則可，其於道均未有得也。回視三代之君，且不可比擬一二，況堯舜乎？
夫三代以上，文本乎道者也；三代以下，文事乎末者也。伴侶新聲，斷烟平蕪，則其叛道亦遠矣，何足與議哉？詩不云乎：「維
translation_en:
…indeed, what deliberate intention could they have had? From there, through Xia and Zhou, the inscription on the basin served as a personal admonition: through it, sagely reverence advanced daily. Admonitions were placed on armrests and staffs: reverence overcoming indolence was what brought good fortune. Phoenixes appeared in stately bearing, and “The Winding Mound” was sung: learning continually advanced toward brightness. Through carving, polishing, and skilful refinement, the Cloudy Han—the Milky Way—formed a celestial pattern. Their cultural accomplishment was manifest; yet was there not still some distance between this and attaining sagehood?
Thereafter, prevailing customs grew progressively diluted, and the age was no longer that of the Three Dynasties. Attainment in letters gradually declined [?], and learning mingled purity with impurity. Brilliant rulers and righteous sovereigns were certainly capable of founding a dynasty’s succession; wielding their literary talents, they could certainly be acclaimed as outstanding figures of their age. Yet the song calling for mighty warriors left an account of supremacy among contending heroes [?], while the singing of “Autumn Wind” culminated in the remorse expressed at Luntai. Ascending a terrace, a ruler expressed himself in writing, yet the move to the left achieved nothing [?]. Having “Against Idleness” depicted on a wall—how could that save Heshuo? A “Eulogy on Confucius and Yan Hui” seemed to show knowledge of the foremost task, yet its author failed to set things right at the beginning. A “Rhapsody on the Imperial Ploughing Field” likewise showed an understanding of the importance of the root, agriculture, yet its author failed to set things right at the end. There was an “Admonition for the Heir Apparent,” but how did it remedy the extravagance of proliferating ornament? There was a “Record of the Studio of Diminution,” but how did it safeguard the security of the state [?]? Their words did not issue from their hearts, and their undertakings did not bring order to the world. One may say that they devoted themselves ardently to literary accomplishment, but none had attained the Way. Looking back to the rulers of the Three Dynasties, they could scarcely compare with them in even one or two respects—how much less with Yao and Shun!
For in the Three Dynasties and earlier, literary accomplishment was rooted in the Way; after the Three Dynasties, it attended to secondary things. With companions and new melodies [?], wisps of mist and level expanses of weeds, its departure from the Way became very great indeed. How could such writing merit discussion alongside theirs? Does the Book of Odes not say, “The…

title: 嘉靖二十八年山西鄉試錄
text:
天之命於穆不已蓋曰天之所以爲天也
而日月星辰之象不與焉於乎不顯文王
之德之純蓋曰文王之所以爲文也而藻
翰辭章之富不與焉知此則我
太祖高皇帝與今
皇上所以經世運而開世務者可識矣粵自皇
風纖渺帝德浸微天厭胡戎之亂我中
夏遠紹自聖誕生肅服而我
聖祖出焉其揮張神武布列皇威功業之迅速
===
萬方之底定固非三代以下諸君所敢輕
議然投戈之暇出其餘續以煥天章如中
原一檄登極一詔多士多方不足擬焉醉
學士歌閱江樓記商盤周誥未足數焉他
如祀郊廟語配享存心省躬諸作則於穆
清廟我將我享之詩有難繼焉蓋炳矣如
天以垂象沛然河漢以中行故當時聖哲
未足窺其閫奥萬世臣民莫得以領其要
會者矣蓋
punctuated: 天之命，於穆不已。」蓋曰天之所以爲天也，而日月星辰之象不與焉。「於乎不顯，文王之德之純！」蓋曰文王之所以爲文也，而藻翰辭章之富不與焉。知此，則我太祖高皇帝與今皇上所以經世運而開世務者可識矣。粵自皇風纖渺，帝德浸微，天厭胡戎之亂我中夏，遠紹自聖，誕生肅服，而我聖祖出焉。其揮張神武，布列皇威，功業之迅速，萬方之底定，固非三代以下諸君所敢輕議。然投戈之暇，出其餘續，以煥天章。如《中原》一檄，《登極》一詔，《多士》《多方》不足擬焉；《醉學士歌》《閱江樓記》，《商盤》《周誥》未足數焉。他如《祀郊廟》《語配享》《存心》《省躬》諸作，則「於穆清廟」「我將我享」之詩有難繼焉。蓋炳矣如天以垂象，沛然河漢以中行。故當時聖哲未足窺其閫奥，萬世臣民莫得以領其要會者矣。蓋
translation_en:
…“Heaven’s mandate—how profound, unceasing!” This speaks of what makes Heaven Heaven; the visible forms of the sun, moon, and stars have no part in it. “Ah, how illustrious is the purity of King Wen’s virtue!” This speaks of what made King Wen truly cultured; abundance of ornate writing and literary composition has no part in it. Understanding this, one can recognize how our Emperor Gao, Taizu, and His present Majesty have ordered the course of the age and inaugurated its undertakings.

When the influence of the ancient sovereigns had grown faint and imperial virtue had gradually declined, Heaven grew weary of the Hu and Rong throwing our central land into disorder. Distantly continuing the sages, born amid reverent submission [?], our sagely ancestor emerged. He displayed divine martial prowess and spread imperial might. The speed of his achievements and his pacification of all regions were certainly beyond what rulers since the Three Dynasties could presume lightly to discuss. Yet in moments of respite from warfare, he brought forth his remaining literary efforts [?] to make his heavenly compositions shine. His proclamation concerning the Central Plain and his edict on ascending the throne surpass even “The Many Officers” and “The Many Regions.” Beside his “Song of the Drunken Academician” and “Record of the River-Viewing Tower,” even the Shang “Pan Geng” and the Zhou announcements scarcely merit mention. Among his other works, those on sacrificing at the suburban altars and ancestral temples, discussing associated sacrificial honors, preserving the mind, and examining oneself surpass what even the poems beginning “Ah, solemn is the pure temple” and “I bring my offerings and present them” can match.

Indeed, his writings shone like Heaven displaying its celestial forms and flowed abundantly like the River of Heaven coursing through the sky. Thus even the sages and wise men of his time could not fully glimpse their innermost depths, and subjects throughout all ages could not grasp their essential meaning. For…

title: 嘉靖二十八年山西鄉試錄
text:
聖祖功超二儀道貫千古心與天同運文與象
並麗天下萬世宜莫得其涯涘夫豈劉基
宋濂郭傳諸臣所可稱擬也哉如可稱也
是以文而已矣文可以盡
聖祖之聖耶
列聖繼統世運方隆天乃錫我
皇上以睿聖莫知之資光大
皇祖純龐之業豐功偉烈至德純仁故其一時
之損益者率皆萬世不刊之規
===
廟堂之所經畫者一惟百王不易之妙禮樂明
備而天地官也孝享時舉而
廟制肅也
天地分祀而體統定也朝日夕月而百神柔也
兩
幸孔庭而敷教寛也數親儒臣而文德洽也
其著之訓者莫不純粹以精而懋日新之
勤立之制者莫不盡善盡美而光富有之
盛著之話言允爲成式浩浩如天蕩蕩難
punctuated:
聖祖功超二儀，道貫千古，心與天同運，文與象並麗，天下萬世宜莫得其涯涘，夫豈劉基、宋濂、郭傳諸臣所可稱擬也哉？如可稱也，是以文而已矣。文可以盡聖祖之聖耶？
列聖繼統，世運方隆，天乃錫我皇上以睿聖莫知之資，光大皇祖純龐之業。豐功偉烈，至德純仁，故其一時之損益者，率皆萬世不刊之規。廟堂之所經畫者，一惟百王不易之妙。禮樂明備而天地官也，孝享時舉而廟制肅也，天地分祀而體統定也，朝日夕月而百神柔也，兩幸孔庭而敷教寛也，數親儒臣而文德洽也。其著之訓者，莫不純粹以精，而懋日新之勤；立之制者，莫不盡善盡美，而光富有之盛。著之話言，允爲成式，浩浩如天，蕩蕩難
translation_en:
…The sagely founder’s achievements surpassed Heaven and Earth; his Way extended throughout the ages. His mind moved in concert with Heaven, and his writings shone alongside the celestial patterns. Surely none in all the world, through all generations, could fathom their bounds. How could such ministers as Liu Ji, Song Lian, and Guo Chuan adequately praise him or compare with him? If they could praise him, it would be through writing alone. Could writing exhaust the sageliness of the sagely founder?
Successive sage emperors inherited the throne, and the fortunes of the age continued to flourish. Heaven then bestowed upon our present emperor unfathomable sagely wisdom, enabling him to magnify his imperial ancestor’s grand and unalloyed enterprise. His abundant achievements and mighty deeds, his consummate virtue and pure benevolence, ensure that the adjustments he makes for his own time are all enduring standards for countless generations. The plans devised at court embody principles so subtle that a hundred kings could never alter them. Rites and music are clearly established and complete, and Heaven and Earth fulfill their offices [?]. Filial offerings are performed at their appointed seasons, and the regulations of the ancestral temples are solemnly observed. Heaven and Earth receive separate sacrifices, and their proper relationship is established. The sun is honored in the morning and the moon in the evening, and the hundred spirits are appeased. Twice the emperor has visited the precincts of Confucius, extending instruction far and wide. He has repeatedly drawn Confucian ministers close to him, spreading the influence of civil virtue everywhere.
The teachings he sets down are without exception pure and refined, encouraging diligent daily renewal. The institutions he establishes are without exception wholly good and wholly beautiful, giving luster to the abundance of his accomplishments. Committed to instructive pronouncements, they truly serve as established models: vast as Heaven, boundless and difficult to…

title: 嘉靖二十八年山西鄉試錄
text:
名如三愛之釋帝王心政之遺烈乎五箴
之註孔顏克復之鑒戒乎敬一之作堯舜
傳心之體要乎上接堯舜之傳中衍湯文
之盛遠繼
太祖景運之隆近紹
列聖無疆之統德盛而化神言近而指遠是豈
漢唐宋諸君之制作所可彷彿其萬一哉
故一時世運之隆而奎纏聚人文之盛而
道化流熙熙無從而贊襄皞皞莫得於名
===
言而菁莪之化樸棫之風蔑以尚矣雖然
天垂象而四時成百物生者何也帝道之
神也聖人垂訓而萬民服萬世仰者何也
皇德之運也德運而不可窮道神而莫能
測此天道之至誠無息而聖人之純德所
以不可已也詩曰勉勉我王綱紀四方又
曰不識不知順帝之則敢敬以是為
今日獻
第二問
punctuated:
名。如《三愛》之釋，帝王心政之遺烈乎？《五箴》之註，孔顏克復之鑒戒乎？《敬一》之作，堯舜傳心之體要乎？上接堯舜之傳，中衍湯文之盛，遠繼太祖景運之隆，近紹列聖無疆之統。德盛而化神，言近而指遠，是豈漢唐宋諸君之制作所可彷彿其萬一哉？故一時世運之隆而奎纏聚，人文之盛而道化流。熙熙無從而贊襄，皞皞莫得於名言，而《菁莪》之化、《樸棫》之風，蔑以尚矣。雖然，天垂象而四時成、百物生者，何也？帝道之神也。聖人垂訓而萬民服、萬世仰者，何也？皇德之運也。德運而不可窮，道神而莫能測，此天道之至誠無息，而聖人之純德所以不可已也。《詩》曰：「勉勉我王，綱紀四方。」又曰：「不識不知，順帝之則。」敢敬以是為今日獻。

第二問
translation_en:
…to name. Is not the exposition of the Three Loves (San ai) a legacy of the ancient emperors’ and kings’ governance of the mind? Is not the commentary on the Five Admonitions (Wu zhen) an instructive mirror of Confucius’s and Yan Hui’s overcoming the self and returning to ritual propriety? Is not the composition Reverent Single-mindedness (Jing yi) the essential substance of the transmission of the mind from Yao to Shun? Your Majesty carries forward the transmission of Yao and Shun from high antiquity and extends the flourishing achievements of Tang and King Wen in the intervening age; more distantly, you continue the grandeur of Taizu’s glorious era, and more immediately, you inherit the boundless succession of the sage emperors. Your virtue is abundant and its transforming influence wondrous; your words are accessible, yet their meaning reaches far. Could the writings and institutions of the rulers of Han, Tang, and Song possibly resemble even one ten-thousandth of this? Thus, amid the flourishing fortunes of this age, auspicious influences gather in the celestial region of Kui, and amid the abundance of cultural accomplishment, the transforming influence of the Way spreads. Such harmony admits of no further assistance, and such expansive contentment cannot be expressed in words. Even the transforming influence celebrated in “Luxuriant Southernwood” (Jing e) and the ethos of “Oak and Thorn” (Pu yu) cannot surpass it.

Yet why is it that Heaven displays its signs, the four seasons complete their courses, and the myriad things come into being? It is the wondrous efficacy of the Supreme Ruler’s Way. Why is it that the sage bequeaths his teachings, the myriad people submit, and ten thousand generations look up to him? It is the working of imperial virtue. Virtue works inexhaustibly, and the Way is wondrous beyond all fathoming. This is the utmost sincerity and ceaselessness of Heaven’s Way, and the reason why the sage’s pure virtue can never cease. The Book of Odes says: “Diligently our king labors, ordering the four quarters.” It also says: “Without conscious knowledge or awareness, he follows the Supreme Ruler’s pattern.” I venture respectfully to offer these words today.

Second Question

title: 嘉靖二十八年山西鄉試錄
text:
郭志仁
同考試官教授蔡　批〔援據古今綽有斷制取之〕
考試官教諭朱　批〔達繁簡之故可謂觀其會通矣〕
考試官教諭鄭　批〔荅述有條而尤知原本〕
立法以官人垂於後而無弊者盡繼天立
極之道者也酌法以任人監於前而無愆
者得通變宜民之神者也蓋因事以建官
則官有尊成之業而天下無曠職因時以
通變則事有專責之職而天下無廢政此
===
三代而上官簡而能治迨乎
今日官多而不擾各有攸當不必以多寡論也
禮曰設官分職以為民極易曰神而化之
使民宜之古今建官之法要不出於此矣
乃若定制之載在典籍
王章之布於中外何莫而非神化宜民者乎
愚生竊伏草茅常有得于見聞而思有以
揚其盛矣請因明問而盡言之粵維隆古
民俗朴野榛榛狉狉相安無事故官不多
punctuated:
郭志仁

同考試官教授蔡　批〔援據古今，綽有斷制，取之。〕
考試官教諭朱　批〔達繁簡之故，可謂觀其會通矣。〕
考試官教諭鄭　批〔荅述有條，而尤知原本。〕

立法以官人，垂於後而無弊者，盡繼天立極之道者也；酌法以任人，監於前而無愆者，得通變宜民之神者也。蓋因事以建官，則官有尊成之業，而天下無曠職；因時以通變，則事有專責之職，而天下無廢政。此三代而上官簡而能治，迨乎今日官多而不擾，各有攸當，不必以多寡論也。禮曰：「設官分職，以為民極。」易曰：「神而化之，使民宜之。」古今建官之法，要不出於此矣。乃若定制之載在典籍，王章之布於中外，何莫而非神化宜民者乎？愚生竊伏草茅，常有得于見聞，而思有以揚其盛矣。請因明問而盡言之。粵維隆古，民俗朴野，榛榛狉狉，相安無事，故官不多
translation_en:
Guo Zhiren

Associate Examiner Cai, Prefectural School Instructor, comments: 〔Drawing on evidence from antiquity and the present, this answer shows ample discernment and judgment. Accept it.〕
Examiner Zhu, County School Instructor, comments: 〔He understands the reasons for complexity and simplicity; one may say that he has discerned how they interconnect.〕
Examiner Zheng, County School Instructor, comments: 〔The answer is orderly in its exposition and, above all, shows an understanding of underlying principles.〕

Those who establish laws for appointing men to office and transmit them to posterity without ill effects fully realize the Way of succeeding Heaven and establishing the supreme standard. Those who weigh the laws when employing men and, taking warning from the past, avoid error grasp the wondrous efficacy of adapting to change for the people's benefit. For when offices are established according to the tasks to be done, each office has its honored work to accomplish [?], and no official duties throughout the realm are neglected. When adjustments are made according to the times, every matter falls within an office specifically responsible for it, and no affairs of government throughout the realm are left unattended. Thus, in the Three Dynasties and earlier, offices were few, yet good government was achieved; down to the present day, offices are numerous, yet cause no disturbance. Each arrangement has its proper circumstances: neither need be judged by numbers alone.

The Book of Rites says: “Establish offices and apportion duties, thereby providing a supreme standard for the people.” The Book of Changes says: “Transform them through wondrous efficacy, enabling the people to find what suits them.” The essential principles for establishing offices, ancient and modern, go no further than this. As for the established institutions recorded in authoritative texts and the royal statutes promulgated at court and throughout the provinces, which of them does not bring about such wondrous transformation for the people's benefit?

I, an unworthy student living obscurely among the common people, have often gained insights from what I have seen and heard, and have wished to give expression to the splendor of these institutions. Permit me to address your illuminating question and state my views fully. In highest antiquity, the people's customs were simple and rustic. Amid luxuriant vegetation and roaming beasts, they lived together peacefully, free from trouble; hence officials were not numerous…

title: 嘉靖二十八年山西鄉試錄
text:
員代無定名伏犧氏以龍紀共工氏以水
紀神農氏以火紀黃帝氏以雲紀皆得於
有所感而命之也顓帝爲民師而命以民
事又置春夏秋冬中五官以掌木火金水
土之五行所以尊奉社稷五祀也然世代
云邈職守莫辨至堯始命羲和欽天授時
分命羲仲宅嵎夷羲叔宅南交和仲宅昧
谷和叔宅朔方允釐百工庶績咸熙虞舜
分爲九官以伯禹作司空棄作后稷契作
===
司徒皐陶作士師垂作共工伯益作虞伯
夷作秩宗夔作典樂龍作納言故考其時
於變之休昭明之化皡皡乎不可尚已夏
商之名皆遵虞制至周始立太師太傅太
保以爲三公論道經邦燮理陰陽又立少
師少傅少保以爲三孤貳公弘化寅亮天
地又立六官以主天地四時之事謂之六
卿冢宰掌邦治司徒掌邦教宗伯掌邦禮
司馬掌邦政司寇掌邦禁司空掌邦土俾
punctuated: 員，代無定名。伏犧氏以龍紀，共工氏以水紀，神農氏以火紀，黃帝氏以雲紀，皆得於有所感而命之也。顓帝爲民師，而命以民事，又置春夏秋冬中五官，以掌木火金水土之五行，所以尊奉社稷五祀也。然世代云邈，職守莫辨。至堯，始命羲和欽天授時，分命羲仲宅嵎夷，羲叔宅南交，和仲宅昧谷，和叔宅朔方，允釐百工，庶績咸熙。虞舜分爲九官，以伯禹作司空，棄作后稷，契作司徒，皐陶作士師，垂作共工，伯益作虞，伯夷作秩宗，夔作典樂，龍作納言。故考其時，於變之休，昭明之化，皡皡乎不可尚已。夏商之名皆遵虞制。至周，始立太師、太傅、太保，以爲三公，論道經邦，燮理陰陽；又立少師、少傅、少保，以爲三孤，貳公弘化，寅亮天地；又立六官，以主天地四時之事，謂之六卿。冢宰掌邦治，司徒掌邦教，宗伯掌邦禮，司馬掌邦政，司寇掌邦禁，司空掌邦土，俾
translation_en: …officials, and their titles were not fixed from one age to the next. Fuxi designated his officials by dragons, Gonggong by water, Shennong by fire, and the Yellow Emperor by clouds. Each adopted these names in response to something that had moved him. Emperor Zhuan acted as the people's teacher and named officials according to the people's affairs. He also established five offices corresponding to spring, summer, autumn, winter, and the center, to oversee the Five Phases—wood, fire, metal, water, and earth—and thereby reverently serve the altars of Soil and Grain and the Five Sacrifices. Yet these ages are so remote that the officials' respective duties can no longer be distinguished. Only with Yao were Xi and He charged to revere Heaven and communicate the seasons to the people. He separately ordered Xi Zhong to reside at Yuyi, Xi Shu at Nanjiao, He Zhong at Meigu, and He Shu in Shuofang. The various officials were duly regulated, and every undertaking flourished. Shun of Yu divided responsibilities among nine officials: he made Bo Yu Minister of Works; Qi, Lord of Millet; Xie, Minister of Education; Gao Yao, Director of Justice; Chui, Director of Works; Bo Yi 伯益, Forester; Bo Yi 伯夷, Director of Sacrifices; Kui, Director of Music; and Long, Court Herald. Thus, when we examine that age, the blessings of harmonious transformation and the effects of enlightened instruction were so vast and luminous that nothing could surpass them. The official titles of Xia and Shang all followed the institutions of Yu. Only under the Zhou were the Grand Preceptor, Grand Mentor, and Grand Guardian established as the Three Dukes, to deliberate on the Way, order the state, and harmonize yin and yang. The Junior Preceptor, Junior Mentor, and Junior Guardian were also established as the Three Solitary Dignitaries, to assist the Three Dukes in extending transforming instruction and reverently aid Heaven and Earth. Six offices were also established to preside over the affairs of Heaven, Earth, and the four seasons; their heads were called the Six Ministers. The Minister of State oversaw the state's administration; the Minister of Education, its instruction; the Minister of Rites, its rituals; the Minister of War, its military affairs; the Minister of Justice, its prohibitions; and the Minister of Works, its lands.
