title: 嘉靖二十八年山西鄉試錄
text:
各率其屬以倡九牧阜成兆民故考其時
永清之治作孚之休熈熈然不可及已是
三五之所以建官設職以立萬世之極以
成淳古之治者於斯爲盛矣而馬氏又謂
陶唐氏以前之官所治者天事也虞夏以
後之官所治者民事也執事復以治天者
遺民治民者遺天爲疑愚竊以爲不然嘗
考堯典以一羲和之官不徒總之於朝廷
而又分之於四方其象以正曆曆以定時
===
雖所以爲天亦所以爲民也烏可獨謂之
治天也乎成周之制冢宰以下雖皆盡掌
乎民事而馮相保章之屬吏世其官專
其業亦專主在天之事而以爲專治民事
可乎嗚呼此唐虞三代之制官簡而能治
所以繼天立極垂於後而無弊者也由周
以降秦不師古盡變其制維時世變風漓
民僞事增故官益其員代無定額漢則以
丞相大司馬御史大夫爲三公矣又有奉
punctuated: 各率其屬，以倡九牧，阜成兆民。故考其時，永清之治，作孚之休，熈熈然不可及已。是三五之所以建官設職，以立萬世之極，以成淳古之治者，於斯爲盛矣。而馬氏又謂：「陶唐氏以前之官，所治者天事也；虞夏以後之官，所治者民事也。」執事復以治天者遺民、治民者遺天爲疑，愚竊以爲不然。嘗考《堯典》，以一羲和之官，不徒總之於朝廷，而又分之於四方。其象以正曆，曆以定時，雖所以爲天，亦所以爲民也，烏可獨謂之治天也乎？成周之制，冢宰以下，雖皆盡掌乎民事，而馮相、保章之屬，吏世其官，專其業，亦專主在天之事，而以爲專治民事，可乎？嗚呼！此唐虞三代之制，官簡而能治，所以繼天立極，垂於後而無弊者也。由周以降，秦不師古，盡變其制。維時世變風漓，民僞事增，故官益其員，代無定額。漢則以丞相、大司馬、御史大夫爲三公矣，又有奉
translation_en:
…each leading his subordinates to guide the nine regional governors and bring prosperity and good order to the myriad people. Thus, examining that age, we find a government of enduring peace and the blessings of inspiring trust: its flourishing harmony could not be surpassed. Here, then, reached their height the institutions through which the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors established offices and assigned duties, set a standard for all ages, and achieved the pure governance of antiquity.

Yet Master Ma also says: “The officials of the time of Taotang and earlier administered celestial affairs; those of Yu and Xia and afterward administered the affairs of the people.” You, sir, further raise the doubt that those who governed celestial affairs neglected the people, while those who governed the people neglected Heaven. In my humble opinion, this was not so. I have examined the Canon of Yao: even the single office of Xi and He was not merely centrally administered at court, but was also distributed among the four quarters. Its observations of celestial phenomena [?] served to rectify the calendar, and the calendar served to determine the seasons. Though this was service to Heaven, it was also service to the people. How could it be called solely the administration of celestial affairs?

Under the institutions of the perfected Zhou, although all officials from the Minister of State downward administered the affairs of the people, subordinate officials such as the Astronomer and Astrologer held their offices hereditarily and specialized in their occupations, taking particular charge of celestial affairs. Could one therefore say that these institutions concerned themselves exclusively with the affairs of the people? Ah! Such were the institutions of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties: their offices were few, yet they achieved good government. Through them, they carried forward Heaven’s work and established the supreme standard, transmitting it to later generations without ill effects.

After the Zhou, the Qin did not take antiquity as its model, but completely altered its institutions. In those times, the world changed and customs deteriorated; the people became deceitful and administrative business multiplied. Consequently, the number of officials increased, with no fixed complement from one dynasty to the next. The Han made the Counselor-in-Chief, the Commander-in-Chief, and the Censor-in-Chief its Three Dukes. There was also the Feng…

title: 嘉靖二十八年山西鄉試錄
text:
常光祿衛尉太僕鴻臚少府司農宗正廷
尉之九卿焉唐以尚書中書侍中爲三省
矣又有太常光祿衛尉宗正太僕大理鴻
臚司農太府之九寺焉宋置中書省樞密
院謂之二府而臺諫則御史臺諫院是也
是漢唐宋之所以建官設職以樹一代之
法以成一代之治者於此爲可知矣而執
事又以爵位之繁簡職守之是非爲問愚
竊以爲均有可議焉觀漢制自大司馬至
===
散騎爲中朝之官丞相至六百石爲外朝
之官此外又有三輔之設爵位太煩黜陟
不明故黿錯以內史得侵宰相之權石顯
以宦官遂恣竊弄之柄張釋之久不得調
公孫弘不數載位至封侯焉若唐內外之
員極七百之衆既有大尉司空司徒又有
尚書省既有尚書省又有九寺名器濫設
爵位紛雜故車載斗量之謠二垂三契之
誚作焉若宋因五代之舊襲苟且之規既
punctuated: 常、光祿、衛尉、太僕、鴻臚、少府、司農、宗正、廷尉之九卿焉。唐以尚書、中書、侍中爲三省矣，又有太常、光祿、衛尉、宗正、太僕、大理、鴻臚、司農、太府之九寺焉。宋置中書省、樞密院，謂之二府，而臺諫則御史臺、諫院是也。是漢、唐、宋之所以建官設職，以樹一代之法，以成一代之治者，於此爲可知矣。而執事又以爵位之繁簡、職守之是非爲問，愚竊以爲均有可議焉。觀漢制，自大司馬至散騎爲中朝之官，丞相至六百石爲外朝之官。此外又有三輔之設，爵位太煩，黜陟不明，故黿錯以內史得侵宰相之權，石顯以宦官遂恣竊弄之柄，張釋之久不得調，公孫弘不數載位至封侯焉。若唐內外之員，極七百之衆，既有大尉、司空、司徒，又有尚書省；既有尚書省，又有九寺，名器濫設，爵位紛雜，故車載斗量之謠、二垂三契之誚作焉。若宋因五代之舊，襲苟且之規，既
translation_en:
…the Chamberlain for Ceremonials, the Chamberlain for Attendants, the Chamberlain for the Palace Garrison, the Chamberlain for the Imperial Stud, the Chamberlain for Dependencies, the Chamberlain for the Palace Revenues, the Chamberlain for the National Treasury, the Chamberlain for the Imperial Clan, and the Commandant of Justice constituted the Nine Chamberlains. The Tang had the Three Departments: State Affairs, the Secretariat, and the Palace Attendant [?]. It also had nine courts: Imperial Sacrifices, Imperial Entertainments, the Imperial Regalia, the Imperial Clan, the Imperial Stud, Judicial Review, State Ceremonial, the National Granaries, and the Imperial Treasury. The Song established the Secretariat and the Bureau of Military Affairs, calling them the Two Administrations; its censorial and remonstrance organs were the Censorate and the Remonstrance Bureau. From these arrangements we can understand how the Han, Tang, and Song established offices and assigned duties, creating the institutions and accomplishing the governance of their respective dynasties.

You further ask whether ranks and positions were too numerous or too few, and whether official responsibilities were properly assigned. In my humble judgment, all these matters admit of criticism. Under the Han system, officials from the Defender-in-Chief down to the Cavalier Attendants belonged to the Inner Court, while those from the Counselor-in-Chief down to officials ranked at six hundred bushels belonged to the Outer Court. Beyond these, there were also the Three Metropolitan Administrations. Ranks and positions were excessively numerous, and demotions and promotions were not judiciously determined. Thus Yuan Cuo [?], as Metropolitan Superintendent, was able to encroach upon the chief minister’s authority; Shi Xian, a eunuch, freely usurped and manipulated power; Zhang Shizhi long went without advancement; while Gongsun Hong rose within a few years to enfeoffment as a marquis.

As for the Tang, its complement of officials within and outside the capital reached as many as seven hundred. It had a Defender-in-Chief [?], a Minister of Works, and a Minister of Education, yet also a Department of State Affairs; it had the Department of State Affairs, yet also the Nine Courts. Official titles and insignia were granted indiscriminately, and ranks and positions proliferated in confusion. Hence arose the satirical song about officials being ‘carried by the cartload and measured by the bushel,’ and the mockery of ‘two Chuis and three Xies.’ As for the Song, it followed the precedents of the Five Dynasties and inherited their makeshift arrangements; it already had …

title: 嘉靖二十八年山西鄉試錄
text:
有六部又有四監旣有四監又有九寺職
任分而不合政雚散而難收而九羊十牧
之譏一壺百挈之議興焉比之三代果無
可議乎嗚呼此漢唐宋之制當變通之時
乖損益之道所以醇疵相半可行於一代
而不可以通於後世也求其因事設官量
能授職參酌今古之宜而足垂萬世之法
者其惟我
聖朝乎其大綱取法乎周官而節目亦兼乎歷
===
代裁定悉成於
聖祖而損益續酌于
累朝如因周之六卿而立六部之長因周之三
百六十屬而立六部之屬掌邦治邦禮者
如故而五教兼掌於宗伯掌邦治邦禁者
如故而百工專領於司空因御史臺而爲
都察院因銀臺司而爲通政司因廷尉而
爲大理寺兵柄分於五府則樞密之遺也
言責寄於六科則諫院之舊也以至太常
punctuated: 有六部，又有四監；旣有四監，又有九寺。職任分而不合，政雚散而難收，而九羊十牧之譏、一壺百挈之議興焉。比之三代，果無可議乎？嗚呼！此漢唐宋之制，當變通之時，乖損益之道，所以醇疵相半，可行於一代，而不可以通於後世也。求其因事設官，量能授職，參酌今古之宜，而足垂萬世之法者，其惟我聖朝乎！其大綱取法乎周官，而節目亦兼乎歷代。裁定悉成於聖祖，而損益續酌于累朝。如因周之六卿而立六部之長，因周之三百六十屬而立六部之屬。掌邦治、邦禮者如故，而五教兼掌於宗伯；掌邦治、邦禁者如故，而百工專領於司空。因御史臺而爲都察院，因銀臺司而爲通政司，因廷尉而爲大理寺。兵柄分於五府，則樞密之遺也；言責寄於六科，則諫院之舊也。以至太常
translation_en:
…there were the Six Ministries, and also four directorates; besides the four directorates, there were also nine courts. Official duties were divided without being coordinated, and governmental authority [?] was dispersed and difficult to gather together. Hence arose the mockery of “nine sheep with ten shepherds” and the criticism of “one pot with a hundred people lifting it.” Compared with the Three Dynasties, were these arrangements really beyond criticism? Alas! When circumstances called for adaptation, these institutions of the Han, Tang, and Song departed from the proper way of making reductions and additions. Thus their merits and defects were equally mixed: they could function within a single dynasty but could not remain applicable to later ages.

If we seek a system that establishes offices according to the tasks at hand, assigns posts according to ability, weighs what is appropriate in both ancient and modern practice, and provides a model sufficient for ten thousand generations, can it be any other than that of our sagely dynasty? Its broad framework follows the Offices of Zhou, while its detailed provisions also draw upon successive dynasties. Its definitive arrangements were all completed by the sagely founder, and reductions and additions have continued to be considered in successive reigns. For example, following Zhou’s six ministers, it established the heads of the Six Ministries; following Zhou’s 360 subordinate offices, it established the subordinate offices of those ministries. Those responsible for the governance and rites of the realm retain their former functions, while the Minister of Rites also oversees the five teachings. Those responsible for the governance [?] and penal prohibitions of the realm retain their former functions, while the Minister of Works has sole charge of the various crafts.

The Censorate (Duchayuan) was established on the basis of the earlier Censorate (Yushitai); the Office of Transmission on the basis of the Silver Terrace Office; and the Court of Judicial Review on the basis of the Chamberlain for Law Enforcement. The division of military authority among the Five Chief Military Commissions preserves a legacy of the Bureau of Military Affairs; the entrusting of remonstrance to the Six Offices of Scrutiny continues the former practice of the Remonstrance Bureau. Extending even to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices…

title: 嘉靖二十八年山西鄉試錄
text:
太僕光祿之類莫不有置而亦各有損益
於其間則又兼總乎漢唐宋之制而爲之
也又如初以
親王領宗人府矣今用勳戚大臣而官不必
備初嘗置三公府矣今爲大臣加贈而府
亦不建革吏部主事之印而事多歸重於
郎中革黃門待詔之員而職惟統於翰院
重宮僚而設詹事等官重臺諫必待試而
不類選其他如改禮儀司爲鴻臚寺回回
監之附於欽天監五軍罷斷事之司六部
增主事之額不可以一二記而亦非有戾
===
於
聖祖之意也因革其大者非苟爲同損益其小
者非苟爲異下順人情上通天道官多而
不擾所以神化宜民監於前而無愆者也
謂非遠追唐虞三代之盛而陋漢唐宋於
下風者哉夫制法以建官者因乎時不因
乎法任人以効職者係乎人不係乎時我
punctuated: 太僕、光祿之類，莫不有置，而亦各有損益於其間，則又兼總乎漢唐宋之制而爲之也。又如初以親王領宗人府矣，今用勳戚大臣，而官不必備；初嘗置三公府矣，今爲大臣加贈，而府亦不建。革吏部主事之印，而事多歸重於郎中；革黃門待詔之員，而職惟統於翰院。重宮僚而設詹事等官，重臺諫必待試而不類選。其他如改禮儀司爲鴻臚寺，回回監之附於欽天監，五軍罷斷事之司，六部增主事之額，不可以一二記，而亦非有戾於聖祖之意也。因革其大者，非苟爲同；損益其小者，非苟爲異。下順人情，上通天道，官多而不擾，所以神化宜民，監於前而無愆者也。謂非遠追唐虞三代之盛，而陋漢唐宋於下風者哉？夫制法以建官者，因乎時，不因乎法；任人以効職者，係乎人，不係乎時。我
translation_en:
…institutions such as the Court of the Imperial Stud and the Court of Imperial Entertainments were all established, with reductions and additions in each case. Thus the institutions of the Han, Tang, and Song were also comprehensively drawn upon in making these arrangements. Furthermore, at first imperial princes headed the Court of the Imperial Clan; now high ministers from among the meritorious nobility and imperial relatives are employed, and its posts need not all be filled. At first an office for the Three Dukes was established; now these titles are conferred on high ministers as additional or posthumous honors, and no such office is maintained. The seals of the secretaries in the Ministry of Personnel were abolished, and responsibility for affairs largely devolved upon the directors. The posts of expectant officials at the palace gates were abolished, and their duties were placed exclusively under the Hanlin Academy. To give due weight to the heir apparent’s household officials, posts such as Household Administrator were established. To give due weight to censorial and remonstrance officials, candidates must undergo testing rather than be selected through ordinary procedures [?]. Other changes include converting the Office of Ceremonies into the Court of State Ceremonial, attaching the Muslim Directorate of Astronomy to the Directorate of Astronomy, abolishing the judicial offices of the Five Chief Military Commissions, and increasing the quota of secretaries in the Six Ministries. These cannot be enumerated in just one or two examples, yet none ran counter to the intentions of the Sagely Founder.

In retaining or reforming the major institutions, conformity was not pursued merely for its own sake; in reducing or adding to the minor ones, difference was not pursued merely for its own sake. Below, these arrangements accorded with human sentiments; above, they harmonized with the Way of Heaven. Though officials were numerous, they caused no harassment. This was how a transformation of wondrous efficacy was achieved and the people suitably governed, taking the past as a mirror and avoiding error. Could one say that this did not reach far back to emulate the flourishing rule of Tang and Yu and the Three Dynasties, leaving the Han, Tang, and Song inferior by comparison? Now, in framing regulations to establish offices, one follows the needs of the times rather than existing regulations; in appointing men to discharge official duties, success depends upon the men rather than the times. Our…

title: 嘉靖二十八年山西鄉試錄
text:
國家所以久安長治以比隆於時雍風動之
休者豈止於建官之法而已哉蓋尤有選
舉考課之法焉夫選舉之途一出於正惟
經明行脩之士得與其列故君子有彙征
之路而空谷無白駒之歌則慎擇以充位
者不患於乏人也考課之法一出於公惟
黜幽陟明之典舉而不爽故惡德罔持祿
之術而官曹勵忠貞之節則居位以圖治
者不敢以不勉也况
===
聖天子勵精圖治于上孜孜焉以作人用賢爲
急則其所以奠丕圖於有永熙鴻號于無
窮者端有在焉愚生固欲鋪張揚厲於萬
一而愧未能也
第三問
王崇雅
同考試官教諭明　批〔淹貫經史折衷古人其學識別矣〕
考試官教諭朱　批〔博而知約殆不欲以文士自居者〕
考試官教諭鄭　批〔學衆志高真所謂以我觀書者〕
punctuated:
國家所以久安長治，以比隆於時雍風動之休者，豈止於建官之法而已哉？蓋尤有選舉考課之法焉。夫選舉之途，一出於正，惟經明行脩之士得與其列，故君子有彙征之路，而空谷無白駒之歌，則慎擇以充位者不患於乏人也。考課之法，一出於公，惟黜幽陟明之典舉而不爽，故惡德罔持祿之術，而官曹勵忠貞之節，則居位以圖治者不敢以不勉也。况聖天子勵精圖治于上，孜孜焉以作人用賢爲急，則其所以奠丕圖於有永，熙鴻號于無窮者，端有在焉。愚生固欲鋪張揚厲於萬一，而愧未能也。
第三問
王崇雅
同考試官教諭明，批〔淹貫經史，折衷古人，其學識別矣。〕
考試官教諭朱，批〔博而知約，殆不欲以文士自居者。〕
考試官教諭鄭，批〔學衆志高，真所謂以我觀書者。〕
translation_en:
…the means by which our state enjoys enduring peace and lasting order, matching the splendor of an age of harmony when virtue moves the people like the wind—can these consist solely in its system for establishing offices? There are, above all, its methods of selecting men and evaluating their performance. The avenues of selection proceed entirely from upright principles: only men who understand the classics and have cultivated their conduct may enter the ranks. Thus gentlemen have a path by which to advance together, and no song of the white colt is heard in the empty valley, lamenting a worthy man’s withdrawal. Those who carefully select men to fill offices therefore need not fear a shortage of suitable people. The methods of performance evaluation proceed entirely from impartiality: the rules for dismissing the unworthy and promoting the worthy are implemented without deviation. Thus men of bad character have no means of retaining their stipends, while officials encourage one another in loyalty and integrity. Those who hold office and seek good government consequently dare not fail to exert themselves. Moreover, our sagely Son of Heaven devotes his energies to good government from above, diligently making the cultivation of talent and employment of worthy men his urgent concern. There is indeed a firm basis for securing his great imperial enterprise forever and making his august name shine without end. I, an ignorant student, would wish to expound and extol even one ten-thousandth of this, but am ashamed that I cannot.
Third Policy Question
Wang Chongya
Associate Examiner Ming, an Instructor, comments: “Thoroughly versed in the classics and histories, he weighs and adjudicates the views of the ancients. His learning and discernment are distinctive.”
Examiner Zhu, an Instructor, comments: “Broadly learned yet able to grasp essentials, he seems unwilling to regard himself merely as a man of letters.”
Examiner Zheng, an Instructor, comments: “His learning is extensive [?] and his aspirations lofty. He is truly what is meant by one who ‘reads books through his own judgment.’”

title: 嘉靖二十八年山西鄉試錄
text:
多識者德之畜乎時敏其功也反躬者文
之實乎作聖其止也夫昭曠之觀病於孤
陋勤勵之力廢於苦難枝葉之鶩流於雜
博模範之遠阻於師資此學易小成而藝
反自畫也格致爲道義之門則採索惟其
富焉積漸爲藏脩之地則終始典其功焉
守約爲逢原之用則記問戒其靡焉濬哲
爲巳心之師則歸宿入於聖焉閔馬父譬
學於殖不學將落愚生以落殖自懼而窺
===
明問作人之心矣夫游神乎經書之林馳
情乎玄妙之中古今豈一族哉日出日中
秉燭時過後學之懲也雖曰老而好學如
秉燭之明勝於冥行遠矣浸潤冰釋理順
精義入神之境也其曰怡然理順乃以我
觀書勝於博我遠矣匡衡取光鄰壁抗疏
有治性之精曹褒鉛筆寢懷定禮爲會通
之助然功名雖薄尚愧劉向之忠聚訟雖
息不過漢代之禮耳挾經採薪之董遇於
punctuated: 多識者，德之畜乎？時敏其功也。反躬者，文之實乎？作聖其止也。夫昭曠之觀，病於孤陋；勤勵之力，廢於苦難；枝葉之鶩，流於雜博；模範之遠，阻於師資。此學易小成，而藝反自畫也。格致爲道義之門，則採索惟其富焉；積漸爲藏脩之地，則終始典其功焉；守約爲逢原之用，則記問戒其靡焉；濬哲爲巳心之師，則歸宿入於聖焉。閔馬父譬學於殖，不學將落。愚生以落殖自懼，而窺明問作人之心矣。夫游神乎經書之林，馳情乎玄妙之中，古今豈一族哉？日出、日中、秉燭，時過後學之懲也。雖曰老而好學，如秉燭之明，勝於冥行遠矣。浸潤、冰釋、理順，精義入神之境也。其曰怡然理順，乃以我觀書，勝於博我遠矣。匡衡取光鄰壁，抗疏有治性之精；曹褒鉛筆寢懷，定禮爲會通之助。然功名雖薄，尚愧劉向之忠；聚訟雖息，不過漢代之禮耳。挾經採薪之董遇，於
translation_en:
Is broad learning the accumulation of virtue? Its achievement lies in timely diligence. Is self-examination the substance of literary cultivation? Its ultimate aim is to become a sage. A clear and comprehensive outlook is impaired by narrow experience; diligent effort is abandoned before hardship; pursuit of peripheral details lapses into miscellaneous erudition; and the remoteness of exemplary models presents an obstacle to finding teachers [?]. Thus learners readily content themselves with small accomplishments and instead set limits upon their own attainments. If investigating things and extending knowledge are the gateway to the Way and righteousness, inquiry must be abundant. If gradual accumulation provides the ground for preserving and cultivating learning, sustained effort must govern its achievement from beginning to end [?]. If holding fast to essentials enables one to encounter the source everywhere, one must beware of dissipating oneself in memorized learning. If penetrating wisdom is the teacher of one’s own mind, one’s final destination will be sagehood. Min Mafu compared learning to planting: without learning, one will wither. Your humble student takes this image of planting and withering as a warning to himself and thereby perceives your discerning question’s intention to nurture men of worth.

Those who have roamed in spirit through the forest of the classics and let their thoughts range amid profound mysteries—have they, from antiquity to the present, been of only one kind? Sunrise, midday, and holding a candle offer an admonition to those who begin learning after the proper time has passed. Yet even if one is old, a love of learning is like the light of a candle, far better than walking in darkness. Gradual permeation, the melting of ice, and the coherent unfolding of principle describe the state of refining one’s understanding of meaning until it penetrates the spiritual. What is called the joyful, coherent unfolding of principle means reading books through one’s own understanding; this is far superior to merely allowing them to broaden one’s learning.

Kuang Heng obtained light through his neighbor’s wall, and the memorials he boldly submitted displayed a subtle understanding of cultivating one’s nature. Cao Bao slept with a writing brush in his bosom, and his establishment of ritual assisted in bringing diverse traditions into a coherent whole. Yet although achievements and reputation might be held of little account [?], there was still cause for shame when measured against Liu Xiang’s loyalty; and although contentious disputes might have ceased, the result amounted to no more than the rites of the Han dynasty. As for Dong Yu, who carried the classics while gathering firewood, in his dealings with …

title: 嘉靖二十八年山西鄉試錄
text:
來學而不肯從篤好春秋之賈逵爲牧守
而月一課然教人先讀百遍勝於杭顏爲
師數學徵於仕優則實化民首務矣盡春
不錯一字張巡在圍城之中專精後爲通
儒王歡無升斗之產先儒曰書多閱而好
忘者只爲理未精耳理精則須記了無去
處也又曰講學切在深潛縝密然後氣味
深長蹊徑不差故巡以精熟而不忘歡以
縝密而旁通然巡之舍生取義歡也何敢
===
望哉好讀不求甚解獨觀大義之儔也邪
招所問不知三人予忘之偶也若杜預癖
左氏而平吳倪寬帶耕鉏而立相則明經
之效君子所推矣戴馮解經不窮賜席至
於五十殷亮講論獨勝重席至於八九其
博洽之故豈以朝夕耶彼紫桑紀義熈之
甲子倚相誦墳典與索丘其所不解不知
後世何敢望哉噫昔人致用之具皆本於
博文終身自得之由則稽於日就愚生未
punctuated: 來學而不肯從。篤好春秋之賈逵，爲牧守而月一課。然教人先讀百遍，勝於杭顏爲師；數學徵於仕優，則實化民首務矣。盡春不錯一字，張巡在圍城之中；專精後爲通儒，王歡無升斗之產。先儒曰：「書多閱而好忘者，只爲理未精耳。理精則須記了，無去處也。」又曰：「講學切在深潛縝密，然後氣味深長，蹊徑不差。」故巡以精熟而不忘，歡以縝密而旁通。然巡之舍生取義，歡也何敢望哉？好讀不求甚解，獨觀大義之儔也邪？招所問不知三人，予忘之偶也。若杜預癖左氏而平吳，倪寬帶耕鉏而立相，則明經之效，君子所推矣。戴馮解經不窮，賜席至於五十；殷亮講論獨勝，重席至於八九。其博洽之故，豈以朝夕耶？彼紫桑紀義熈之甲子，倚相誦墳典與索丘，其所不解不知，後世何敢望哉？噫！昔人致用之具，皆本於博文；終身自得之由，則稽於日就。愚生未
translation_en:
…when people came to study, he would not comply. Jia Kui, who was deeply devoted to the Spring and Autumn Annals, served as a prefect and examined his students once a month [?]. Yet teaching people first to read a text a hundred times was better than having Hang Yan as their teacher [?]; repeated study, borne out by the principle of studying when official duties leave leisure, is indeed the foremost task in transforming the people.

Zhang Xun, within a besieged city, did not mistake a single character throughout the spring [?]. Wang Huan, who through concentrated study eventually became a broadly learned scholar, had no property yielding even a sheng or dou of grain. An earlier Confucian said: “Those who read books often but readily forget them do so only because their understanding of principle is not yet exact. Once their understanding is exact, they will necessarily remember: there is nowhere for it to escape.” He also said: “In discussing learning, the essential thing is profound immersion and meticulous attention. Only then will its savor be deep and lasting, and the path taken free from error.” Thus Xun did not forget because of his thorough mastery, while Huan extended his understanding to other subjects through meticulous attention. Yet how could Huan dare aspire to Xun’s sacrifice of his life for righteousness?

Was the man who loved reading but did not seek exhaustive explanations of the same company as those who attended only to the larger meaning? The three who did not know what they were asked were companions to me in my forgetfulness [?]. As for Du Yu, whose passion for the Zuo Commentary accompanied his pacification of Wu, and Ni Kuan, who carried his books while working with the hoe and later became a chief minister, these exemplify the efficacy of understanding the Classics, which the gentleman esteems. Dai Feng’s explanations of the Classics were inexhaustible, and the mats bestowed on him reached fifty [?]; Yin Liang alone prevailed in learned discussion, and his stacked mats reached eight or nine. Could their extensive learning have been acquired in a single morning or evening?

As for Zisang’s recording of the cyclical dates of the Yixi era [?], and Yi Xiang’s recitation of the Three Tombs, Five Canons, Eight Cords, and Nine Mounds: even in what they did not understand or know, how could later generations dare hope to equal them? Alas! The resources that the men of old brought to practical affairs were all rooted in broad learning; the means by which they attained understanding for themselves throughout their lives lay in daily progress. I, an ignorant student, have not yet…

title: 嘉靖二十八年山西鄉試錄
text:
爲下惟之董子深愧不學之萊公況敢比
明問所及者乎然飛蟲弋獲竊有獻焉程
子曰今之學者如登山麓方其迤邐莫不
闊步及到峻處便逡巡謝上蔡曰顏子工
夫真百世軌範舍此應無入路無住宅夫
逡巡於峻極則其闊步爲徒勞軌範而不
學聖賢則其所就皆苟爾夫自結繩之後
書契繁矣雖習服講貫終年無怠日夜之
推移有限心力之運用必窮況溺技辭章
===
非上士之操也役心編簡非無言之誨也
物理散於萬而統之則一吾心有良師而
求之則餘夫子三絶於韋編而語道於一
貫則六經之秘豈待句讀而後明況百氏
之書又有致遠而恐泥耶謹對
第四問
武道脩
考試官教諭朱　批〔造語不襲斷制無遺眞善士之　可爲者〕
punctuated:
爲下惟之董子，深愧不學之萊公，況敢比明問所及者乎？然飛蟲弋獲，竊有獻焉。程子曰：「今之學者如登山麓，方其迤邐，莫不闊步；及到峻處，便逡巡。」謝上蔡曰：「顏子工夫，真百世軌範，舍此應無入路，無住宅。」夫逡巡於峻極，則其闊步爲徒勞；軌範而不學聖賢，則其所就皆苟爾。夫自結繩之後，書契繁矣。雖習服講貫，終年無怠，日夜之推移有限，心力之運用必窮。況溺技辭章，非上士之操也；役心編簡，非無言之誨也。物理散於萬，而統之則一；吾心有良師，而求之則餘。夫子三絶於韋編，而語道於一貫，則六經之秘，豈待句讀而後明？況百氏之書，又有致遠而恐泥耶？謹對。

第四問
武道脩
考試官教諭朱　批〔造語不襲，斷制無遺，眞善士之　可爲者。〕
translation_en:
…become a Master Dong studying behind a lowered curtain [?], and I feel deeply ashamed before the unlearned Duke of Lai. How, then, could I dare compare myself with those mentioned in your illuminating question? Yet, like someone who happens to bring down a flying creature with an arrow, I venture to offer something I have gained.

Master Cheng said: “Students today are like people ascending the foothills of a mountain. While the path winds gently upward, all stride boldly ahead; once they reach a steep place, they hesitate.” Xie Shangcai said: “Master Yan’s efforts truly provide a model for a hundred generations. Abandon this, and there can be no path of entry and no place to dwell.” If one hesitates at the steepest heights, those bold strides amount to wasted effort. If one takes a model but does not learn from the sages and worthies, whatever one achieves will be merely makeshift.

Since the age of knotted cords, written records have proliferated. Even if one studies, practices, discusses, and thoroughly masters them without flagging throughout the year, the days and nights available are limited, and the application of mental powers must eventually reach exhaustion. Moreover, immersion in literary technique and composition is not the conduct of a superior scholar; taxing the mind over written texts is not instruction without words. The principles of things are dispersed among the myriad things, yet, brought together, they are one. Within my own mind there is a good teacher; if I seek there, I have more than enough. The Master wore through the leather bindings three times, yet spoke of the Way as running through everything in a single thread. Must the secrets of the Six Classics, then, await the parsing of sentences before they become clear? How much more must one fear that the writings of the hundred schools, when used to reach far, may instead prove an impediment? Respectfully submitted in reply.

Fourth Question
Wu Daoxiu
Examiner Zhu, Instructor, comments: 〔His phrasing borrows from no predecessor, and his judgments leave nothing unaddressed. This is truly what a worthy scholar can accomplish.〕

title: 嘉靖二十八年山西鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭鄭　批〔文似青錢心昭白日〕
善人天下之紀也見而舉之忠莫上焉知
人聖哲之難也精而擇之事莫先焉夫天
下之才不類君子之器無方經綸之具猶
濟豫章其公輔之略黼黻之猷未試逆知
其炳蔚之文欲以曹好而徇聲則無容之
隋珠益遠欲以全美而待物則維籜之樹
檀日增不有公焉以順其應旁招之典廢
於朋從以秦茅爲私分矣不有明焉以燭
===
其微可否之極紛於秦宇以燕石爲奇珍
矣然公以生明幾無不貫誠之動物氣自
相求執事者又何慮哉昔有立子不爲比
舉偏不爲黨祁奚能舉善也若解狐與荆
伯玉爲怨上黨之守獨揚於簡子舅犯與
子羔爲仇西河之守首稱於文公祁奚固
聞舅犯之風解狐誠不負祁奚之舉也狐
又嘗薦雠爲相雠往拜賜引弓而迎射之
羔嘗候謝于犯犯謂曰子其夫矣顧吾射
punctuated:
考試官教諭鄭，批〔文似青錢，心昭白日。〕
善人，天下之紀也；見而舉之，忠莫上焉。知人，聖哲之難也；精而擇之，事莫先焉。夫天下之才不類，君子之器無方。經綸之具猶濟豫章，其公輔之略、黼黻之猷，未試逆知其炳蔚之文。欲以曹好而徇聲，則無容之隋珠益遠；欲以全美而待物，則維籜之樹檀日增。不有公焉以順其應，旁招之典廢於朋從，以秦茅爲私分矣；不有明焉以燭其微，可否之極紛於秦宇，以燕石爲奇珍矣。然公以生明，幾無不貫；誠之動物，氣自相求。執事者又何慮哉？昔有立子不爲比，舉偏不爲黨，祁奚能舉善也。若解狐與荆伯玉爲怨，上黨之守獨揚於簡子；舅犯與子羔爲仇，西河之守首稱於文公。祁奚固聞舅犯之風，解狐誠不負祁奚之舉也。狐又嘗薦雠爲相，雠往拜賜，引弓而迎射之。羔嘗候謝于犯，犯謂曰：「子其夫矣，顧吾射
translation_en:
Examiner Zheng, Instructor, comments: 〔The writing is like fine bronze coinage; the heart shines as brightly as the sun.〕
Worthy men are the guiding framework of the realm. To recognize and recommend them is the highest loyalty. Judging men is difficult even for sages and wise men; nothing takes precedence over scrutinizing and selecting them. The talents of the realm are diverse, and the capacities of the gentleman have no fixed form. Those equipped to order affairs resemble fine timber [?]. Their strategies for serving as the highest ministers and their plans for embellishing government reveal their splendid qualities even before they have been tried [?]. If one follows the preferences of one’s associates and defers to reputation, pearls like that of the Marquis of Sui, finding no acceptance, become ever more remote [?]. If one insists upon complete perfection in judging others, the sandalwood trees rejected for their sheaths daily increase [?]. Without impartiality to respond appropriately, the established practice of seeking talent far and wide is ruined by factional allegiances, and “Qin thatch” is treated as a private allotment [?]. Without discernment to illuminate subtleties, the standards of approval and rejection become confused amid “Qin’s domain” [?], and ordinary stones from Yan are regarded as rare treasures. Yet impartiality gives rise to discernment, penetrating every subtle indication. When sincerity moves others, kindred vital energies naturally seek one another. What, then, need you gentlemen charged with this responsibility fear?
In former times, a man could appoint his son without being considered partial, and recommend his subordinate without being considered factional: Qi Xi was able to recommend worthy men. Jie Hu, for example, was at enmity with Jing Boyu, yet singled him out to Jianzi for the post of Governor of Shangdang. Jiu Fan was hostile to Zigao, yet recommended him first to Duke Wen for the post of Governor of Xihe. Qi Xi had indeed heard of Jiu Fan’s example, and Jie Hu truly did not disappoint Qi Xi’s recommendation of him. Hu also once recommended an enemy to serve as minister. When the enemy went to express thanks for this favor, Hu drew his bow and shot at him as he approached. Zigao once visited Fan to thank him. Fan said: “You should leave [?], lest I shoot …

title: 嘉靖二十八年山西鄉試錄
text:
子矣是又過故人知君者之言固怨將誰
歸者之度也然則舅犯祁奚解狐不謂之
公與明乎執事又謂私易滴而公可學鑑
易昏而明難同愚謂公與明非二道也譬
諸水鑑焉無先主待物之私者公也能盡
萬物之情者明也夫陽剛陰柔天下有一
定之彙薰蕕異器人情無兩可之從傾蓋
故知非緣介紹懸衡内朗遂定終身故林
宗見子師有一日千里之許鍾會見裴王
===
有清通簡要之賢卒而子師樹績於司徒
二童馳聲於吏部焉許劭多長者之遊而
不詣陳寔叔度締累日之雅而不宿奉高
蓋以大丘之道廣難周奉高之器狹易挹
焉僑札神孚以立談而披素管鮑深信與
生我而同恩惟賢知賢兹其試乎或因小
揣巨歟任安分麋鹿於邑中耿嵩主廩給
於荒歲人皆稱平焉宰肉必均之器也或
定交因親歟禰衡北遊許都則懷刺漫滅
punctuated: 子矣！」是又過「故人知君」者之言、「固怨將誰歸」者之度也。然則舅犯、祁奚、解狐，不謂之公與明乎？執事又謂私易滴而公可學，鑑易昏而明難同。愚謂公與明非二道也。譬諸水鑑焉，無先主待物之私者，公也；能盡萬物之情者，明也。夫陽剛陰柔，天下有一定之彙；薰蕕異器，人情無兩可之從。傾蓋故知，非緣介紹；懸衡内朗，遂定終身。故林宗見子師，有一日千里之許；鍾會見裴、王，有清通簡要之賢。卒而子師樹績於司徒，二童馳聲於吏部焉。許劭多長者之遊，而不詣陳寔；叔度締累日之雅，而不宿奉高。蓋以大丘之道廣難周，奉高之器狹易挹焉。僑、札神孚，以立談而披素；管、鮑深信，與生我而同恩。惟賢知賢，兹其試乎？或因小揣巨歟？任安分麋鹿於邑中，耿嵩主廩給於荒歲，人皆稱平焉，宰肉必均之器也。或定交因親歟？禰衡北遊許都，則懷刺漫滅
translation_en:
…you!” This goes beyond both the saying “An old friend understands you” and the magnanimity expressed in “If I persist in resentment, to whom shall I turn?” Can Jiu Fan, Qi Xi, and Jie Hu, then, not be called impartial and discerning?

You further say that selfishness is easily overcome [?], so impartiality can be learned, whereas the mirror is easily clouded, so discernment is difficult to equal. In my humble view, impartiality and discernment are not two separate ways. Consider water as a mirror: to receive things without the selfishness of a preconceived judgment is impartiality; to apprehend fully the true circumstances of all things is discernment. Yang is firm and yin yielding: the world has its fixed categories. Fragrant and foul-smelling plants belong in separate vessels: in human dispositions, one cannot follow both indiscriminately. People may meet briefly, their carriage canopies touching, and become as old friends, without depending on an introduction. With the balance suspended and the mind inwardly clear, one can reach a judgment that holds for a lifetime.

Thus, when Linzong met Zishi, he acclaimed him as capable of covering a thousand li in a day; when Zhong Hui met Pei and Wang, he praised their clarity and penetration, simplicity and grasp of essentials. Eventually Zishi established a record of achievement as Minister of Education, and the two youths won renown in the Ministry of Personnel. Xu Shao associated with many respected elders, yet did not visit Chen Shi. Shudu cultivated friendships through visits lasting several days, yet did not stay overnight with Fenggao. This was because the Way of the Elder of Daqiu was so broad that it was difficult to comprehend fully, whereas Fenggao’s capacity was narrow and easily drawn dry. Qiao and Zha trusted one another in spirit, laying bare their hearts in a conversation held standing; Guan and Bao trusted one another deeply, with a debt of gratitude equal to that owed to those who gave one life. Only the worthy recognize the worthy: are these not proofs of it?

Or does one infer great capacities from small matters? Ren An distributed deer in his locality, and Geng Song managed grain allowances in a famine year; everyone praised their fairness. They possessed the capacity exemplified by one who invariably divides the meat equally when acting as carver. Or does one establish friendship through personal affinity? When Mi Heng traveled north to the capital at Xu, the visiting card he carried became worn and illegible…

title: 嘉靖二十八年山西鄉試錄
text:
而無所遇反南見趙戩則干將莫耶乃形
於嘆月旦評人之風也阮瑀謂通士以四
奇高人必有四難之忌質士以四短違人
必有四安之報言多而中難處不若少辭
之宜政也術饒而要難求不若寡知之鎮
物也意弘而情難足不若一道之專思也
性察而下難事不若混濛之能容也茲可
鑒夫自賢而明其退讓矣然通士非大受
之才質士亦木訥之近青白眞贗固必有
===
折衷乎夫子觀由察安無遺照矣慨於澹
臺而不失澹臺孔明開誠布公成大忠矣
誤於馬謖而卒誅馬謖官人若將效法之
不暇而又何懲哉張輔優劣名士固識三
國之雄矣至謂若令玄德據有中州將與
周室比隆其有所激而發乎孔融昌論汝
潁固謂汝南之勝矣至謂許掾敎鄧晨圖
開稻陂數萬頃夜有火光其亦求可之議
乎愚生堂下顓蒙久佩方人之訓泮宮雌
punctuated: 而無所遇，反南見趙戩，則干將莫耶乃形於嘆，月旦評人之風也。阮瑀謂通士以四奇高人，必有四難之忌；質士以四短違人，必有四安之報。言多而中難處，不若少辭之宜政也；術饒而要難求，不若寡知之鎮物也；意弘而情難足，不若一道之專思也；性察而下難事，不若混濛之能容也。茲可鑒夫自賢，而明其退讓矣。然通士非大受之才，質士亦木訥之近，青白眞贗，固必有折衷乎！夫子觀由察安，無遺照矣；慨於澹臺，而不失澹臺。孔明開誠布公，成大忠矣；誤於馬謖，而卒誅馬謖。官人若將效法之不暇，而又何懲哉？張輔優劣名士，固識三國之雄矣；至謂若令玄德據有中州，將與周室比隆，其有所激而發乎？孔融昌論汝潁，固謂汝南之勝矣；至謂許掾敎鄧晨圖開稻陂數萬頃，夜有火光，其亦求可之議乎？愚生堂下顓蒙，久佩方人之訓，泮宮雌
translation_en:
…yet found no one to receive him. Returning south and meeting Zhao Jian, however, he expressed his admiration by invoking the swords Ganjiang and Moye: this exemplified the spirit of the monthly appraisals of men.

Ruan Yu said that accomplished scholars surpass others through four exceptional qualities, yet inevitably incur resentment for four corresponding difficulties; plain scholars fall short of others through four deficiencies, yet inevitably receive recompense for four corresponding sources of ease. Those who speak much are difficult to keep within due bounds; they are less suited to government than those sparing of words. Those rich in techniques make their essential principles hard to discern; they are less capable of keeping affairs settled than those with little cleverness. Those expansive in aspiration have desires difficult to satisfy; they are less focused in thought than those devoted to a single way. Those discerning by nature are difficult for subordinates to serve; they are less tolerant than those of an undifferentiated simplicity. This can serve as a mirror for those who esteem their own worth, making clear the value of modest withdrawal and deference. Yet accomplished scholars are not necessarily talents fit for great responsibilities, while plain scholars merely approach the quality of being unpolished and sparing of speech. Surely there must be a balanced judgment distinguishing the pure from the impure and the genuine from the false!

The Master observed the paths people followed and examined where they found contentment, leaving nothing unilluminated. He regretted his judgment of Tantai, yet did not ultimately fail to recognize Tantai. Kongming laid bare his sincerity and acted impartially, achieving great loyalty. He erred in judging Ma Su, yet ultimately executed Ma Su. Those appointing men to office should scarcely have time enough to emulate them; what, then, is there to deter them?

In ranking eminent men, Zhang Fu certainly recognized the outstanding figures of the Three Kingdoms. But when he said that, had Xuande occupied the Central Region, his achievements would have rivaled those of the Zhou royal house, was he speaking under the impulse of some particular provocation? In his outspoken discussion of Ru and Ying, Kong Rong certainly maintained the superiority of Runan. But when he went so far as to say that Clerk Xu advised Deng Chen to plan the opening of rice irrigation reservoirs covering tens of thousands of qing, and that flames appeared there at night, was this too an argument seeking acceptance [?]?

I, an ignorant student below the hall, dull and unenlightened, have long cherished the admonition concerning the appraisal of others. Within the prefectural school, submissively…

title: 嘉靖二十八年山西鄉試錄
text:
伏未當薦士之雈方懼穢形於鑑室又何
獻助於階前然尚友之衷僭有所擬焉解
狐子犯古之遺直也僑札管鮑古之朋來
也其公與明盡矣林宗以櫜甑得敏許劭
以英雄名曹其鑒別固歷試也然林宗知
幾宏度豈劭所班耶阮瑀以藻梲垂聲孔
融以英傑震世其文藝固相侔也然曹瞞
獨憚孔融豈瑀可配耶若鍾會能識裴王
而不相容於鄧艾禰衡能知陳長文而不
===
能免於黃祖君子固當取法於上也夫子
曰舉爾所知爾所不知人其舍諸又曰聽
其言而觀其行執事者毋亦是務乎
吳國詔
第五問
同考試官教諭黃　批〔善言其鄉有見於道〕
同考試官教授錢　批〔學知所宗言盡其大〕
考試官教諭朱　批〔不苟爲同品藻尤當〕
考試官教諭鄭　批〔詳盡〕
punctuated:
伏，未當薦士之雈，方懼穢形於鑑室，又何獻助於階前？然尚友之衷，僭有所擬焉。解狐、子犯，古之遺直也；僑、札、管、鮑，古之朋來也。其公與明盡矣。林宗以櫜甑得敏，許劭以英雄名曹，其鑒別固歷試也。然林宗知幾宏度，豈劭所班耶？阮瑀以藻梲垂聲，孔融以英傑震世，其文藝固相侔也。然曹瞞獨憚孔融，豈瑀可配耶？若鍾會能識裴、王，而不相容於鄧艾；禰衡能知陳長文，而不能免於黃祖，君子固當取法於上也。夫子曰：「舉爾所知，爾所不知，人其舍諸？」又曰：「聽其言而觀其行。」執事者毋亦是務乎？
吳國詔
第五問
同考試官教諭黃　批〔善言其鄉，有見於道。〕
同考試官教授錢　批〔學知所宗，言盡其大。〕
考試官教諭朱　批〔不苟爲同，品藻尤當。〕
考試官教諭鄭　批〔詳盡。〕
translation_en:
…lying low, I have not yet assumed the responsibility of recommending worthy men [?]. Fearing even now that my unworthy appearance will sully the chamber of mirrors, what assistance could I offer before your steps? Yet, in my desire to befriend the worthies of antiquity, I venture to make some comparisons. Jie Hu and Zifan preserved the uprightness of antiquity; Qiao, Zha, Guan, and Bao exemplified its friendships. Their impartiality and discernment were complete. Linzong recognized Min through an incident involving a cooking vessel [?], while Xu Shao declared Cao a hero: their discernment was certainly tested in practice. Yet could Shao rank alongside Linzong in perceiving incipient developments and possessing breadth of mind? Ruan Yu won lasting renown through literary embellishment [?], while Kong Rong stirred the world with his outstanding talent: their literary accomplishments were indeed comparable. Yet Cao Man feared Kong Rong alone; could Yu be his equal? As for Zhong Hui, he could recognize the merits of Pei and Wang, yet could not coexist with Deng Ai; Mi Heng could appreciate Chen Changwen, yet could not escape death at Huang Zu’s hands. A gentleman should certainly take the highest examples as his models. The Master said: “Promote those you know. As for those you do not know, will others pass them over?” He also said: “Listen to their words and observe their conduct.” Should not you who hold responsibility devote yourselves to this?
Wu Guozhao
Fifth Question
Associate Examiner Huang, Instructor, comments: “He speaks well of his native region and has insight into the Way.”
Associate Examiner Qian, Professor, comments: “In learning, he knows which authorities to follow; his words fully express the essentials.”
Examiner Zhu, Instructor, comments: “He does not casually follow others’ opinions; his evaluations are especially apt.”
Examiner Zheng, Instructor, comments: “Detailed and thorough.”

title: 嘉靖二十八年山西鄉試錄
text:
有一代之名儒有不世之眞儒文衰道弊
毅然自任著書立言直追前古而功業之
純駁不與焉謂非一代之名儒不可也盡
心知性篤志力行窮達一心險夷一節而
著述之多寡不與焉謂非不世之眞儒不
可也知此則王通氏之於隋世薛瑄氏之
在
國朝有可斷按者矣請因明問而僭以春秋
之義上下之可乎甞謂唐堯世遠孔鐸不
===
聞政教衰而儒濫法治弊而道塞秦漢而
下隋亦極矣乃若龍門萃秀王通氏出焉
講明倡道欲紹孔氏之傳博覽採輯有志
六經之道四方嚮慕一時稱盛亦可謂間
世而出者矣是故考其中説之傳則語楊
素蘇夔李德林以所不及而有禮樂之遺
焉語叔恬以不費而及巡狩之典焉遊
孔廟而嘆夫子之神道並行居家不捨周禮
而曰
punctuated: 有一代之名儒，有不世之眞儒。文衰道弊，毅然自任，著書立言，直追前古，而功業之純駁不與焉，謂非一代之名儒不可也。盡心知性，篤志力行，窮達一心，險夷一節，而著述之多寡不與焉，謂非不世之眞儒不可也。知此，則王通氏之於隋世、薛瑄氏之在國朝，有可斷按者矣。請因明問，而僭以《春秋》之義上下之，可乎？甞謂唐堯世遠，孔鐸不聞，政教衰而儒濫，法治弊而道塞。秦漢而下，隋亦極矣。乃若龍門萃秀，王通氏出焉，講明倡道，欲紹孔氏之傳；博覽採輯，有志六經之道。四方嚮慕，一時稱盛，亦可謂間世而出者矣。是故考其《中説》之傳，則語楊素、蘇夔、李德林以所不及，而有禮樂之遺焉；語叔恬以不費，而及巡狩之典焉；遊孔廟，而嘆夫子之神道並行；居家不捨《周禮》，而曰：
translation_en:
There are renowned Confucian scholars who distinguish an age, and there are true Confucian scholars rarely seen in the world. When letters decline and the Way falls into decay, a man resolutely takes responsibility upon himself, writes books and establishes teachings, aspiring directly to the achievements of high antiquity. Whether his accomplishments are pure or mixed does not enter into this judgment: one cannot deny that he is a renowned Confucian scholar of his age. Another fully realizes his heart and understands his nature, makes his resolve firm and acts diligently, maintaining the same heart in adversity and success, and the same integrity in danger and ease. How much or little he writes does not enter into this judgment: one cannot deny that he is a true Confucian scholar rarely seen in the world. Once this distinction is understood, there is a basis for assessing Wang Tong of the Sui and Xue Xuan of our own dynasty. May I, in response to your discerning question, venture to rank them according to the principles of the Spring and Autumn Annals?

I have long held that the age of Yao of Tang is distant, and Confucius’s bell of instruction is no longer heard. Government and moral instruction declined, while the ranks of Confucian scholars became indiscriminate; laws and governance deteriorated, and the Way was obstructed. From the Qin and Han onward, these failings reached an extreme under the Sui. Yet the finest influences of Longmen gathered, and Wang Tong emerged there. He expounded and promoted the Way, seeking to continue the transmission of Confucius; he read widely and gathered texts, aspiring to the Way of the Six Classics. Men throughout the land admired him, and his movement flourished in its day. He too may be called a man who appears only once in several generations.

Thus, examining the transmitted text of his Balanced Discourses (Zhongshuo), we find that he spoke to Yang Su, Su Kui, and Li Delin about what they had failed to attain, preserving something of the legacy of rites and music. He spoke to Shutian about avoiding expenditure, touching upon the institutions of royal inspection tours. Visiting the temple of Confucius, he marveled that the Master’s numinous Way moved in concert [with Heaven and Earth]. At home he never put aside the Rites of Zhou, and said: …

title: 嘉靖二十八年山西鄉試錄
text:
先師以王道極他如語賈瓊以王伯之畧語
叔達以鬼神之道語董常實儼以周公孔
子之事業而其他有難以遍及者矣續經
之作則易讚出而卦畫立焉七制行而典
謨繼焉雜曹劉沈謝之韻以爲風雅桑叔
孫通曹褒荀勗之製以作禮樂裁宋魏南
北君臣之統續以擬春秋而其中有難以
槩論者矣方其一見隋文也鋭意於明德
新民之學而欲置身於伊周湯武之間及
===
其不遇也究心於言語文字之末而欲脫
迹於孔孟傳授之業雖其智不度德才不
量力而其志其功獨無一得之可進者乎
繼之於孟子之賢固非其倫而比之於董
韓之列葢相上下而尤廓大者也故程子
嘗稱曰文中子隱君子也其議論極有格
言又曰樂天知命吾何憂窮理盡性吾何
疑此言極好朱子亦稱之曰文中子儘有
可觀文取陸機史取陳壽又曰仲淹粗識
punctuated: 「先師以王道極。」他如語賈瓊以王伯之畧，語叔達以鬼神之道，語董常、實儼以周公、孔子之事業，而其他有難以遍及者矣。續經之作，則《易讚》出而卦畫立焉，《七制》行而典謨繼焉。雜曹、劉、沈、謝之韻以爲風雅，桑叔孫通、曹褒、荀勗之製以作禮樂，裁宋、魏、南北君臣之統續以擬《春秋》，而其中有難以槩論者矣。方其一見隋文也，鋭意於明德新民之學，而欲置身於伊、周、湯、武之間。及其不遇也，究心於言語文字之末，而欲脫迹於孔、孟傳授之業。雖其智不度德，才不量力，而其志其功，獨無一得之可進者乎？繼之於孟子之賢，固非其倫；而比之於董、韓之列，葢相上下，而尤廓大者也。故程子嘗稱曰：「文中子，隱君子也。其議論極有格言。」又曰：「樂天知命，吾何憂？窮理盡性，吾何疑？此言極好。」朱子亦稱之曰：「文中子儘有可觀，文取陸機，史取陳壽。」又曰：「仲淹粗識
translation_en:
…“The former master took the Way of Kings as the ultimate standard.” Other examples include his speaking to Jia Qiong about the strategies of kings and hegemons, to Shuda about the way of ghosts and spirits, and to Dong Chang and Shi Yan [?] about the undertakings of the Duke of Zhou and Confucius. There are still other examples too numerous to cover fully. As for his continuations of the classics, his Praises of the Changes appeared and established the hexagram figures; his Seven Institutions circulated and carried forward the Documents’ canons and counsels. He combined the verse of Cao, Liu, Shen, and Xie to constitute his Airs and Odes; drew upon [?] the institutions of Shusun Tong, Cao Bao, and Xun Xu to compose works on rites and music; and selected and arranged the succession of rulers and ministers of Song, Wei, and the northern and southern dynasties to emulate the Spring and Autumn Annals. These works contain matters difficult to discuss comprehensively.

When he first obtained an audience with Emperor Wen of Sui, he devoted himself eagerly to the learning of illuminating luminous virtue and renewing the people, wishing to place himself among Yi Yin, the Duke of Zhou, Tang, and King Wu. When he failed to find recognition, he applied himself to the lesser matters of speech and writing, wishing to distinguish himself in the enterprise transmitted by Confucius and Mencius. Although in exercising his wisdom he did not assess his virtue, and in exercising his talent he did not gauge his strength, could his aspirations and achievements really contain not a single insight worthy of recognition? To rank him as a worthy successor to Mencius would certainly place him outside his proper company; but compared with the ranks of Dong Zhongshu and Han Yu, he was probably their equal, and even broader in scope.

Thus Master Cheng once praised him, saying: “Master Wenzhong was a gentleman living in retirement. His discussions contain truly exemplary sayings.” He also said: “‘Rejoicing in Heaven and knowing my allotted fate, what have I to worry about? Fathoming principle and fully realizing my nature, what have I to doubt?’ These words are excellent.” Master Zhu likewise praised him, saying: “There is much worth considering in Master Wenzhong. In literary writing he took Lu Ji as his model; in history, Chen Shou.” He also said: “Zhongyan had a rough understanding of …

title: 嘉靖二十八年山西鄉試錄
text:
聖賢之用而於道之未嘗忘者蓋有意焉
又曰仲淹之學頗近於正則王通氏之爲
人可識矣或者乃以六經續孔子之僭中
說彷論語之謬疑之是春秋責備賢者之
意也蓋言則取法於先王事必直任乎孔
子通亦不可謂無志者也謂之無見於道
可乎由百世之后等百世之前愚故以一
代之名儒歸之陽臨五位帝德昌明道化
一而民俗同性真統而風敎偃遠我
===
國朝蔑以尚矣乃河汾衍靈薛瑄氏生焉紫
衣謁見詩賦著監司之奇潛心誦讀道學
傳程朱之正表裏無間終始一節亦可謂
抱德名世者矣是故考讀書錄所載則首
論道體而太極無極之妙著焉次論經說
而六經四書之理盡焉言學則體認切而
知行實力也論心則嗜欲少而心淸理明
也性則辨氣質人物之所以分敬則發寧
靜專一之所以力爲仁則有李核之喻出
punctuated:
聖賢之用，而於道之未嘗忘者，蓋有意焉。」又曰：「仲淹之學頗近於正。」則王通氏之爲人可識矣。或者乃以六經續孔子之僭、中說彷論語之謬疑之，是春秋責備賢者之意也。蓋言則取法於先王，事必直任乎孔子，通亦不可謂無志者也。謂之無見於道，可乎？由百世之后，等百世之前，愚故以一代之名儒歸之。
陽臨五位，帝德昌明，道化一而民俗同，性真統而風敎偃遠，我國朝蔑以尚矣。乃河汾衍靈，薛瑄氏生焉。紫衣謁見，詩賦著監司之奇；潛心誦讀，道學傳程朱之正。表裏無間，終始一節，亦可謂抱德名世者矣。是故考《讀書錄》所載，則首論道體，而太極無極之妙著焉；次論經說，而六經四書之理盡焉。言學，則體認切而知行實力也；論心，則嗜欲少而心淸理明也；性，則辨氣質人物之所以分；敬，則發寧靜專一之所以力；爲仁，則有李核之喻；出
translation_en:
…the practical application of the teachings of the sages and worthies; in never forgetting the Way, he surely had a purpose.” He also said: “Zhongyan’s learning comes quite close to what is correct.” From this, Wang Tong’s character can be understood. Some, however, question him for the presumption of continuing Confucius’s Six Classics and the error of modeling his Central Discourses (Zhongshuo) on the Analects. This reflects the intent of the Spring and Autumn Annals in demanding perfection of the worthy. In his words he took the former kings as his models, and in his undertakings he assumed directly the responsibility of Confucius. Tong, too, cannot be said to have lacked aspiration. Can one say that he had no insight into the Way? Looking back from a hundred generations later and assessing those a hundred generations earlier, I therefore rank him among the eminent Confucian scholars of his age.
Yang occupies the fifth position [?], and imperial virtue shines brightly. Transformation through the Way is unified, and the people’s customs are alike; the true nature is brought under a single guiding principle [?], and moral instruction extends its sway afar. Nothing can surpass our dynasty in this. Then the spiritual potency of the He and Fen rivers brought forth Xue Xuan. Appearing for an audience in purple robes [?], he won the admiration of the surveillance officials through his poetry and rhapsodies. Devoting himself to recitation and reading, he transmitted the orthodox Learning of the Way of the Cheng brothers and Zhu Xi. His outward conduct and inner character were wholly consistent, and his integrity remained constant from beginning to end. He may indeed be called a man who cherished virtue and became renowned in his age.
Thus, examining what is recorded in his Record of Reading (Dushu lu), we find that it first discusses the substance of the Way, revealing the subtleties of the Supreme Ultimate and the Ultimateless. Next it discusses interpretations of the classics, fully setting forth the principles of the Six Classics and Four Books. In speaking of learning, it stresses close personal apprehension and earnest effort in both knowing and acting. In discussing the mind, it shows that when appetites and desires are few, the mind is clear and principle shines forth. On human nature, it distinguishes how material endowment differentiates people and other beings. On reverent attentiveness, it explains how to exert oneself in tranquility and single-minded concentration. For practicing humaneness, it offers the analogy of a plum stone. As for taking office…

title: 嘉靖二十八年山西鄉試錄
text:
處則唯義命之歸啓端所以作教也脩身
所以本治也事理文史之兼該諸子異端
之具悉而所以言道學者則尤諄諄焉夷
考其行則監湖廣銀塲而性理必書思忘
寢食而有得即記提調山東學校而不事
櫝楚正色立朝而不拜私門遇諸道途而
不屑餞於江上而不往其被逮也怡然以
辨冤獲咎爲無愧其放歸也居家以六年
閉門而不出抗章辨蹈海之冤見幾辭內
===
閣之任於學者以復性爲教於窮理以體
驗爲實一言一動不違於禮辭受取予必
揆諸義而其出處大節光明峻偉尤不可
及者也其造詣之深也則純篤簡諒董韓
諸人不足以擬其高其履歷之詳也精金
良玉魏范以下難以與之匹雖所施未竟
其用所任不盡其長而其學其蘊夫豈一
時所可及者乎擬之訓詁之功似若少間
而進之於陸蔡之儔蓋相出入而尤爲誠
punctuated: 處則唯義命之歸。啓端所以作教也，脩身所以本治也。事理文史之兼該，諸子異端之具悉，而所以言道學者則尤諄諄焉。夷考其行，則監湖廣銀塲而性理必書，思忘寢食而有得即記；提調山東學校而不事櫝楚；正色立朝而不拜私門；遇諸道途而不屑，餞於江上而不往。其被逮也，怡然以辨冤獲咎爲無愧；其放歸也，居家以六年，閉門而不出。抗章辨蹈海之冤，見幾辭內閣之任。於學者以復性爲教，於窮理以體驗爲實。一言一動不違於禮，辭受取予必揆諸義，而其出處大節，光明峻偉，尤不可及者也。其造詣之深也，則純篤簡諒，董韓諸人不足以擬其高；其履歷之詳也，精金良玉，魏范以下難以與之匹。雖所施未竟其用，所任不盡其長，而其學其蘊，夫豈一時所可及者乎？擬之訓詁之功，似若少間，而進之於陸蔡之儔，蓋相出入，而尤爲誠
translation_en: …in taking office or withdrawing, he followed only righteousness and Heaven’s decree. Opening the way to understanding was his means of teaching; cultivating himself was his means of establishing the foundation of government. He comprehensively encompassed the principles of affairs, literature, and history, and thoroughly understood the various philosophical masters and heterodox teachings. Yet he was especially earnest and persistent in discussing the Learning of the Way. Examining his conduct, we find that while supervising the silver works in Huguang, he invariably wrote about human nature and principle. His reflections made him forget sleep and food, and whenever he gained an insight he immediately recorded it. As Proctor of the schools in Shandong, he did not employ corporal punishment [?]. He maintained a dignified bearing at court and did not pay visits to private patrons. He disdained encounters on the road [?] and would not attend a farewell gathering by the river. When arrested, he remained composed, feeling no shame at incurring punishment for defending someone unjustly accused. When released to return home, he lived there for six years, keeping his doors closed and not going out. He submitted a forthright memorial contesting the injustice concerning a death by drowning in the sea [?], and, discerning the first signs of trouble, declined an appointment to the Grand Secretariat. He taught students to recover their original nature and made personal experience and verification the substance of investigating principle. Not a word or movement of his departed from ritual propriety; in declining or accepting, taking or giving, he invariably measured his actions against righteousness. His integrity in the great decisions of entering office or withdrawing was luminous, lofty, and magnificent, and especially beyond others’ reach. In the depth of his attainments, he was pure, earnest, unassuming, and trustworthy: men such as Dong and Han could not measure up to his eminence. Examined in detail, his career was like refined gold and fine jade; from Wei and Fan downward, others could hardly match him. Although what he put into practice did not fully realize its usefulness, and his appointments did not exhaust his abilities, how could his learning and accumulated understanding have been equaled by his contemporaries? Compared in the work of textual exegesis, he seems to have fallen somewhat short; but ranked among the company of Lu and Cai, he was broadly their equal, and was especially sincere…

title: 嘉靖二十八年山西鄉試錄
text:
篤者也故山東士人稱爲夫子尚書何文
淵則曰不愧往哲學士江淵則曰躬行實
踐李賢稱爲
本朝理學一人張鼎稱爲學已至乎樂地觀
感而興者尤多張九功稱爲今之眞儒姚
謨稱爲明體適用而其見之
奏章下諸
廷議者又人人推服無容異焉則薛瑄氏之
爲人可識矣或者乃以姑緩以俟將來是
===
非久而后定罷之是正有待於今日之意
也蓋平易簡切不爲奇僻居敬窮理踐履
篤實瑄亦理學之不可少者也謂之無得
於道可乎由力行之實進之於講明之列
愚故以不世之眞儒許之夫一代之名儒
固不可以接孟軻氏矣無亦隋之氣運使
然乎使通幸而生於聖門焉則切磨以聖
人之道德漸染以羣賢之輔翼當與冉有
季路齊驅矣是得以著述者通之幸也而
punctuated:
篤者也。故山東士人稱爲夫子，尚書何文淵則曰：「不愧往哲。」學士江淵則曰：「躬行實踐。」李賢稱爲本朝理學一人，張鼎稱爲學已至乎樂地，觀感而興者尤多。張九功稱爲今之眞儒，姚謨稱爲明體適用。而其見之奏章、下諸廷議者，又人人推服，無容異焉，則薛瑄氏之爲人可識矣。或者乃以姑緩以俟將來，是非久而后定，罷之，是正有待於今日之意也。蓋平易簡切，不爲奇僻，居敬窮理，踐履篤實，瑄亦理學之不可少者也。謂之無得於道，可乎？由力行之實，進之於講明之列，愚故以不世之眞儒許之。
夫一代之名儒，固不可以接孟軻氏矣，無亦隋之氣運使然乎？使通幸而生於聖門焉，則切磨以聖人之道德，漸染以羣賢之輔翼，當與冉有、季路齊驅矣。是得以著述者，通之幸也，而
translation_en:
…earnest indeed. Thus the scholars of Shandong called him “the Master.” He Wenyuan, a Minister, said that he “was worthy of the philosophers of old”; Jiang Yuan, a Hanlin Academician, said that he “personally put his learning into practice.” Li Xian called him the foremost scholar of the Learning of Principle in our dynasty. Zhang Ding said that his learning had already reached the realm of joy; especially numerous were those stirred to aspiration by witnessing his example. Zhang Jiugong called him a true Confucian of the present age, and Yao Mo praised him for illuminating the underlying substance and applying it appropriately. Moreover, in the memorials submitted about him and the deliberations referred to the court, everyone admired and acknowledged him, leaving no room for dissent. From this one can understand the character of Xue Xuan. Some, however, set the matter aside on the grounds that it should be deferred to the future, since right and wrong would be settled only after a long time [?]. This meant precisely that its resolution awaited the present day. Plain and accessible, concise and pertinent, he pursued nothing eccentric; he maintained reverent attentiveness, investigated principle, and was steadfast and sincere in practice. Xuan, too, is indispensable to the Learning of Principle. Can one say that he attained nothing of the Way? On the strength of his actual practice, he should be advanced into the ranks of those who elucidated it. I therefore venture to acclaim him as a true Confucian rarely seen in any age.
Now, this renowned Confucian of his age certainly cannot be regarded as carrying on the succession from Meng Ke; yet might this not have resulted from the historical fortunes of the Sui dynasty? Had Wang Tong been fortunate enough to study at the Sage’s gate, he would have refined himself through the Sage’s Way and virtue and gradually absorbed their influence with the support of the assembled worthies. He would surely have kept pace with Ran You and Jilu. That he was able to distinguish himself through writing was Tong’s good fortune, and…

title: 嘉靖二十八年山西鄉試錄
text:
不得以躬行實踐者通之不幸也不世之
眞儒無忝於集大成之晦菴氏矣無亦
聖朝之培植有然乎使瑄而生於宋代焉則釋
解六經之訓剝切百家之言當不在周程
朱張之下矣是不得以著述者瑄之不幸
也而得以躬行實踐者瑄之幸也此王通
氏之著述所以不得爲大儒而薛瑄氏之
不著述所以不得爲宋儒也歟說者謂註
周禮註大事記爲有功於訓詁集尚書選
===
著四書五經私抄爲發明於聖門而欲以
宋濂王褘楊守陳諸人與薛瑄氏並稱則
薛瑄氏者力守乎斯道者也之數子者闡
明乎斯道者也著述發揚之功未必無一
言之幾於道而所以繼承往哲垂訓將來
亦未必無所補矣以之分席
孔庭昭建
聖化之極明示趨向誕開爲學之路是亦遐不
作人之一助也夫豈不可哉雖然天下是
punctuated:
不得以躬行實踐者，通之不幸也。不世之眞儒，無忝於集大成之晦菴氏矣，無亦聖朝之培植有然乎？使瑄而生於宋代焉，則釋解六經之訓，剝切百家之言，當不在周程朱張之下矣。是不得以著述者，瑄之不幸也；而得以躬行實踐者，瑄之幸也。此王通氏之著述所以不得爲大儒，而薛瑄氏之不著述所以不得爲宋儒也歟？

說者謂註《周禮》、註《大事記》，爲有功於訓詁；集《尚書選》、著《四書五經私抄》，爲發明於聖門，而欲以宋濂、王褘、楊守陳諸人與薛瑄氏並稱。則薛瑄氏者，力守乎斯道者也；之數子者，闡明乎斯道者也。著述發揚之功，未必無一言之幾於道，而所以繼承往哲、垂訓將來，亦未必無所補矣。以之分席孔庭，昭建聖化之極，明示趨向，誕開爲學之路，是亦遐不作人之一助也，夫豈不可哉？雖然，天下是
translation_en:
…that he could not put it into personal practice was Tong’s misfortune. As a true Confucian scholar rarely seen in an age, Xue Xuan was no disgrace to Hui’an (Zhu Xi), who brought the tradition to its fullest synthesis. Might this not also have resulted from the nurturing influence of our sagely dynasty? Had Xuan lived in the Song, his explication of the teachings of the Six Classics and critical analysis of the sayings of the hundred schools would surely have ranked no lower than those of Zhou Dunyi, the Cheng brothers, Zhu Xi, and Zhang Zai. Thus, his lack of opportunity to write was Xuan’s misfortune, while his opportunity to put the teachings into personal practice was his good fortune. Is this why Wang Tong’s writings did not make him a great Confucian scholar, while Xue Xuan’s lack of writings prevented him from being counted as a Song Confucian scholar [?]?

Some argue that commentaries on the Rites of Zhou and the Record of Major Events contributed to textual exegesis, and that compiling Selections from the Book of Documents and writing Private Notes on the Four Books and Five Classics elucidated the teachings of the sages. They therefore wish to rank Song Lian, Wang Hui, Yang Shouchen, and others alongside Xue Xuan. Now Xue Xuan was one who steadfastly upheld this Way; these other men were those who elucidated it. In their achievement of setting forth and disseminating the teachings through writing, there may well have been some words that approached the Way. Their work may also have contributed to carrying on the legacy of earlier philosophers and transmitting instruction to future generations. To grant them places in the court of Confucius would conspicuously establish the highest standard of sagely transformation, clearly indicate the direction to follow, and open wide the path of learning. Would this not also help nurture worthy men? Why should it be unacceptable? Nevertheless, the world’s judgments of right…

title: 嘉靖二十八年山西鄉試錄
text:
非之鑑昭於下則勸懲之道明天下是非
之權昭於上則勸懲之典公是非者一時
之議也勸懲者萬世之典也安可以一時
之議而僭萬世之典乎然欲執二子之是
非進之
孔庭以順天下理學者觀望焉則惟監司之
明權衡之當而已愚也何敢贅言哉
punctuated: 非之鑑昭於下，則勸懲之道明；天下是非之權昭於上，則勸懲之典公。是非者，一時之議也；勸懲者，萬世之典也。安可以一時之議而僭萬世之典乎？然欲執二子之是非，進之孔庭，以順天下理學者觀望焉，則惟監司之明、權衡之當而已。愚也，何敢贅言哉？
translation_en: …when the mirror of right and wrong shines clearly among those below, the way of encouragement and admonition becomes clear; when the authority to judge right and wrong throughout the realm is clearly exercised by those above, the institutions of encouragement and admonition are impartial. Judgments of right and wrong are the opinions of a particular time; the institutions of encouragement and admonition are standards for all ages. How can the opinions of a particular time presume to override standards for all ages? Yet if these two masters’ merits and faults are to be adjudicated and they are to be admitted to the temple of Confucius, thereby answering the expectations of students of the Learning of Principle throughout the realm, this depends solely upon the discernment of the surveillance commissioners and the soundness of their judgment. In my ignorance, how would I dare add further words?

title: 嘉靖二十八年山西鄉試錄
text:
山西鄉試錄後序
歲己酉秋八月山西試事畣
期巡按監察御史陳〔九德〕
命下在
朝巡按監察御史黃〔洪毗〕暨藩
臬長貳之彥內外執事之良
一心以貞百度〔安道〕當告厥
===
成焉撫純古之載籍仰三晉
之文獻欲陟太行涉河汾久
矣茲行其野三務功成與與
翼翼翼曰美哉豐年之瑞也禮
義由興乎入其鄙連雲戰格
士嬉馬騰曰美哉綏靖之略
也人文滋昭乎處其館十兩
punctuated:
山西鄉試錄後序

歲己酉秋八月，山西試事畣期，巡按監察御史陳〔九德〕命下在朝，巡按監察御史黃〔洪毗〕暨藩臬長貳之彥、內外執事之良，一心以貞百度。〔安道〕當告厥成焉。

撫純古之載籍，仰三晉之文獻，欲陟太行、涉河汾久矣。茲行其野，三務功成，與與翼翼翼，曰：「美哉！豐年之瑞也！禮義由興乎！」入其鄙，連雲戰格，士嬉馬騰，曰：「美哉！綏靖之略也！人文滋昭乎！」處其館，十兩
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Shanxi Provincial Examination

In the eighth month of autumn in the jiyou year [1549], the Shanxi examination reached its appointed time [?]. The appointment of Regional Inspector Chen〔Jiude〕was issued at court [?]. Regional Inspector Huang〔Hongpi〕, together with the outstanding chief and deputy officials of the Provincial Administration and Surveillance Commissions and the capable personnel serving inside and outside the examination compound, worked with one purpose to set all procedures aright. I,〔Andao〕, was to report its successful completion.

Poring over the records of remote antiquity and admiring the writings and worthies of the Three Jin regions, I had long wished to climb the Taihang Mountains and cross the Yellow and Fen Rivers. Now, travelling through this countryside, I saw the work of the three agricultural seasons brought to completion, everything flourishing and orderly [?]. I said: “How splendid! These are auspicious signs of a bountiful year! Surely ritual propriety and righteousness will flourish from this!” Entering its borderlands, I saw defensive structures reaching to the clouds [?], soldiers at play, and horses galloping. I said: “How splendid! Such is the strategy for securing peace! Surely cultural refinement will shine ever more brightly!” Lodging in its guesthouse, ten carriages [?] …

title: 嘉靖二十八年山西鄉試錄
text:
五風凜秋序應入簾之役雲
陰盡解義馭正輝曰美哉肴
歲之休也鍾祥有兆乎淑氣
成象靈於物者動之英華外
朗順於中者積之不必閱故
秉稽菅閩已有季札思深之
觀矣備官承乏謬主考試乃
===
謀于同事鄭〔廷俊〕及分經專
較者矣之曰時至而不秉非
迂衡之訓也毋貪良菌而獎
莠毋眩頑鈍而匿文毋偏於
柔剛而遺元氣衆咸曰所不
殫慮以負玆舉者河山表□
監之閱卷既畢則見其□□
punctuated:
五風，凜秋序，應入簾之役。雲陰盡解，義馭正輝，曰：「美哉，肴歲之休也！鍾祥有兆乎！」淑氣成象，靈於物者動之；英華外朗，順於中者積之。不必閱故秉、稽菅閩，已有季札思深之觀矣。
備官承乏，謬主考試，乃謀于同事鄭〔廷俊〕及分經專較者，矣之曰：「時至而不秉，非迂衡之訓也。毋貪良菌而獎莠，毋眩頑鈍而匿文，毋偏於柔剛而遺元氣。」衆咸曰：「所不殫慮以負玆舉者，河山表□監之！」閱卷既畢，則見其□□
translation_en:
…the five winds [?]. Amid the chill of autumn, I answered the call to enter the examination enclosure. The clouds and gloom cleared completely, and the sun’s chariot [?] shone brightly. I said: “How beautiful—the blessings of a bountiful year [?]! Is this a sign of auspicious fortune gathering here?” Harmonious influences took visible form, stirred by the spiritual potency of things; brilliance shone outward, accumulated from inward harmony. Without having to examine ancient records or investigate past precedents [?], I already enjoyed an insight as profound as that of Ji Zha [?].
Filling an office for want of someone more capable, I had undeservedly been placed in charge of the examination. I therefore consulted my colleague Zheng 〔Tingjun〕 and those assigned to evaluate the individual Classics, declaring to them [?]: “When the moment arrives, failing to take hold of it accords neither with the teaching of Yu Heng [?] nor with our duty. Do not, in seeking fine grain [?], reward weeds; do not let dullness cloud your judgment and conceal literary merit. Do not favor either softness or firmness so much that you overlook vital vigor.” All replied: “Should any of us fail to give this undertaking our utmost thought and thereby betray it, let the mountains and rivers bear witness and judge us [?]!” Once the reading of the examination papers was complete, we saw their [two illegible characters]…

title: 嘉靖二十八年山西鄉試錄
text:
義理炳煥章程是穮是蔉嘉
種熟矣有正有奇利器開矣
載陰載陽變化備矣乃援殊
尤遵
制額中式六十五人梓其文二十
餘篇以
獻拘於數而不盡取蓋多焉安道
===
乃信先澤之遠與密邇
畿甸之深也玆地邃古皇以先
天帝以久化王以龍嘘霸以
虎視民心固有弈世流風士
宜翹然在昔也況離
輦轂數十舍漸涵
列聖衣被
punctuated:
義理炳煥章程：是穮是蔉，嘉種熟矣；有正有奇，利器開矣；載陰載陽，變化備矣。乃援殊尤，遵制額，中式六十五人，梓其文二十餘篇以獻。拘於數而不盡取，蓋多焉。
安道乃信先澤之遠與密邇畿甸之深也。玆地邃古，皇以先天，帝以久化，王以龍嘘，霸以虎視。民心固有弈世流風，士宜翹然在昔也。況離輦轂數十舍，漸涵列聖衣被
translation_en:
…the principles of right conduct shone brilliantly in their compositions. With hoeing and heaping earth about the roots, the fine grain had ripened; with both orthodox and unconventional methods, keen instruments had been brought into use; with yin and yang in alternation, the full range of transformations was present. We therefore selected those of exceptional merit and, observing the imperially prescribed quota, passed sixty-five candidates. We had more than twenty of their compositions printed from woodblocks for presentation to the throne. The numerical limit prevented us from selecting all that merited inclusion; indeed, many were left out.
Andao now truly understood the enduring reach of the beneficence inherited from earlier ages, and the profound influence of close proximity to the metropolitan region. In this land’s remote antiquity, august sovereigns anticipated Heaven [?], emperors transformed the people over long ages, kings breathed forth like dragons, and hegemons gazed like tigers. The people’s hearts surely retain the influence transmitted through successive generations; its scholars should fittingly stand out as they did of old. Moreover, only several tens of travel stages separate them from the imperial capital, and they have been steeped in the beneficence bestowed by successive sage emperors…

title: 嘉靖二十八年山西鄉試錄
text:
今倂與四方丕式自倍矣萃秖發
祥固其所哉然傳巖符夢自
靖三篇諸士三試之言憲章
說命他日不負
帝賚能使無專美否耶〔安道〕識喜
因繼之以規云
江西撫州府東鄉縣儒學教
諭朱〔安道〕謹序
punctuated:
今倂與四方丕式，自倍矣。萃秖發祥，固其所哉！然傳巖符夢，自靖三篇，諸士三試之言，憲章《說命》，他日不負帝賚，能使無專美否耶？〔安道〕識喜，因繼之以規云。
江西撫州府東鄉縣儒學教諭朱〔安道〕謹序。
translation_en:
…Now, together with the four quarters, they take this as their great model and redouble their efforts. Surely this is a fitting place for blessings to gather and auspicious signs to emerge [?]. Yet consider the dream fulfilled at Fu Yan [transcribed 傳巖, apparently for 傅巖], and the three chapters expressing his dedication. If the candidates’ writings in the three examination sessions take the Charge to Yue (Yue ming) as their model, can they, in days to come, prove worthy of the Emperor’s gift and ensure that such excellence is no longer Fu Yue’s alone? I, Andao, record my delight and therefore follow it with these words of admonition.
Preface respectfully written by Zhu Andao, Instructor of the Confucian School of Dongxiang County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi.
